children.title: Layered Path Representation
children.top_down_role: Structural organization of decisions, states, transitions, solution paths, and path values.

children.title: Diagram Layers
children.top_down_role: Layer positions, sequencing roles, skipped layers, plus terminal placement.

knowledge_statements.title: Diagram Layers
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Layer partition of an ordered, acyclic decision diagram.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A layered decision diagram of depth \(n\) has a node set partitioned as \(V=V_0\mathbin{\dot\cup}\cdots\mathbin{\dot\cup}V_n\), where \(V_0=\{r\}\) contains the root and \(V_n=\{t\}\) contains the terminal. Its arc set is partitioned as \(A=A_1\mathbin{\dot\cup}\cdots\mathbin{\dot\cup}A_n\), and every \(a\in A_i\) has its tail in \(V_{i-1}\) and its head in \(V_i\). Consequently, every directed root-to-terminal path visits exactly one node from every layer in increasing layer order.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The node and arc sets are partitioned into consecutive layers from the root to the terminal, and every root-to-terminal path visits each node layer once in order.
assumptions_latex: \(n\in\mathbb{N}\)
\(D=(V,A)\) is a finite directed graph with distinguished nodes \(r\) and \(t\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(A=\mathbin{\dot\bigcup}_{i=1}^{n}A_i\), every \(a\in A_i\) advances from \(V_{i-1}\) to \(V_i\), and every \(r\)-to-\(t\) path visits one node in each \(V_i\).

notation.meaning: arcs advancing from layer i-1 to layer i

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard definition of a strictly layered decision diagram
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

children.title: Layer Decision Domains
children.top_down_role: Decision alphabets associated with individual layers.

knowledge_statements.title: Layer Decision Domains
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Decision values available at each variable layer.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For ordered decision variables \(x_1,\ldots,x_n\), the decision domain at layer \(i\) is a finite set \(X_i\). Every arc \(a\in A_i\) has exactly one label \(\ell_i(a)\in X_i\), interpreted as assigning \(x_i=\ell_i(a)\). For a node \(u\in V_{i-1}\), the labels of arcs in \(A_i\) leaving \(u\) form the subset of \(X_i\) admitted at \(u\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Layer i has a finite decision domain; each layer-i arc assigns one domain value, and a node may admit only the values labeling its outgoing arcs.
assumptions_latex: \(i\in\{1,\ldots,n\}\)
Every \(a\in A_i\) advances from \(V_{i-1}\) to \(V_i\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: There is a labeling map \(\ell_i:A_i\to X_i\), with \(\ell_i(a)\) interpreted as the assigned value of \(x_i\).

notation.meaning: decision variable assigned at layer i

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard labeled-layer convention for decision diagrams
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

children.title: Transition Arcs
children.top_down_role: Permitted transitions between successive diagram states.

knowledge_statements.title: Transition Arcs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Labeled transitions between consecutive diagram layers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A transition arc at layer \(i\) is a triple \(a=(u,d,v)\) with \(u\in V_{i-1}\), \(d\in X_i\), and \(v\in V_i\). Traversing the arc appends the decision \(x_i=d\) to the label sequence of the path reaching \(u\) and continues to the state represented by \(v\). Arcs with the same endpoints but different labels are distinct.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A transition arc advances between consecutive layers and appends one labeled decision value to the path's decision sequence.
assumptions_latex: \(i\in\{1,\ldots,n\}\)
\(V_{i-1}\) and \(V_i\) are consecutive layers
\(X_i\) is the decision domain at layer \(i\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(A_i\subseteq V_{i-1}\times X_i\times V_i\).

notation.meaning: arc from u to v labeled d

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard transition semantics for layered decision diagrams
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

children.title: Layer–Arc Compatibility
children.top_down_role: Compatibility between layer domains, arc labels, source states, plus destination states.

knowledge_statements.title: Layer–Arc Compatibility
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Incidence and label condition for valid layered transitions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A labeled triple \(a=(u,d,v)\) is compatible with layer \(i\) precisely when \(a\in V_{i-1}\times X_i\times V_i\). A layered transition structure is compatible when every actual arc \(a\in A\) is compatible with a unique \(i\in\{1,\ldots,n\}\); equivalently, \(A\) is partitioned into sets \(A_i\subseteq V_{i-1}\times X_i\times V_i\). Consequently, no compatible arc skips a layer, remains within a layer, or points backward.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An actual arc is layer-compatible exactly when it advances one layer and carries a value from that layer's domain.
assumptions_latex: \(V_0,\ldots,V_n\) are pairwise disjoint
\(X_1,\ldots,X_n\) are prescribed decision domains
\(A\) is the set of actual labeled arcs
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(A=\mathbin{\dot\bigcup}_{i=1}^{n}A_i\) with \(A_i\subseteq V_{i-1}\times X_i\times V_i\).

notation.meaning: actual arcs compatible with layer i
decision domain assigned at layer i

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: direct compatibility predicate for a layered labeled graph
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

children.title: Root-to-Terminal Paths
children.top_down_role: Complete diagram paths from the root through the terminal layer.

knowledge_statements.title: Root-to-Terminal Paths
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Complete directed paths through all decision layers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A root-to-terminal path is a sequence \(P=(a_1,\ldots,a_n)\) such that \(a_i=(v_{i-1},d_i,v_i)\in A_i\), \(v_0=r\), and \(v_n=t\). Consecutive arcs share their intermediate node, so the path selects one compatible transition at every layer and has exactly \(n\) arcs.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A root-to-terminal path chooses one connected transition at every layer from the root to the terminal.
assumptions_latex: \(D\) is a depth-\(n\) layered decision diagram
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P\in\mathcal{P}_{r,t}\) iff \(P=(a_1,\ldots,a_n)\) satisfies the stated incidence conditions.

notation.meaning: decision label selected at layer i

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard directed-path definition specialized to a layered diagram

children.title: Solution Encoding
children.top_down_role: Decision assignments represented by complete paths.

knowledge_statements.title: Solution Encoding
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reading a complete assignment from path labels.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a root-to-terminal path \(P=(a_1,\ldots,a_n)\), with \(a_i=(v_{i-1},d_i,v_i)\), its encoded decision vector is \(\chi(P)=(d_1,\ldots,d_n)\in X_1\times\cdots\times X_n\). Thus the coordinate order is fixed by the layers, independently of the identities of the intermediate nodes.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The ordered arc labels of a complete path form its encoded decision vector.
assumptions_latex: \(P\in\mathcal{P}_{r,t}\)
Each arc in \(A_i\) has one label in \(X_i\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\chi:\mathcal{P}_{r,t}\to X_1\times\cdots\times X_n\), with \(\chi(P)_i=\ell_i(a_i)\).

notation.meaning: decision label of the path arc at layer i

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard label-sequence encoding of layered decision-diagram paths

children.title: Path–Solution Correspondence
children.top_down_role: One-to-one, many-to-one, or partial correspondence regimes.

knowledge_statements.title: Path–Solution Correspondence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact decision diagram semantics for feasible assignments.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\subseteq X_1\times\cdots\times X_n\) be the feasible set. The layered diagram is exact for \(F\) when its decoding map satisfies \(\chi(\mathcal{P}_{r,t})=F\). The correspondence is bijective when, additionally, distinct root-to-terminal paths have distinct label sequences. Under bijectivity, every feasible assignment has exactly one representing path and every representing path decodes to a feasible assignment.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An exact diagram represents all and only feasible solutions; injective decoding makes the representation one-to-one.
assumptions_latex: \(F\subseteq X_1\times\cdots\times X_n\)
\(\chi:\mathcal{P}_{r,t}\to X_1\times\cdots\times X_n\) is the path decoder
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Exactness is \(\chi(\mathcal{P}_{r,t})=F\); bijective correspondence is equivalent to exactness plus injectivity of \(\chi\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard exactness semantics for decision diagrams

children.title: Incomplete Path Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Path structures that do not encode complete admissible solutions.

knowledge_statements.title: Incomplete Path Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Why partial paths do not by themselves encode complete solutions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A directed prefix ending at layer \(k<n\) determines only \((d_1,\ldots,d_k)\) and therefore is not a complete assignment in \(X_1\times\cdots\times X_n\). It certifies extendability only when its final node can reach \(t\). If no such continuation exists, the prefix is a dead end; if continuations exist, it generally represents the set of all feasible completions rather than a single solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A partial path encodes only a prefix and may be dead or admit multiple feasible completions.
assumptions_latex: The path prefix ends at some \(v_k\in V_k\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The prefix encodes a complete solution only after extension to an element of \(\mathcal{P}_{r,t}\).

notation.meaning: last layer reached by the incomplete path

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: direct boundary of complete path encoding

children.title: Arc Value Encodings
children.top_down_role: Objective or resource contributions attached to transition arcs.

knowledge_statements.title: Arc Value Encodings
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Recovering a path value from contributions attached to arcs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \((M,\oplus,0)\) be a commutative monoid and let \(w:A\to M\) assign a value contribution to every arc. The arc-value encoding of a root-to-terminal path \(P=(a_1,
\ldots,a_n)\) is \(W(P)=w(a_1)\oplus\cdots\oplus w(a_n)\). For vector assignments, one may take \(M\) as a product space and let each \(w(a_i)\) have only coordinate \(i\) nonzero.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Arc values encode a path by aggregating the contributions attached to its selected arcs.
assumptions_latex: \((M,\oplus,0)\) is a commutative monoid
\(P=(a_1,\ldots,a_n)\in\mathcal{P}_{r,t}\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(W(P)=\bigoplus_{i=1}^{n}w(a_i)\).

notation.meaning: value contribution attached to arc a
aggregate value encoded by path P

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: additive path valuation is standard, but the intended arc-terminal convention is not source-resolved

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The monoid aggregation formula is mathematically standard, but no source establishes that it is the intended local meaning of arc-value encoding. The vector example also says coordinates are nonzero, although a general monoid only supplies an identity element.

children.title: Terminal Value Encodings
children.top_down_role: Residual or aggregate values attached to terminal nodes.

knowledge_statements.title: Terminal Value Encodings
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Recovering a path value from its terminal readout.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(T\) be a set of terminal nodes and \(g:T\to Y\) a terminal readout. A terminal-value encoding assigns to every root-to-terminal path \(P\) the value \(G(P)=g(\operatorname{term}(P))\). Such an encoding represents a prescribed path-value map \(H:\mathcal{P}_{r,T}\to Y\) exactly if \(H(P)=H(Q)\) whenever \(P\) and \(Q\) end at the same terminal; then \(g(t)\) equals this common value.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A terminal encoding is exact precisely when paths sharing a terminal must have the same prescribed value.
assumptions_latex: \(T\) is the diagram's terminal-node set
\(H:\mathcal{P}_{r,T}\to Y\) is the prescribed path-value map
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: An exact \(g:T\to Y\) exists iff \(\operatorname{term}(P)=\operatorname{term}(Q)\Rightarrow H(P)=H(Q)\).

notation.meaning: prescribed value of a complete path

review_flags: intended meaning of terminal value encoding is ambiguous without a decision-diagram source
single-terminal diagrams require an augmented or multiple-terminal convention for nonconstant values

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The factorization criterion through a terminal map is correct in isolation, but the surrounding diagram model previously has a single terminal. A source is required to determine whether this leaf intends multiple terminals, augmented terminal states, or a different terminal-value convention.

children.title: Distributed Path Value Encodings
children.top_down_role: Value allocation across multiple arcs along a path.

knowledge_statements.title: Distributed Path Value Encodings
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Path values decomposed across transitions and endpoint readouts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((M,\oplus,0)\) be a commutative monoid, let \(w_i:A_i\to M\) be layerwise contributions, and let \(g:T\to M\) be a terminal contribution. The distributed value encoded by \(P=(a_1,\ldots,a_n)\), ending at \(t_P\in T\), is \(H(P)=w_1(a_1)\oplus\cdots\oplus w_n(a_n)\oplus g(t_P)\). Arc-only and terminal-only encodings arise by setting, respectively, \(g=0\) or every \(w_i=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A distributed encoding aggregates layerwise arc contributions together with a terminal contribution.
assumptions_latex: \((M,\oplus,0)\) is a commutative monoid
\(P=(a_1,\ldots,a_n)\in\mathcal{P}_{r,T}\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(H(P)=\left(\bigoplus_{i=1}^{n}w_i(a_i)\right)\oplus g(t_P)\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: algebraic decomposition of a path value

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algebraic decomposition is coherent, but its terminal component inherits the unresolved change from one terminal to a terminal set. The intended decision-diagram encoding convention cannot be fixed reliably without a source.

children.title: Arc–Terminal Value Equivalence
children.top_down_role: Representation-preserving transfers between arc-local values plus terminal values.

knowledge_statements.title: Arc–Terminal Value Equivalence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalence criterion for moving value between arcs and terminals.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((G,+,0)\) be an abelian group and let \(w:A\to G\) define \(W(P)=\sum_{a\in P}w(a)\). An equivalent terminal encoding \(g:T\to G\), satisfying \(W(P)=g(\operatorname{term}(P))\) for every root-to-terminal path \(P\), exists if and only if all root-to-terminal paths ending at the same terminal have equal arc sums. When this condition holds, \(g(t)\) is that common sum and is uniquely determined for each reachable terminal.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Arc sums can be replaced by terminal values exactly when every path to a given terminal has the same sum.
assumptions_latex: \((G,+,0)\) is an abelian group
Every terminal under consideration is reachable from \(r\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\exists g\;\forall P,\ W(P)=g(\operatorname{term}(P))\iff \forall P,Q,\ \operatorname{term}(P)=\operatorname{term}(Q)\Rightarrow W(P)=W(Q)\).

notation.meaning: sum of arc values on path P

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: elementary factorization criterion through the terminal map

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The displayed factorization criterion is mathematically valid, but no source supports this as the intended arc-terminal equivalence, and it relies on the unresolved multiple-terminal convention. The claim is an equivalence property rather than mathematical duality, so its content kind also requires correction once the intended local concept is sourced.

children.title: Decision-Alphabet Diagram Family
children.top_down_role: Optimization diagrams distinguished by binary or finite-domain decision alphabets.

knowledge_statements.title: Binary Decision Diagrams
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Binary, rooted, acyclic decision-diagram representation of a Boolean function.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\{0,1\}^n\to\{0,1\}\). A binary decision diagram for \(f\) is a rooted directed acyclic graph whose nonterminal nodes are labeled by variables \(x_i\), each having exactly two outgoing arcs labeled \(0\) and \(1\), and whose terminal nodes are labeled \(0\) or \(1\). For every \(a\in\{0,1\}^n\), following at a node labeled \(x_i\) the arc labeled \(a_i\) reaches a terminal labeled \(f(a)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A binary decision diagram evaluates a Boolean function by following 0- or 1-labeled arcs according to a binary assignment until the corresponding output terminal is reached.
assumptions_latex: \(n\in\mathbb{N}\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{val}_D(a)=f(a)\) for every \(a\in\{0,1\}^n\).

notation.meaning: terminal value reached under assignment a

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition and content kind fit the Binary Decision Diagrams leaf, and the notation is sufficiently introduced. However, the record has no citation, locator, or standard-field rationale, so its graph and evaluation conventions lack the required evidence.

knowledge_statements.title: Multivalued Decision Diagrams
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Decision diagrams for variables with arbitrary finite domains.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X_i\) have a finite domain \(\mathcal D_i\), and let \(F:\prod_{i=1}^n\mathcal D_i\to\mathcal T\). A multivalued decision diagram for \(F\) is a rooted directed acyclic graph whose nonterminal nodes are labeled by variables and whose node labeled \(X_i\) has one outgoing arc for each admissible value in \(\mathcal D_i\). Terminals are labeled in \(\mathcal T\), and following arcs selected by any assignment \(a\) reaches the terminal labeled \(F(a)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An MDD represents a finite-domain function by branching once for each possible value of the variable tested at a node.
assumptions_latex: \(n\in\mathbb N\)
\(1\leq |\mathcal D_i|<\infty\) for every \(i\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{val}_D(a)=F(a)\) for every \(a\in\prod_{i=1}^n\mathcal D_i\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition fits the Multivalued Decision Diagrams leaf and consistently describes finite-domain branching. A source is required to establish the intended MDD convention, particularly the arbitrary terminal-label set and the requirement of one arc per admissible value.

children.title: Canonical Diagram Form Regimes
children.top_down_role: Ordering restrictions and graph reductions governing equivalence, compactness, and canonical representation.

knowledge_statements.title: Ordered Decision Diagrams
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Decision diagrams respecting one fixed variable order on every root-to-terminal path.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix a permutation \(\pi\) of \(\{1,\ldots,n\}\). A decision diagram is ordered with respect to \(\pi\) if, on every directed root-to-terminal path, each variable occurs at most once and the encountered variable labels form a subsequence of \(x_{\pi(1)},\ldots,x_{\pi(n)}\). Equivalently, every arc from a node labeled \(x_{\pi(i)}\) to a nonterminal node labeled \(x_{\pi(j)}\) satisfies \(i<j\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An ordered decision diagram tests variables without repetition and in a single fixed relative order along every evaluation path.
assumptions_latex: \(\pi\) is a permutation of \(\{1,\ldots,n\}\)
\(D\) is a finite rooted acyclic decision diagram
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((u,v)\in A\), \(\ell(u)=x_{\pi(i)}\), and \(\ell(v)=x_{\pi(j)}\) imply \(i<j\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition and content kind fit Ordered Decision Diagrams. The path-based and arc-based formulations are standard under the implicit assumption that relevant nodes lie on root-to-terminal paths, but no authoritative source or inspectable locator supports that convention.

children.title: Reduced Forms
children.top_down_role: Diagram forms after all selected redundancy eliminations.

knowledge_statements.title: Reduced Forms
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Standard reduction conditions for ordered binary decision diagrams.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An ordered binary decision diagram is reduced if it satisfies both conditions: no nonterminal node has identical \(0\)- and \(1\)-successors, and no two distinct nonterminal nodes have the same variable label together with the same \(0\)-successor and the same \(1\)-successor. Thus redundant tests have been eliminated and roots of isomorphic labeled subdiagrams have been merged.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A reduced ordered BDD contains neither a test with equal outcomes nor two distinct nodes representing the same labeled residual subfunction.
assumptions_latex: \(D\) is an ordered binary decision diagram
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{lo}(v)\neq\operatorname{hi}(v)\) for every nonterminal \(v\), and equal labeled successor triples identify the same node.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition correctly states the two usual reduction conditions for ordered BDDs and fits the Reduced Forms leaf. It cannot pass evidence review because no source or specific locator is supplied.

children.title: Quasireduced Forms
children.top_down_role: Layer-preserving forms retaining selected structural redundancies.

knowledge_statements.title: Quasireduced Forms
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Ordered diagrams merging duplicate subdiagrams while retaining redundant variable tests.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An ordered binary decision diagram with fixed variable order is quasireduced if every root-to-terminal path contains exactly one node for each variable, and no two distinct nonterminal nodes have the same variable label, \(0\)-successor, and \(1\)-successor. Nodes with equal \(0\)- and \(1\)-successors are permitted, so all variables remain represented on every path even when a test does not affect the residual function.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A quasireduced ordered BDD merges duplicate subdiagrams but retains redundant tests so that every path includes every variable level.
assumptions_latex: \(D\) is an ordered binary decision diagram with a fixed order
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every root-to-terminal path has \(n\) nonterminal nodes, while equal labeled successor triples identify the same node.

notation.meaning: number of variables in the fixed order

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition fits the Quasireduced Forms leaf, but quasireduced terminology varies across the literature. An authoritative source is needed to confirm that this taxonomy requires every root-to-terminal path to contain every variable while applying only isomorphic-subdiagram merging.

children.title: Unreduced Forms
children.top_down_role: Diagram forms prior to structural reduction.

knowledge_statements.title: Unreduced Forms
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Ordered diagrams before either standard node-reduction rule is imposed.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An unreduced ordered binary decision diagram is an ordered binary decision diagram on which neither reduction condition is required: distinct nodes may have the same variable label and identical ordered successor pair, and a node may have the same \(0\)- and \(1\)-successor. Its semantics remains determined by root-to-terminal evaluation, independently of these structural redundancies.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An unreduced ordered BDD may contain duplicate residual subdiagrams and tests whose two outcomes lead to the same continuation.
assumptions_latex: \(D\) is an ordered binary decision diagram
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Duplicate labeled successor triples and nodes satisfying \(\operatorname{lo}(v)=\operatorname{hi}(v)\) are allowed.

notation.meaning: the two successors of node v

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition and content kind fit Unreduced Forms, and the stated redundancies are semantically harmless. The precise reduction-level terminology nevertheless has no cited source or locator.

children.title: Reduction-Level Tradeoffs
children.top_down_role: Size, layering, canonicality, plus operational tradeoffs across reduction levels.

knowledge_statements.title: Reduction-Level Tradeoffs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Size and structural regularity across standard ordered-BDD reduction levels.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a fixed Boolean function and variable order, applying only isomorphic-subdiagram merging to the complete ordered decision tree yields a quasireduced diagram; additionally eliminating every node with identical successors yields the reduced diagram. Neither operation changes the represented function, and each weakly decreases the numbers of nodes and arcs. Quasireduction preserves one node per variable level on every path, whereas full reduction may skip levels and usually gives the smallest diagram under these two rules.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Stronger reduction cannot enlarge a fixed-order BDD and preserves its function, but full reduction sacrifices the uniform level structure retained by quasireduction.
assumptions_latex: The Boolean function and variable order are fixed
Reduction uses duplicate-subdiagram merging and redundant-test elimination
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(|V_{m red}|\leq |V_{m quasi}|\leq |V_{m tree}|\), with all three diagrams representing the same function.

notation.meaning: node set of the complete ordered decision tree

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The property role fits Reduction-Level Tradeoffs, and the preservation and monotone-size claims are plausible. A source is required for the exact quasireduction convention and for the statement that full reduction 'usually' gives the smallest diagram, which is too imprecise to assess without the intended comparison class.

children.title: Canonical Representation Regimes
children.top_down_role: Ordering, reduction, plus labeling regimes supporting unique representations.

knowledge_statements.title: Canonical Representation Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditions under which a decision-diagram representation is canonical up to isomorphism.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A decision-diagram regime \(\mathcal R\) is canonical for a function class \(\mathcal F\) if every \(f\in\mathcal F\) has a diagram in \(\mathcal R\), and any two diagrams \(D_1,D_2\in\mathcal R\) representing \(f\) are isomorphic as rooted, arc-labeled, node-labeled directed acyclic graphs. For ordered binary decision diagrams, fixing the variable order and terminal labels and imposing both standard reduction rules defines such a regime.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A regime is canonical when each represented function determines exactly one permitted diagram up to a label-preserving rooted graph isomorphism.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal F\) is a specified function class
\(\mathcal R\) fixes all representation conventions relevant to identity
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(D_1,D_2\in\mathcal R\) and \(f_{D_1}=f_{D_2}\) imply \(D_1\cong D_2\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition content kind fits Canonical Representation Regimes, and the abstract uniqueness-up-to-isomorphism condition is coherent. The existence requirement and the claimed reduced ordered-BDD instance need an authoritative source with a specific locator.

children.title: Diagram Isomorphism
children.top_down_role: Structural equivalence under admissible node or label correspondence.

knowledge_statements.title: Diagram Isomorphism
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Label-preserving rooted isomorphism for decision diagrams.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Decision diagrams \(D=(V,A,r,\ell_V,\ell_A)\) and \(D'=(V',A',r',\ell'_V,\ell'_A)\) are isomorphic if there exists a bijection \(\varphi:V\to V'\) such that \(\varphi(r)=r'\), node labels satisfy \(\ell'_V(\varphi(v))=\ell_V(v)\), and \((u,v)\in A\) with arc label \(a\) holds exactly when \((\varphi(u),\varphi(v))\in A'\) has label \(a\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Two diagrams are isomorphic when a root- and label-preserving vertex bijection preserves exactly all directed labeled arcs.
assumptions_latex: \(D\) and \(D'\) are finite rooted arc- and node-labeled directed acyclic graphs
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(D\cong D'\) if and only if such a bijection \(\varphi\) exists.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The label-preserving rooted graph-isomorphism definition fits the Diagram Isomorphism leaf and is internally consistent. It lacks the required decision-diagram-specific citation and locator.

children.title: Canonicality via Isomorphism
children.top_down_role: Use of isomorphism classes when comparing canonical diagram forms.

knowledge_statements.title: Canonicality via Isomorphism
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonicity theorem for reduced ordered binary decision diagrams.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D_1\) and \(D_2\) be reduced ordered binary decision diagrams over the same Boolean variables, with the same fixed variable order and the same terminal-label convention. If they represent Boolean functions \(f_1\) and \(f_2\), respectively, then \(f_1=f_2\) if and only if \(D_1\cong D_2\) by a root-, node-label-, and arc-label-preserving isomorphism.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With variable order and terminal conventions fixed, two reduced ordered BDDs represent the same Boolean function exactly when their labeled rooted graphs are isomorphic.
assumptions_latex: \(D_1,D_2\) are reduced ordered binary decision diagrams
Both diagrams use the same variable order and terminal convention

notation.meaning: Boolean function represented by diagram D

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The theorem content kind is correct for the canonicity claim, and the fixed variable order, reduction, and terminal conventions are the essential hypotheses. Because this is a nontrivial theorem and no source or theorem locator is provided, it requires authoritative evidence.

children.title: Canonicality Failure Regimes
children.top_down_role: Representation choices under which equivalent objects admit distinct diagram forms.

knowledge_statements.title: Canonicality Failure Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concrete mechanisms destroying uniqueness of decision-diagram representations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Canonicity fails if either the variable order or full reduction is not fixed. For \(f(x_1,x_2)=x_1\wedge x_2\), reduced ordered diagrams using orders \(x_1<x_2\) and \(x_2<x_1\) represent the same function but are not label-preserving isomorphic. With one fixed order, duplicating an isomorphic residual subdiagram or inserting a node whose two arcs share a successor likewise produces a distinct unreduced diagram for the same function.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Different variable orders, duplicate subdiagrams, or redundant tests can yield nonisomorphic diagrams representing the same Boolean function.
assumptions_latex: Diagram identity must preserve variable and arc labels
At least one ordering or reduction convention is omitted
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: There exist \(D_1\not\cong D_2\) such that \(f_{D_1}=f_{D_2}\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure_boundary kind fits the leaf, and the examples identify standard mechanisms for loss of uniqueness. A source is needed to support the exact regime-level claim and to confirm that the omitted conventions are quantified as intended.

children.title: Intersection Diagrams
children.top_down_role: Diagram constructions retaining paths admitted by every component.

knowledge_statements.title: Intersection Diagrams
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Synchronized product representation of the intersection of two diagram languages.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D_1,D_2\) be layered decision diagrams over the same ordered variables and compatible arc alphabets, representing assignment sets \(S_1,S_2\). Form a diagram whose layer-\(i\) nodes are reachable pairs \((u_1,u_2)\), with an arc labeled \(a\) from \((u_1,u_2)\) to \((v_1,v_2)\) exactly when each \(D_j\) contains an arc labeled \(a\) from \(u_j\) to \(v_j\). Its accepting terminal pairs represent exactly \(S_1\cap S_2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Synchronizing equal-labeled transitions in two compatible layered diagrams produces a product diagram whose accepted assignments are exactly their intersection.
assumptions_latex: \(D_1,D_2\) use the same variable layering and compatible value labels
\(S_j\) is the assignment set accepted by \(D_j\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(S(D_1\otimes D_2)=S(D_1)\cap S(D_2)=S_1\cap S_2\).

notation.meaning: assignment set accepted by diagram D

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation kind fits Intersection Diagrams, and the synchronized-product construction plausibly recognizes the intersection. An authoritative source is required for the compatibility assumptions, accepting-terminal convention, and exact intersection conclusion.

children.title: Product Diagrams
children.top_down_role: Synchronized state-space constructions over component diagrams.

assumptions_latex: Each diagram is a finite layered directed acyclic graph with common variable order \(x_1,\ldots,x_n\).
Every arc from layer \(i-1\) to layer \(i\) carries a value in the domain \(D_i\).

notation.meaning: Language of root-to-terminal label sequences accepted by a diagram

review_flags: No supplied locator directly supports decision-diagram products; specialist source required.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Layer-synchronous product for diagrams sharing a variable order.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For layered diagrams \(G_1=(V_1,A_1)\) and \(G_2=(V_2,A_2)\), their product \(P=G_1\otimes G_2\) has at layer \(i\) the reachable node pairs \((u_1,u_2)\), with root \((r_1,r_2)\) and terminal \((t_1,t_2)\). It contains an arc labeled \(a\in D_i\) from \((u_1,u_2)\) to \((v_1,v_2)\) exactly when each \(G_j\) contains an arc labeled \(a\) from \(u_j\) to \(v_j\). Consequently, a label sequence is accepted by \(P\) exactly when both factors accept it, so \(L(P)=L(G_1)\cap L(G_2)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A product diagram pairs same-layer states and advances both components on the same label; its accepted assignments are exactly those accepted by both factor diagrams.
knowledge_statements.title: Product Diagrams

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition fits the Product Diagrams leaf and is internally coherent for layer-synchronous labeled diagrams, but source_refs is empty. A specialist decision-diagram or automata source with a specific definition, theorem, section, or page locator is required before the intersection-language claim can be reviewed as sourced candidate knowledge.

children.title: Synchronized Product Structure
children.top_down_role: Layer, variable, state, plus transition alignment across product components.

assumptions_latex: The factor diagrams use identical layers and label domains \(D_1,\ldots,D_n\).
Only node pairs reachable from the paired root are retained.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\delta_i((u_1,u_2),a)=(\delta_i^1(u_1,a),\delta_i^2(u_2,a))\) whenever both component transitions exist.
review_flags: No supplied locator directly supports synchronized decision-diagram products; specialist source required.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Transition-level description of a layer-synchronized product.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At layer \(i\), the synchronized product state is a pair \((u_1,u_2)\). For a label \(a\in D_i\), its transition is defined by \(\delta_i((u_1,u_2),a)=(\delta_i^1(u_1,a),\delta_i^2(u_2,a))\) if both component transitions are defined, and is undefined otherwise. Thus every product path projects to two factor paths with the same label sequence, and any two factor paths having the same label sequence lift uniquely to a product path when the factors are deterministic.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A synchronized product moves both component states on one common variable value, rejecting a move whenever either component lacks the corresponding transition.
knowledge_statements.title: Synchronized Product Structure

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation fits Synchronized Product Structure, and the deterministic qualification appropriately limits unique lifting. However, no citation supports the transition construction or its scope. A specific specialist locator is required to establish the intended deterministic decision-diagram convention and synchronized-product semantics.

children.title: Intersection–Product Equivalence Regimes
children.top_down_role: Conditions under which product constructions realize diagram intersections.

assumptions_latex: The diagrams are exact, layered, and share the same variable order and label domains.
The product retains every reachable synchronized pair and every common labeled transition.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L(G_1\otimes G_2)=L(G_1)\cap L(G_2)\), while omission of reachable pairs or common transitions may destroy equality.
review_flags: No supplied locator directly supports the exact equivalence regime; specialist source required.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact-language regime, excluding relaxed or reduced products that discard required structure.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G_1\) and \(G_2\) be exact layered diagrams over the same ordered variables and domains. If \(G_1\otimes G_2\) contains precisely all reachable synchronized state pairs and all transitions whose labels occur simultaneously in both factors, then \(L(G_1\otimes G_2)=L(G_1)\cap L(G_2)\). The equivalence need not hold for factors with incompatible orders, for asynchronous composition without an explicit alignment construction, or after deleting a reachable pair or common transition that lies on an accepting product path.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Intersection and product coincide for complete synchronous products of exact, order-compatible diagrams; incompatible orders or incomplete products fall outside this equivalence regime.
knowledge_statements.title: Intersection–Product Equivalence Regimes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The theorem kind fits the equivalence-regime leaf, and the synchronous intersection identity is plausible under the stated compatibility assumptions. No source is cited, however, and the boundary claims concerning incompatible orders, asynchronous composition, and deletion of accepting structure require specialist support with an inspectable locator.

assumptions_latex: Each \(G_k\) is an exact diagram for a constraint-defined set \(X_k\subseteq D_1\times\cdots\times D_n\).
All diagrams use a common variable order.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(X=\bigcap_{k=1}^m X_k=\bigcap_{k=1}^m L(G_k)=L(G_1\otimes\cdots\otimes G_m)\).

notation.meaning: Feasible set represented by component k

review_flags: No supplied locator addresses multiple decision-diagram decompositions; specialist source required.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conjunctive decomposition into exact diagrams with a common order.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose a feasible set decomposes as \(X=\bigcap_{k=1}^m X_k\), where each component set \(X_k\subseteq D_1\times\cdots\times D_n\) has an exact layered diagram \(G_k\) satisfying \(L(G_k)=X_k\). The collection \((G_1,\ldots,G_m)\) is a multiple-diagram decomposition of \(X\). Feasibility of an assignment is equivalent to acceptance by every component, and the iterated synchronized product, when fully constructed, satisfies \(L(G_1\otimes\cdots\otimes G_m)=X\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible set may be represented by several exact component diagrams; an assignment is feasible precisely when every component accepts it.
knowledge_statements.title: Multiple-Diagram Decompositions

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation kind fits this topic and the conjunctive decomposition is mathematically plausible when assignments and label sequences are identified under the common order. Because source_refs is empty, the multiple-diagram construction and iterated-product equality lack inspectable support. A specialist source with a specific locator is required.

children.title: State Sufficiency
children.top_down_role: State information adequate for preserving future feasibility plus objective distinctions.

assumptions_latex: A finite-horizon recursive model has histories \(h_i\) after decisions \(1,\ldots,i\).
For each history, feasible continuations and their continuation costs are well defined.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(s_i\) is sufficient exactly when equal states induce identical feasible continuation-cost functions.

notation.meaning: Optimal continuation cost under suffix y, with infeasibility represented by positive infinity

review_flags: No supplied locator directly supports sufficient states in exact diagram compilation; specialist source required.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sufficiency includes both future feasibility and continuation cost.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A state map \(s_i\) is sufficient at layer \(i\) if, for every pair of histories \(h_i,h_i'\) with \(s_i(h_i)=s_i(h_i')\), every suffix \(y\in D_{i+1}\times\cdots\times D_n\) has identical continuation value: \(Q_i(h_i,y)=Q_i(h_i',y)\), where \(Q_i=+\infty\) denotes an infeasible suffix. Equivalently, the state determines all information from the prefix needed to decide future feasibility and evaluate every future contribution to the objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A state is sufficient when histories mapped to it have exactly the same feasible suffixes and the same cost for every suffix.
knowledge_statements.title: State Sufficiency

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition kind fits State Sufficiency and the intended future-behavior criterion is clear. The record nevertheless has no source, and Q_i is described as an optimal continuation cost 'under suffix y' even though a fixed suffix normally determines a continuation value rather than an optimization. A specialist locator is needed to fix and support the precise value semantics.

children.title: History Compression
children.top_down_role: Replacement of decision histories by compact state summaries.

assumptions_latex: Histories at layer \(i\) form a set \(H_i\).
A map \(s_i:H_i\to S_i\) is given.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The compression is exact precisely when every fiber \(s_i^{-1}(q)\) consists of continuation-equivalent histories.

notation.meaning: Set of decision histories through layer i
Compressed state set at layer i

review_flags: No supplied locator directly supports history compression for decision diagrams; specialist source required.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Compression is a quotient of prefix histories by future behavior.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: History compression at layer \(i\) is a map \(s_i:H_i\to S_i\) that replaces each prefix history \(h_i\) by a state \(s_i(h_i)\). It is exact when \(s_i(h_i)=s_i(h_i')\) implies that \(h_i\) and \(h_i'\) admit the same feasible suffixes and assign the same continuation cost to each suffix. Hence each fiber \(s_i^{-1}(q)\) may be represented by one diagram node without changing the represented feasible assignments or their path values.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: History compression maps many prefixes to one state and is exact when all prefixes in each state have identical future feasibility and costs.
knowledge_statements.title: History Compression

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition fits History Compression, but no citation is supplied. Moreover, the final inference that each fiber can be represented by one node also depends on well-defined state transitions and arc values, not solely continuation equivalence as stated. A specialist source is needed to determine the exact hypotheses and formulation.

children.title: Sufficient-State Compression
children.top_down_role: Compression regimes that retain all distinctions needed by later layers.

assumptions_latex: The recursive model has finite decision domains and horizon \(n\).
Each state map \(s_i\) is sufficient for future feasibility and continuation cost.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The state-layer diagram is exact, and its layer width is at most \(|s_i(H_i)|\).
review_flags: No supplied locator directly supports the sufficient-state compression principle; specialist source required.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact compilation by retaining one node per reachable sufficient state.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Construct a layered diagram whose layer-\(i\) nodes are the reachable values in \(s_i(H_i)\), and whose arc labeled \(a\in D_{i+1}\) maps state \(s_i(h_i)\) to \(s_{i+1}(h_i,a)\) whenever the extended history is feasible. If every \(s_i\) is sufficient and the transition and arc value depend only on the current state and \(a\), then the diagram preserves every feasible assignment and its objective value. Its width at layer \(i\) is at most \(|s_i(H_i)|\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: One node per reachable sufficient state yields an exact diagram when transitions and arc values depend only on that state and the next decision.
knowledge_statements.title: Sufficient-State Compression

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The principle kind fits Sufficient-State Compression and the compilation idea is plausible. No source supports the construction, exactness claim, or width statement. Also, if the layer nodes are exactly the reachable values s_i(H_i), the width is ordinarily equal to their cardinality rather than merely bounded above by it, absent further node elimination or conventions. A specialist locator is required.

children.title: Information-Loss Boundaries
children.top_down_role: History distinctions whose removal compromises exact representation.

assumptions_latex: Two reachable histories \(h_i,h_i'\) are mapped to one state.
There exists a suffix whose feasibility or continuation cost differs between the histories.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Any single-node continuation rule for the merged state must misrepresent at least one of the two histories.

notation.meaning: Feasible suffix set after a history
Continuation cost of suffix y after a history

review_flags: No supplied locator directly supports this exactness boundary; specialist source required.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp obstruction to exact compression of two histories.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If histories \(h_i\) and \(h_i'\) satisfy either \(F_i(h_i)\ne F_i(h_i')\) or \(Q_i(h_i,y)\ne Q_i(h_i',y)\) for some suffix \(y\) feasible after both, then identifying them loses information required for exact compilation. A single merged node assigns one availability and one continuation value to each suffix, so it must either admit an infeasible assignment, exclude a feasible assignment, or assign an incorrect path value. Thus continuation equivalence is necessary for an exact merge.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Merging histories with different feasible suffixes or suffix costs necessarily introduces a feasibility or objective-value error.
knowledge_statements.title: Information-Loss Boundaries

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure_boundary kind is appropriate and the obstruction is plausible for a merged node constrained to one history-independent continuation mapping. With no source_refs, however, the necessity claim and the assumed exact-compilation model are unsupported. A specialist source with a precise locator is required.

children.title: State Equivalence
children.top_down_role: Future-behavior equivalence among states at compatible diagram positions.

assumptions_latex: Nodes \(u\) and \(v\) lie in the same layer of a weighted decision diagram.
Suffix paths are compared by label sequence and accumulated weight.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(u\sim v\) exactly when their weighted residual languages coincide.

notation.meaning: Residual mapping from suffix labels to path value, undefined for rejected suffixes

review_flags: No supplied locator directly supports weighted state equivalence in decision diagrams; specialist source required.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Weighted residual equivalence for nodes in one layer.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For same-layer nodes \(u\) and \(v\), define \(u\sim v\) if their weighted residual mappings are identical: for every suffix label sequence \(y\), a path labeled \(y\) reaches the terminal from \(u\) if and only if one does so from \(v\), and whenever such paths exist their accumulated continuation values agree. In symbols, \(u\sim v\) exactly when \(R_u=R_v\), including equality of their domains. In an unweighted diagram this reduces to equality of residual languages.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Two same-layer states are equivalent when they accept exactly the same suffixes and assign the same continuation value to each suffix.
knowledge_statements.title: State Equivalence

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition kind fits State Equivalence, but the residual mapping R_u is not necessarily a function when several paths with the same suffix label sequence can have different accumulated weights. Determinism or path-value uniqueness must be stated, or the residual object must be set-valued. Because no source is cited, a specialist locator is needed to resolve the intended weighted-diagram model.

children.title: Exact Node Merging
children.top_down_role: Node consolidation that preserves the represented solution space plus values.

assumptions_latex: Nodes \(u\) and \(v\) lie in the same layer and satisfy \(u\sim v\).
All incoming arcs can be redirected while preserving their labels and weights.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Merging \(u\) and \(v\) preserves the diagram's accepted assignments and root-to-terminal values.

notation.meaning: State-equivalence relation defined by equal weighted residuals

review_flags: No supplied locator directly supports exact node merging in weighted decision diagrams; specialist source required.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact quotienting of same-layer nodes with identical weighted residual behavior.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G'\) be obtained from \(G\) by replacing same-layer nodes \(u\) and \(v\) satisfying \(u\sim v\) with one node, redirecting every incoming arc to that node, and retaining one equivalent copy of their continuation structure. Then every root-to-terminal path in \(G\) has a path in \(G'\) with the same label sequence and total value, and conversely. Therefore \(G'\) represents the same feasible assignments and assignment values as \(G\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Equivalent same-layer nodes may be identified without changing accepted assignments or their path values.
knowledge_statements.title: Exact Node Merging

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The theorem kind fits Exact Node Merging, but the construction relies on an undefined choice of an 'equivalent copy' of continuation structure and inherits the unstated path-value-uniqueness assumptions of the equivalence definition. No source supports the theorem or construction. A specialist locator is required before its hypotheses and conclusion can be validated.

children.title: Equivalence-Based Merging
children.top_down_role: Use of state-equivalence classes as exact merge groups.

assumptions_latex: A finite layered decision diagram \(G\) and a decidable same-layer equivalence relation \(\sim\) are given.
Equivalent nodes have identical weighted residual mappings.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The quotient diagram \(G/{\sim}\) is exact and has one node for each reachable equivalence class.
review_flags: No supplied locator directly supports the quotient construction; specialist source required.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Layerwise quotient construction under exact state equivalence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input \(G\) and \(\sim\). At each layer, partition reachable nodes into classes \([u]_{\sim}\). Create one quotient node per class. For every original arc \(u\xrightarrow{a,w}v\), insert \([u]_{\sim}\xrightarrow{a,w}[v]_{\sim}\), coalescing duplicate arcs. Initialize with the class of the root and retain classes that can reach the terminal. Stop after the final layer and output \(G/{\sim}\). Because \(\sim\) equates weighted residual mappings, the output preserves all accepted label sequences and their values.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Partition each layer into exact equivalence classes, redirect arcs between classes, remove duplicates and dead classes, and return the resulting exact quotient diagram.
knowledge_statements.title: Equivalence-Based Merging

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits Equivalence-Based Merging, but the quotient procedure is not yet reliable. Coalescing duplicate arcs can lose distinct weights, and equality of residual mappings alone does not explicitly establish that the proposed arc-level quotient is well defined for every representative. With no cited source, specialist support is required to specify congruence and duplicate-arc conditions.

children.title: Unsafe Merge Boundaries
children.top_down_role: State distinctions whose collapse changes feasibility, values, or continuation structure.

assumptions_latex: Same-layer nodes \(u\) and \(v\) are not state-equivalent.
They are nevertheless replaced by a single node with one continuation structure.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The merge cannot preserve every accepted suffix and its continuation value for both incoming histories.

notation.meaning: Weighted residual mapping at node u

review_flags: No supplied locator directly supports the unsafe-merge boundary; specialist source required.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exactness boundary for identifying two same-layer nodes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(u\not\sim v\), then either the residual-language domains differ or some common suffix has different continuation value. In the first case, a suffix in \(\operatorname{dom}(R_u)\triangle\operatorname{dom}(R_v)\) must become incorrectly admitted or excluded after merging. In the second case, a merged node can assign only one continuation value to a common suffix and therefore cannot preserve both \(R_u\) and \(R_v\). Hence merging non-equivalent nodes is unsafe for exact representation, although it may define a deliberate relaxation or restriction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Non-equivalent nodes cannot be merged exactly: some suffix is admitted incorrectly, excluded incorrectly, or assigned the wrong continuation value.
knowledge_statements.title: Unsafe Merge Boundaries

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure_boundary kind fits Unsafe Merge Boundaries, and the conclusion follows under a functional weighted-residual model. That model requires determinism or unique continuation values for each suffix, which is not explicitly assumed, and no source is provided. A specialist locator is required to validate the exact unsafe-merge boundary.

children.title: Resource State Components
children.top_down_role: Accumulated or residual resource information carried by diagram states.

knowledge_statements.title: Resource State Components
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Resource coordinates in a layered exact decision-diagram state model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let decisions be ordered as \(x_1,\ldots,x_n\), with domains \(D_i\), and let a prefix be \(p=(x_1,\ldots,x_i)\). A resource state component is a map \(r_i:P_i\to R_i\) for which there exist transition maps \(T_i:R_{i-1}\times D_i\to R_i\) satisfying \(r_i(p)=T_i(r_{i-1}(p^-),x_i)\). It is resource-sufficient when any two prefixes \(p,q\in P_i\) with \(r_i(p)=r_i(q)\) have identical admissible resource continuations: for every suffix \(y\in D_{i+1}\times\cdots\times D_n\), extending \(p\) by \(y\) satisfies all tracked resource restrictions if and only if extending \(q\) by \(y\) does.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A resource component recursively summarizes a prefix so equal summaries admit exactly the same resource-feasible suffixes.
assumptions_latex: \(P_i\subseteq D_1\times\cdots\times D_i\) is the set of reachable prefixes.
Tracked resource restrictions have a well-defined truth value for every complete decision sequence.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Equality of resource states implies equality of the tracked resource-continuation languages.

notation.meaning: Prefix obtained from p by deleting its last decision.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition fits the resource-state leaf and is internally coherent, but no citation supports this particular recursive sufficiency formulation or terminology.

children.title: Feasibility State Components
children.top_down_role: State information used to distinguish admissible future continuations.

knowledge_statements.title: Feasibility State Components
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Residual-feasibility coordinates for exact recursive compilation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F\subseteq D_1\times\cdots\times D_n\) be the feasible decision sequences and let \(P_i\) contain the reachable length-\(i\) prefixes. A feasibility state component is a map \(f_i:P_i\to S_i\) such that, whenever \(f_i(p)=f_i(q)\), the residual feasible languages coincide:
\[
\{y\in D_{i+1}\times\cdots\times D_n:(p,y)\in F\}=\{y\in D_{i+1}\times\cdots\times D_n:(q,y)\in F\}.
\]
If maps \(U_i:S_{i-1}\times D_i\to S_i\) also satisfy \(f_i(p)=U_i(f_{i-1}(p^-),x_i)\), the component is recursively updateable and may serve as an exact node-merging key.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasibility component identifies prefixes precisely when they admit the same feasible suffixes, and may be updated recursively.
assumptions_latex: Each domain \(D_i\) is finite.
Feasibility is represented by a set \(F\) of complete sequences.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Equal feasibility states have equal residual feasible languages.

notation.meaning: Set of feasible complete decision sequences.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The residual-language condition fits the leaf, but no source is cited. The plain statement says prefixes are identified precisely when their suffix languages agree, whereas the formal statement requires only that equal states imply equal languages.

children.title: Objective State Components
children.top_down_role: State information needed to preserve future objective contributions.

knowledge_statements.title: Objective State Components
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cost coordinates sufficient for exact optimization over diagram suffixes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an ordered finite-domain minimization problem, let \(c(p,y)\) denote the objective value of the complete sequence formed from prefix \(p\in P_i\) and suffix \(y\). An objective state component is a pair \((a_i,o_i)\), where \(a_i:P_i\to\mathbb{R}\) is accumulated cost and \(o_i:P_i\to O_i\) is a residual-objective descriptor, such that \(o_i(p)=o_i(q)\) implies the existence of a constant \(\delta=a_i(p)-a_i(q)\) satisfying \(c(p,y)=c(q,y)+\delta\) for every suffix \(y\) feasible after both prefixes. Consequently, one shared continuation subdiagram can represent both prefixes after adjusting their incoming path costs by \(\delta\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An objective component records accumulated cost and a residual descriptor making continuation costs identical up to a prefix-dependent constant.
assumptions_latex: All decision domains are finite.
The objective \(c\) is real-valued on feasible complete sequences.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Equal residual-objective descriptors permit cost-preserving subdiagram sharing after an additive path-cost adjustment.

notation.meaning: Additive cost offset between two prefixes.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The content kind and local topic fit, but the additive-offset convention and resulting cost-preserving subdiagram sharing require an authoritative weighted-decision-diagram source.

children.title: Coupled State Components
children.top_down_role: Interactions among resource, feasibility, plus objective state information.

knowledge_statements.title: Coupled State Components
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Joint coordinates required when feasibility, resources, and costs interact.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P_i\) be the reachable prefixes at layer \(i\). A coupled state component is a map \(z_i:P_i\to Z_i\) summarizing two or more interacting aspects of a prefix, with a recursive update \(z_i(p)=H_i(z_{i-1}(p^-),x_i)\), such that no Cartesian factorization \(Z_i=Z_i^{(1)}\times Z_i^{(2)}\) into independently updateable summaries preserves both the residual feasible language and all continuation-objective differences. The component is exact when \(z_i(p)=z_i(q)\) implies that \(p\) and \(q\) have identical feasible suffixes and identical suffix-dependent objective increments, possibly after a prefix-only additive offset.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A coupled component jointly stores interacting information that cannot be separated while preserving feasibility and continuation costs.
assumptions_latex: The problem has ordered finite-domain decisions.
Residual feasibility and continuation-objective increments are defined for every reachable prefix.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Equality of exact coupled states permits feasibility- and objective-preserving node merging.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The proposed irreducible nonfactorization requirement is stronger than the ordinary notion of a joint state component and lacks authoritative support. A source is needed to determine the intended mathematical definition.

children.title: Exact Compilation Paradigms
children.top_down_role: Construction routes that preserve the represented solution space.

top_down_textbook_witnesses.source: Decision Diagrams for Discrete Optimization: A Survey of Recent Advances
top_down_textbook_witnesses.locator: Recursive models and exact decision diagrams
top_down_textbook_witnesses.source_title: Decision Diagrams for Discrete Optimization: A Survey of Recent Advances

knowledge_statements.title: Top-Down State-Space Compilation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact forward compilation of a layered decision diagram from recursive states.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input finite domains \(D_1,\ldots,D_n\), finite state spaces \(S_0,\ldots,S_n\), an initial state \(s_0\in S_0\), transition maps \(T_i:S_{i-1}\times D_i\to S_i\cup\{\bot\}\), arc-cost maps \(w_i:S_{i-1}\times D_i\to\mathbb{R}\), and a set \(A\subseteq S_n\) of accepting states. Initialize \(L_0=\{s_0\}\). For \(i=1,\ldots,n\), for every \(s\in L_{i-1}\) and \(a\in D_i\), compute \(s'=T_i(s,a)\); if \(s'\ne\bot\), insert \(s'\) into \(L_i\) and add an arc from \(s\) to \(s'\), labeled \(a\), with cost \(w_i(s,a)\). Merge equal states within each layer. Retain the states in \(L_n\cap A\) as accepting terminals, delete nodes not lying on a root-to-accepting path, and output the resulting layered diagram.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Expand recursive states layer by layer, omit infeasible transitions, merge equal states, retain the designated accepting states, and prune nodes outside accepting paths.
assumptions_latex: Each domain \(D_i\) and state space \(S_i\) is finite.
The state is sufficient for future feasibility and objective increments.
For every reachable \(s\in S_{i-1}\) and \(a\in D_i\), \(T_i(s,a)=\bot\) exactly when choosing \(a\) cannot begin any feasible completion from \(s\).
A complete decision sequence is feasible exactly when its transitions avoid \(\bot\) and its final state lies in \(A\).
The sum of the arc costs \(w_i\) along a feasible path equals the objective value of its decision sequence.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output root-to-accepting paths encode exactly the feasible sequences, with path costs equal to their objective values.

notation.meaning: Compiled node set at layer i.
Set of accepting states in the final layer.
Arc-cost map for decisions at layer i.

children.title: Separation-Based Compilation
children.top_down_role: Compilation driven by detected representational conflicts or violated distinctions.

knowledge_statements.title: Separation-Based Compilation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact compilation by separating spurious paths from a relaxed diagram.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a layered diagram \(G_0\) whose path language contains the target language \(F\), and a separation oracle. At iteration \(k\), optimize over root-to-terminal paths of \(G_k\). If the selected path \(x^k\) belongs to \(F\), record it; otherwise the oracle returns a valid separator \(C_k\) satisfied by every member of \(F\) but violated by \(x^k\). Compile \(C_k\) into the diagram by augmenting or splitting states so that all paths violating \(C_k\) are removed, producing \(G_{k+1}\). Stop when every remaining path is certified feasible, or when the optimization-specific stopping test certifies that no unexamined spurious path can improve the incumbent.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeatedly find a spurious diagram path, separate it by a valid constraint, and compile that separator into the diagram.
assumptions_latex: The initial diagram language contains \(F\).
Every returned separator is valid for all of \(F\).
Separator compilation never removes a path in \(F\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Upon exhaustive certification, the terminal diagram has path language exactly \(F\).

notation.meaning: Valid separator returned at iteration k.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithmic role fits the leaf, but no source supports the asserted separator-to-diagram compilation procedure, preservation invariant, or optimization-specific stopping alternative.

children.title: Refinement-Based Compilation
children.top_down_role: Progressive strengthening of an initially coarse diagram representation.

knowledge_statements.title: Refinement-Based Compilation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact compilation through monotone splitting of coarse diagram states.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a layered diagram \(G_0\) obtained by mapping exact prefix states into finitely many coarse blocks. At iteration \(k\), choose a block containing prefixes with unequal residual feasible languages or unequal continuation-cost functions. Select a distinguishing predicate \(P_k\) and replace the block by nonempty subblocks determined by \(P_k\), redirecting each incoming and outgoing arc according to its exact transition. Preserve all feasible root-to-terminal paths and their costs. Repeat until every block is homogeneous: any two prefixes in it have identical feasible suffixes and continuation costs up to an allowed prefix offset. Delete spurious and unreachable arcs, then output the refined diagram.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Split coarse state blocks using distinguishing predicates until every block has uniform feasible continuations and continuation costs.
assumptions_latex: The exact reachable prefix-state set is finite.
Each refinement strictly splits at least one non-singleton block.
Arc redirection is computed from exact state transitions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: At termination, quotienting each homogeneous block to one node yields an exact decision diagram.

notation.meaning: Predicate distinguishing states in the selected block.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm fits the refinement leaf and its finite-state assumptions are explicit, but the exact block-refinement and arc-redirection construction has no cited support.

children.title: Separation-Guided Refinement
children.top_down_role: Refinement choices prioritized by separation outcomes.

knowledge_statements.title: Separation-Guided Refinement
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Refinement rule driven by certificates separating spurious from feasible paths.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a relaxed layered diagram \(G_0\), a target language \(F\subseteq D_1\times\cdots\times D_n\), reachable-prefix sets \(Q_i\subseteq D_1\times\cdots\times D_i\), and an oracle that, for any spurious path \(x\notin F\), identifies a layer \(i\) and returns a predicate \(P:Q_i\to\{0,1\}\) that distinguishes the length-\(i\) prefix of \(x\) from a currently merged prefix having different residual behavior. At iteration \(k\), select a spurious path \(x^k\) in \(G_k\), obtain \(i_k\) and \(P_k:Q_{i_k}\to\{0,1\}\), and split each ambiguous node at layer \(i_k\) according to the value of \(P_k\) on its represented prefixes. Recompute incident arcs from the underlying exact transitions and retain all paths in \(F\). Continue until no spurious path remains; output the refined diagram and the sequence of separating predicates.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For each spurious path, use an oracle predicate on prefixes at a specified layer to split ambiguous states, preserving feasible paths until the diagram becomes exact.
assumptions_latex: The initial path language contains \(F\).
Every oracle predicate \(P_k\) strictly separates at least one currently merged pair of prefixes with different residual behavior.
Refinement and arc reconstruction preserve every path in \(F\).
A spurious path can be detected whenever the current diagram language strictly contains \(F\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If the procedure terminates with no spurious path, the output path language equals \(F\).

notation.meaning: Spurious path selected at iteration k.
Oracle predicate on prefixes at layer i_k guiding the kth refinement.
Set of reachable prefixes of length i.

children.title: Compilation Termination Regimes
children.top_down_role: Exactness, resource, or stabilization criteria governing compilation completion.

knowledge_statements.title: Compilation Termination Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sufficient finite-termination conditions for monotone exact diagram refinement.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider diagrams \(G_0,G_1,\ldots\) whose nodes represent partitions of a finite exact state set \(S=\bigcup_{i=0}^n S_i\). A refinement compilation is in the strict finite regime when each nonterminal iteration splits at least one current block, never merges previously separated exact states, and preserves all target paths. Because a partition of \(S\) can undergo at most \(|S|-b_0\) strict block-increasing refinements, where \(b_0\) is the initial number of blocks, the process terminates after at most \(|S|-b_0\) iterations. If \(S\) is infinite, or refinements need not increase the partition strictly, finite termination is not implied without an additional well-founded progress measure.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Strict monotone splitting of a finite exact state set terminates; infinite states or non-strict updates require another progress measure.
assumptions_latex: \(S\) is finite in the finite regime.
Each unfinished iteration strictly increases the number of partition blocks.
No refinement removes a target path.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The finite regime terminates within \(|S|-b_0\) strict refinement iterations; outside it, this bound does not apply.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition role fits the termination-regimes leaf, and the finite partition bound is mathematically plausible, but no source supports its application to this compilation model.

knowledge_statements.title: Problem-Specific Recursive Compilation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact compilation from a problem-derived recursive state formulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input ordered variables \(x_i\in D_i\), a problem-specific state \(s_i\), initial state \(s_0\), transition functions \(s_i=T_i(s_{i-1},x_i)\), feasibility tests \(A_i(s_{i-1},x_i)\), and incremental costs \(w_i(s_{i-1},x_i)\). Starting at \(s_0\), recursively enumerate every decision \(a\in D_i\) satisfying \(A_i(s,a)\), create an arc labeled \(a\) with cost \(w_i(s,a)\) to \(T_i(s,a)\), and memoize the subproblem keyed by \((i,T_i(s,a))\). Accept a terminal state exactly when the complete assignment is feasible. Return the memoized directed acyclic graph after deleting states that cannot reach an accepting terminal.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Recursively expand problem-specific states and memoize equal residual subproblems to obtain an exact layered diagram.
assumptions_latex: Every domain \(D_i\) is finite.
The state and feasibility tests determine exactly which suffixes are feasible.
Incremental arc costs sum to the complete objective value.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The returned paths are in bijection with feasible assignments and preserve their objective values.

notation.meaning: Admissibility predicate for the next decision.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm fits the topic and its hypotheses are largely sufficient, but no decision-diagram source supports the stated memoized compilation construction and exactness conclusion.

children.title: Diagram Redundancy Elimination
children.top_down_role: Interleaved and post-compilation mechanisms for eliminating representational redundancy.

children.title: Equivalent-Node Reduction
children.top_down_role: Consolidation of nodes with indistinguishable continuation structure.

knowledge_statements.title: Equivalent-Node Reduction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Layerwise quotienting by equality of residual path behavior.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a rooted layered decision diagram \(G\). For nodes \(u,v\) in the same layer, declare \(u\equiv v\) when their labeled, costed residual path sets to accepting terminals are identical. For each equivalence class, retain one representative \(r\), redirect every incoming arc of each removed node to \(r\), and delete duplicate arcs. When accumulated prefix offsets are stored separately, equality may be tested after a common normalization of residual costs. Process classes without combining different layers, then remove unreachable nodes. Output the quotient diagram \(G/{\equiv}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Merge same-layer nodes having identical labeled and costed continuations, redirect incoming arcs, and remove duplicates.
assumptions_latex: The diagram is acyclic and layered.
Only nodes with identical acceptance behavior are compared.
Arc-cost normalization preserves every complete path cost.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The quotient \(G/{\equiv}\) represents the same feasible sequences with the same objective values as \(G\).

notation.meaning: Equality of residual labeled, costed path behavior.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm fits equivalent-node reduction, but the weighted residual-path equivalence and normalization convention require a specific authoritative source.

children.title: Isomorphic-Subgraph Reduction
children.top_down_role: Sharing or consolidation of structurally matching descendant subgraphs.

knowledge_statements.title: Isomorphic-Subgraph Reduction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bottom-up sharing of identical rooted continuation subgraphs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Input a finite acyclic decision diagram with labeled, weighted arcs and marked terminal types. Process nodes in reverse topological order. Assign each terminal a signature determined by its terminal type. For every nonterminal node \(u\), form the canonical signature
\[
\sigma(u)=\operatorname{sort}\{(a,w(u,v),\sigma(v)):(u,v)\text{ is an outgoing arc labeled }a\}.
\]
Whenever two nodes in the same admissible layer have equal signatures, retain one representative, redirect all incoming arcs of the other to it, and delete the duplicate node. Continue until every signature class has one representative, and output the shared directed acyclic graph.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Compute bottom-up canonical signatures and merge nodes whose rooted labeled, weighted continuation subgraphs are isomorphic.
assumptions_latex: The input diagram is finite and acyclic.
Arc labels, arc weights, and terminal types are part of the isomorphism.
Merging is restricted to layers allowed by the decision ordering.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The reduced diagram preserves all labeled root-to-terminal paths and their weights while sharing every detected isomorphic continuation subgraph.

notation.meaning: Canonical signature of the subgraph rooted at u.
Weight of arc from u to v.
Decision label on an outgoing arc.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The bottom-up signature algorithm fits isomorphic-subgraph reduction and is formally coherent, but no cited source supports this labeled, weighted decision-diagram version.

children.title: Local Equivalence Detection
children.top_down_role: Detection regimes for equivalent nodes within compatible layers.

assumptions_latex: The diagram is a finite, rooted, deterministic, layered decision DAG with a fixed variable order.
Every node denotes the set or value function of its root-to-terminal completions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Replacing one node by the other preserves the function represented by the root.

notation.meaning: Label and ordered outgoing-arc signature of \(u\).

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: In an ordered deterministic decision DAG, equality of terminal labels or of labeled successor signatures is the standard local test for residual-function equivalence.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bottom-up equivalence test for deterministic ordered decision diagrams.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For nodes \(u\) and \(v\) in the same layer, define local equivalence recursively. If both are terminals, then \(u\equiv v\) exactly when their terminal values coincide. If both are nonterminals, then \(u\equiv v\) exactly when they test the same variable and, for every admissible decision label \(a\), their \(a\)-arcs have equal weights, when weights are present, and lead to equivalent successors. Thus \(\sigma(u)=\sigma(v)\) implies \(F_u=F_v\). Consequently, redirecting every incoming arc of either node to the other does not change the root residual function.
