children.title: Restricted Decision Diagrams
children.top_down_role: Under-approximating diagrams produced through path, node, or arc retention.

children.title: Node Discarding
children.top_down_role: Removal of selected states from a restricted diagram.

knowledge_statements.title: Node Discarding
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Width reduction by deleting selected nodes from a restricted decision diagram.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a finite layered decision diagram \(D=(V,A)\) and, for each layer \(i\), a retained node set \(K_i\subseteq V_i\). Delete every node in \(V_i\setminus K_i\) together with all incident arcs. Repeatedly delete nonterminal nodes unreachable from the root or unable to reach the terminal. Output the induced surviving diagram \(D'\). Every root-to-terminal path of \(D'\) was a path of \(D\), so \(\mathcal{X}(D')\subseteq\mathcal{X}(D)\). If \(|K_i|\le W\) for every layer, the output width is at most \(W\), but discarded nodes may remove feasible solutions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Delete unretained nodes and unusable remnants; the resulting diagram has only original paths but may lose feasible solutions.
assumptions_latex: \(D\) is finite, layered, and acyclic.
The root and terminal are retained.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal{X}(D')\subseteq\mathcal{X}(D)\) and \(\max_i|V_i(D')|\le W\) when \(|K_i|\le W\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind and subdiagram-containment statement fit node discarding, but no inspectable source is provided for this restricted-decision-diagram construction and its terminology.

children.title: Arc Discarding
children.top_down_role: Removal of selected transitions from a restricted diagram.

knowledge_statements.title: Arc Discarding
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Restricted-diagram construction by deleting selected transitions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a finite layered decision diagram \(D=(V,A)\) and a retained arc set \(B\subseteq A\). Form \(D_B=(V,B)\), then remove every nonterminal node that is unreachable from the root or cannot reach the terminal, together with its incident arcs. Output the surviving diagram \(D'\). Since no new arc is introduced, every root-to-terminal path in \(D'\) is a path in \(D\), and therefore \(\mathcal{X}(D')\subseteq\mathcal{X}(D)\). A feasible assignment is preserved whenever at least one of its representing paths uses only arcs in \(B\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Keep selected arcs and prune unusable nodes; all surviving paths are original, while solutions lacking a fully retained path are lost.
assumptions_latex: \(D\) is finite, layered, and acyclic.
Arc labels determine the represented decision sequence.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal{X}(D')\subseteq\mathcal{X}(D)\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits arc discarding, and the graph-containment claim is coherent. An inspectable decision-diagram source is still required.

children.title: Coordinated Structural Discarding
children.top_down_role: Coupled node-level plus arc-level pruning policies.

knowledge_statements.title: Coordinated Structural Discarding
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Joint node-and-arc selection under incidence, reachability, and width constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a layered diagram \(D=(V,A)\), width limit \(W\), and retention scores. Select sets \(K\subseteq V\) and \(B\subseteq A\) jointly so that every arc in \(B\) has both endpoints in \(K\), the root and terminal belong to \(K\), and \(|K\cap V_i|\le W\) for every layer. Form the subgraph \(D'=(K,B)\), then remove nodes and arcs not belonging to any root-to-terminal path. The output is a restricted diagram because it introduces no structure absent from \(D\); coordinated selection avoids retaining nodes whose connecting arcs were discarded.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Choose nodes and arcs jointly, respecting incidence and width, then retain only structure lying on a surviving complete path.
assumptions_latex: \(D\) is finite, layered, and acyclic.
The selected subgraph contains at least one root-to-terminal path.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal{X}(D')\subseteq\mathcal{X}(D)\) and \(\max_i|K\cap V_i|\le W\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits the container, but no source supports this coordinated policy. The retention scores are inputs yet no objective or selection rule using them is specified, so the algorithm does not uniquely determine K and B.

children.title: Feasibility-Loss Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Discarding choices that eliminate high-quality or all feasible root-to-terminal paths.

knowledge_statements.title: Feasibility-Loss Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact path-hitting condition for loss caused by structural discarding.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D'\) be obtained from \(D\) by deleting a structural set \(H\subseteq V\cup A\), and let \(\mathcal{P}_x(D)\) be all root-to-terminal paths of \(D\) representing feasible assignment \(x\). Then \(x\) is absent from \(D'\) exactly when every representing path is hit by the deletion: \(x\notin\mathcal{X}(D')\) if and only if \(p\cap H\ne\varnothing\) for every \(p\in\mathcal{P}_x(D)\). Consequently, deleting a node or arc causes feasibility loss only when the deleted structure intersects all alternative representations of at least one feasible assignment.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible assignment is lost exactly when the discarded nodes and arcs hit every path representing that assignment.
assumptions_latex: \(D'\) is obtained solely by deleting nodes or arcs from \(D\).
\(x\in\mathcal{X}(D)\) is feasible.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x\notin\mathcal{X}(D')\iff(\forall p\in\mathcal{P}_x(D))\;p\cap H\ne\varnothing\).

notation.meaning: paths in D representing assignment x

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary kind fits the leaf and the path-hitting characterization is plausible. A source is needed, and the record should clarify that each path is identified with its incident vertices and arcs so that intersection with H subseteq V union A is well-defined.

children.title: Path-Retention Policies
children.top_down_role: Policies determining which partial or complete paths remain represented.

knowledge_statements.title: Path-Retention Policies
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Restricted-diagram construction retaining a prescribed number of ranked complete paths.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a finite acyclic decision diagram \(D\), a path-ranking functional \(r\), and an integer budget \(K\ge1\). Enumerate or generate root-to-terminal paths in nonincreasing order of \(r\), choose the first \(K\) distinct paths, and retain every arc and endpoint appearing on a chosen path. Delete all other arcs and then prune nodes outside every surviving root-to-terminal path. Output the resulting subdiagram \(D_K\). Each selected path remains represented, and every path of \(D_K\) uses only original arcs, although shared nodes may permit additional recombinations of retained path segments.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Retain arcs belonging to the top-ranked complete paths and prune the rest; selected paths survive, with possible recombinations through shared nodes.
assumptions_latex: \(D\) is finite and acyclic.
At least \(K\) distinct root-to-terminal paths exist.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\{p_1,\ldots,p_K\}\subseteq\mathcal{P}(D_K)\subseteq\mathcal{P}(D)\).

notation.meaning: subdiagram induced by retained path arcs

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits the terminal container. The subgraph and recombination statements are coherent, but no inspectable source supports this ranked complete-path retention policy as a decision-diagram method.

children.title: Path Ranking Policies
children.top_down_role: Priority criteria for comparing paths under limited width.

knowledge_statements.title: Path Ranking Policies
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Ordering rule for candidate root-to-terminal paths.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal{P}(D)\) be the root-to-terminal paths of a finite decision diagram. A path-ranking policy is a map \(r:\mathcal{P}(D)\to\mathbb{R}\), together with a fixed tie-breaking rule, inducing the total preorder \(p\succeq_r q\) exactly when \(r(p)\ge r(q)\). The score may combine accumulated arc value, admissible completion estimates, or structural penalties, but these components and their scaling must be fixed before selection. A top-\(K\) policy retains paths occupying the first \(K\) positions of the resulting order.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A path-ranking policy assigns each complete diagram path a score and fixed tie-breaker, thereby defining which paths are retained first.
assumptions_latex: \(D\) is finite and has at least one root-to-terminal path.
The tie-breaking rule is deterministic.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(r\) and its tie-breaker determine an ordered list of \(\mathcal{P}(D)\).

notation.meaning: ranking score assigned to path p
preference relation induced by the score

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition kind fits the leaf, but no source is supplied. The score induces a total preorder, whereas adding a deterministic tie-breaker induces a total order; the record currently conflates these two structures.

children.title: Diversity-Aware Retention
children.top_down_role: Retention policies balancing path quality against structural or state diversity.

knowledge_statements.title: Diversity-Aware Retention
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Greedy path retention balancing rank quality and dissimilarity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input candidate paths \(P\), normalized quality \(q:P\to[0,1]\), normalized distance \(d:P\times P\to[0,1]\), budget \(K\), and \(\lambda\in[0,1]\). Initialize \(S\) with a maximizer of \(q\). While \(|S|<K\), add a path maximizing \(\lambda q(p)+(1-\lambda)\min_{s\in S}d(p,s)\) over \(p\in P\setminus S\), using a fixed tie-breaker. Return \(S\) and the subdiagram induced by its arcs. The rule favors high-ranked paths while penalizing redundancy; \(\lambda=1\) reduces to quality-only greedy retention.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Greedily retain paths using a weighted combination of path quality and distance from the paths already selected.
assumptions_latex: \(P\) is finite and \(1\le K\le|P|\).
\(q\) and \(d\) are normalized to \([0,1]\).
Ties are resolved deterministically.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(|S|=K\), with each addition maximizing the stated quality-diversity score.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits diversity-aware retention and the finite greedy rule is internally executable. No inspectable source establishes this particular quality-diversity formula or its use for restricted decision diagrams.

children.title: Ranking Bias Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Ranking choices that systematically discard promising feasible regions.

assumptions_latex: The instance class consists of finite minimization problems with nonnegative path costs and strictly positive optimal value.
Lower values of the retention score are preferred, and the score is not required to satisfy a valid dominance rule or an admissible completion bound.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sup z_R/z^*=+\infty\) over this instance class.

notation.meaning: best cost represented by the width-one restricted diagram
strictly positive optimal cost in the exact diagram

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Worst-case limitation of unconstrained score-only retention in width-restricted decision diagrams.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider score-only width-one retention for finite minimization problems with strictly positive optimum, where a smaller score \(r\) is preferred. Without any dominance or admissible-completion requirement on \(r\), no finite worst-case approximation ratio is guaranteed: for every \(M>1\), there can be two prefixes \(p\) and \(q\) with \(r(p)<r(q)\), such that every completion of \(p\) has cost at least \(M\), while \(q\) has a feasible completion of cost \(1\). Retaining only \(p\) can therefore produce \(z_R\ge M\) when \(z^*=1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For every target factor, an unconstrained score-only width-one policy can prefer a prefix whose best completion is that factor worse than the discarded optimal prefix.
knowledge_statements.title: Ranking Bias Boundaries
Restricted-Diagram Feasibility Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Path-based primal certificate for a restricted decision diagram.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D_R\) be a layered restricted decision diagram obtained only by deleting exact states or arcs, so every root-to-terminal path remains an exact feasible path. A root-to-terminal path \(P=(a_1,\ldots,a_n)\) certifies the assignment \(x(P)=(\ell(a_1),\ldots,\ell(a_n))\). Verification consists of checking arc incidence, the root and terminal endpoints, and the original constraints at \(x(P)\). If arc costs decompose the objective, also check \(f(x(P))=\sum_{i=1}^n c(a_i)\). These checks certify feasibility and the reported primal value, but not global optimality for the original problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Any root-to-terminal path in a deletion-only restricted diagram gives a directly checkable feasible assignment and primal objective value.
assumptions_latex: Restriction introduces no new state, arc, or transition.
Arc labels encode complete assignments and arc costs encode the objective.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: P\in\mathcal P(D_R)\Longrightarrow x(P)\in X\text{ and }f(x(P))=\sum_{a\in P}c(a).

notation.meaning: root-to-terminal paths of the restricted diagram

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The certificate role and deletion-only feasibility claim are coherent, including the limitation that the path does not certify global optimality. No cited source supports the decision-diagram path semantics or verification conditions.

children.title: Approximate Diagram Construction Calculus
children.top_down_role: Construction and strengthening families shared by relaxed and restricted diagrams.

top_down_textbook_witnesses.source: Decision Diagrams for Discrete Optimization: A Survey of Recent Advances
top_down_textbook_witnesses.locator: Approximate DD Compilation: top-down and iterative refinement
top_down_textbook_witnesses.source_title: Decision Diagrams for Discrete Optimization: A Survey of Recent Advances

knowledge_statements.title: Width-Limited Top-Down Compilation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Layerwise compilation under a prescribed maximum width.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given variable order \((x_1,\ldots,x_n)\), root state \(s_0\), transition map \(T_i\), and width limit \(W\), initialize \(L_0=\{s_0\}\). For \(i=1,\ldots,n\), expand every admissible transition \(s'=T_i(s,v)\) from \(s\in L_{i-1}\), creating labeled arcs and the provisional layer \(\widehat L_i\). If \(|\widehat L_i|>W\), apply a compilation operator \(C_i\) producing \(L_i=C_i(\widehat L_i)\) with \(|L_i|\le W\), and redirect or delete arcs consistently. Remove states that cannot reach a terminal. Output the resulting layered diagram after layer \(n\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Compile layers in variable order, expanding valid transitions and applying a restriction or relaxation operator whenever provisional width exceeds the limit.
assumptions_latex: Each transition map determines the next state and admissibility.
Each operator preserves the intended restricted- or relaxed-diagram invariant.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \max_{0\le i\le n}|L_i|\le W.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind matches the leaf and the width conclusion follows from the stated operator contract. A decision-diagram source is needed for the top-down construction and the distinct validity requirements on restriction versus relaxation operators.

assumptions_latex: For every \(k\), the restricted diagram represents a subset of the original feasible set and the relaxed diagram represents a superset of it.
The represented sets are nested as \(X_R^k\subseteq X_R^{k+1}\subseteq X\subseteq X_L^{k+1}\subseteq X_L^k\).
Path problems on all intermediate diagrams are solved exactly with objective-consistent costs.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(z_L^k\le z_L^{k+1}\le z^*\le z_R^{k+1}\le z_R^k\).

notation.meaning: restricted and relaxed diagrams after k refinement iterations
relaxed-diagram lower bound at iteration k
restricted-diagram upper bound at iteration k

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nested improvement of paired restricted and relaxed diagrams and their optimization bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Start with a restricted diagram \(D_R^0\) and a relaxed diagram \(D_L^0\). At iteration \(k\), solve their path problems, select an inexact state, arc, or aggregate exposed by a current solution, and refine while preserving nested represented sets \(X_R^k\subseteq X_R^{k+1}\subseteq X\subseteq X_L^{k+1}\subseteq X_L^k\). For minimization with objective-consistent path costs, the resulting bounds satisfy \(z_L^k\le z_L^{k+1}\le z^*\le z_R^{k+1}\le z_R^k\). Stop at exactness of the relevant solution, equality of the bounds, or a resource limit, and return the best feasible path and valid lower bound found.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeatedly enlarge the restricted represented set and tighten the relaxed represented set while preserving validity; their upper and lower bounds then improve monotonically until exactness, bound closure, or a resource limit.
knowledge_statements.title: Iterative Refinement

children.title: State Splitting
children.top_down_role: Replacement of coarse states by more discriminating state partitions.

assumptions_latex: Each aggregate node has a defined set of represented exact partial states.
Transition compatibility can be determined for every partition class.
Arc redistribution preserves the approximation invariant required of the diagram.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(S(u)=\mathbin{\dot\bigcup}_{j=1}^m S(u_j)\), with the applicable exact, restricted, or relaxed validity invariant preserved.

notation.meaning: exact partial states represented by node u
child aggregate created by the split

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Refinement of an aggregated decision-diagram state into distinguishable subclasses.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a layer node \(u\) represent a set \(S(u)\) of exact partial states. A state split replaces \(u\) by nodes \(u_1,\ldots,u_m\), where \(m\ge2\) and \(S(u)=S(u_1)\mathbin{\dot\cup}\cdots\mathbin{\dot\cup}S(u_m)\), and redistributes incoming and outgoing arcs according to transition compatibility with the partition classes. The split is valid when it preserves the diagram's required invariant: equality with \(X\) for an exact diagram, inclusion in \(X\) for a restricted diagram, or containment of \(X\) for a relaxed diagram. A relaxed-diagram split is strict when it removes at least one previously represented spurious prefix-suffix combination.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: State splitting partitions the exact partial states represented by an aggregate node and redistributes compatible arcs while preserving the diagram's exact, restricted, or relaxed validity invariant.
knowledge_statements.title: State Splitting

children.title: Separation-Driven Refinement
children.top_down_role: Diagram strengthening guided by detected conflicts or violated distinctions.

knowledge_statements.title: Separation-Driven Refinement
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Refinement triggered by a separating inequality violated by an approximate path.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a relaxed diagram \(D^k\), solve its minimum-cost path problem and decode a candidate \(\bar x^k\). If \(\bar x^k\in X\), return it with the current bound. Otherwise, call a separation oracle to obtain an inequality \(a^\top x\le b\) valid for every \(x\in X\) but violated by \(\bar x^k\). Refine states or arcs so accumulated information sufficient to enforce this inequality is distinguished, producing \(D^{k+1}\) with \(X\subseteq\mathcal X(D^{k+1})\subsetneq\mathcal X(D^k)\) and \(\bar x^k\notin\mathcal X(D^{k+1})\). Repeat until feasibility, bound closure, or a resource limit.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Separate an infeasible relaxed path, refine the diagram to enforce the separator, and repeat while preserving all truly feasible assignments.
assumptions_latex: A separation oracle returns an inequality valid for the original feasible set.
The refinement can encode enough separator information without deleting feasible assignments.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: X\subseteq\mathcal X(D^{k+1})\subsetneq\mathcal X(D^k)\text{ and }\bar x^k\notin\mathcal X(D^{k+1}).

notation.meaning: candidate decoded from the current optimal path

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm role fits and the strict containment conclusion follows only under the strong stated assumption that the separator can be encoded without deleting feasible assignments. A source with a specific decision-diagram refinement locator is required to support that construction.

children.title: Separation-Guided State Splits
children.top_down_role: Selection of state partitions using separation information.

assumptions_latex: The separator decomposes across the diagram variable order.
Aggregate nodes identify their represented prefixes or retain sufficient partial-activity information.
Every split redistributes arcs so that no member of the original feasible set is deleted.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If the performed splits eliminate the offending combination, then \(\bar x\notin\mathcal X(D')\) and \(X\subseteq\mathcal X(D')\); exhaustion of the width budget need not eliminate \(\bar x\).

notation.meaning: separator activity accumulated by prefix p through layer t
diagram after the performed guided splits

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Choosing state partitions from the residual information of a violated separator.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(a^\top x\le b\) separate a relaxed path \(\bar x\) from the feasible set, and let an aggregate node \(u\) at layer \(t\) contain prefixes with partial activities \(\alpha_t(p)=\sum_{i=1}^{t}a_i p_i\). Choose a threshold \(\tau\) that places the offending prefix and at least one other represented prefix in different classes. Split \(u\) into nodes representing \(\alpha_t(p)\le\tau\) and \(\alpha_t(p)>\tau\), redistribute arcs by transition compatibility, and retain sufficient residual-activity information. Repeat until the offending root-to-terminal combination is absent or the width budget is exhausted. If it is eliminated, the refined diagram \(D'\) must satisfy \(\bar x\notin\mathcal X(D')\) and \(X\subseteq\mathcal X(D')\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Use partial activity of a violated inequality to split aggregate states; feasible assignments must remain represented, but elimination of the offending relaxed path is guaranteed only if enough splits are completed before the width budget is exhausted.
knowledge_statements.title: Separation-Guided State Splits

children.title: Refinement Stall Regimes
children.top_down_role: Cases where available splits provide little structural or bound improvement.

knowledge_statements.title: Refinement Stall Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditions under which valid refinement cannot improve the current diagram bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D^k\) be a relaxed diagram with optimal represented assignment \(\bar x^k\notin X\), and let \(\mathcal R_k\) be the refinements permitted by the current width, state descriptors, and separator family. Refinement stalls at iteration \(k\) when every \(R\in\mathcal R_k\) either leaves \(\bar x^k\) represented or violates validity by deleting some member of \(X\). Then no admissible refinement can raise the minimization lower bound solely by excluding \(\bar x^k\). Progress requires enlarging the width or state language, strengthening separation, changing the variable order, or accepting a nonmonotone reconstruction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Refinement stalls when every permitted valid operation either retains the offending relaxed path or deletes a truly feasible assignment.
assumptions_latex: The current relaxed path is infeasible for the original problem.
Only refinements in the specified admissible family may be used.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \bigl(\forall R\in\mathcal R_k:\ \bar x^k\in\mathcal X(R(D^k))\ \lor\ X\nsubseteq\mathcal X(R(D^k))\bigr)\Longrightarrow\text{no admissible exclusion refinement exists}.

notation.meaning: admissible refinement operations at iteration k

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary kind fits, and the formal conclusion is essentially the definition of nonexistence of a permitted valid exclusion refinement. A source is needed to establish this as a recognized decision-diagram stall regime and to support the listed remedies.

knowledge_statements.title: Peeling-Based Refinement
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local refinement obtained by extracting a selected path or subgraph from aggregated states.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given an approximate layered diagram \(D\) and a selected root-to-terminal path \(P\), process the internal nodes of \(P\) in layer order. Whenever a path node aggregates states also used by paths outside \(P\), create a copy representing the selected predecessor-transition class, redirect the corresponding path arcs to the copy, and retain the complementary states in the original node. Recompute compatible outgoing arcs for both nodes and prune unreachable nodes. Continue until \(P\) is represented by exact transition classes or a width limit is reached. Output the peeled diagram \(D'\), preserving the chosen restricted or relaxed validity invariant.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Peeling isolates states along a selected path from shared aggregates, redirects compatible arcs, and thereby refines the diagram locally.
assumptions_latex: Node copying and arc redistribution can be performed by exact transition compatibility.
Each split preserves the chosen approximation invariant.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathcal X(D')\text{ preserves the required approximation of }X\text{ and distinguishes the processed classes along }P.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits, but the asserted meaning of peeling, its node-copying mechanics, and preservation of either approximation invariant are domain-specific and cannot be validated from the supplied inventory.

children.title: Primal-Dual Diagram Pair
children.top_down_role: Coordinated approximation families providing dual bounds, feasible solutions, and search guidance.

top_down_textbook_witnesses.locator: Relaxed BDD bounds and restricted BDD primal heuristic

knowledge_statements.title: Primal–Dual Diagram Pairing
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Paired restricted and relaxed diagrams for primal and dual bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a finite minimization problem \(z^*=\min\{f(x):x\in X\}\), let a restricted diagram \(D_R\) represent \(X_R\subseteq X\), and let a relaxed diagram \(D_L\) represent \(X\subseteq X_L\). Assume path costs equal \(f\) on represented assignments. Define \(z_R=\min_{x\in X_R}f(x)\) and \(z_L=\min_{x\in X_L}f(x)\), with \(z_R=+\infty\) if \(X_R=\varnothing\). Then \(z_L\le z^*\le z_R\). A feasible path attaining \(z_R\) is a primal certificate, and the relaxed path optimum supplies the paired dual bound; equality certifies optimality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A restricted diagram gives an upper bound and feasible solution, while a relaxed diagram gives a lower bound; equality certifies optimality.
assumptions_latex: The original problem is finite and is a minimization problem.
Both diagrams use objective-consistent path costs.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: z_L\le z^*\le z_R\text{, and }z_L=z_R\Longrightarrow z_L=z^*=z_R.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The duality kind matches the pairing leaf, and the set inclusions correctly imply the stated minimization bounds. No source supports the decision-diagram pairing terminology or its certificate interpretation.

children.title: Shared Width Policies
children.top_down_role: Coordinated width limits across paired approximation diagrams.

knowledge_statements.title: Shared Width Policies
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Common per-layer width constraint for a primal–dual diagram pair.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D_R\) and \(D_L\) be paired restricted and relaxed diagrams with layer sets \(L_i^R\) and \(L_i^L\). A shared-width policy with limit \(W\in\mathbb N\) requires both diagrams to obey the same layerwise cap: \(\lvert L_i^R\rvert\le W\) and \(\lvert L_i^L\rvert\le W\) for every layer \(i\). When a provisional layer exceeds \(W\), the restricted compiler must delete only in a validity-preserving manner, whereas the relaxed compiler must merge or relax states without excluding an original feasible assignment. The common cap coordinates memory limits but does not require identical retained states.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Both paired diagrams obey the same layer-width cap, while each uses its own validity-preserving overflow operation.
assumptions_latex: The paired diagrams have aligned layers.
Restricted and relaxed overflow operators preserve their respective invariants.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \max_i|L_i^R|\le W\quad\text{and}\quad\max_i|L_i^L|\le W.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition kind is appropriate and the common width cap is internally consistent. A decision-diagram source is required for the shared-width policy and the respective overflow invariants.

children.title: Shared Compilation Policies
children.top_down_role: Common ordering, state, refinement, or pruning choices across the pair.

knowledge_statements.title: Shared Compilation Policies
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Synchronized construction of restricted and relaxed diagrams from common transition semantics.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given one variable order, exact transition system, restricted operator \(C_i^R\), and relaxed operator \(C_i^L\), initialize paired roots \(L_0^R=L_0^L=\{s_0\}\). At each layer \(i\), expand both current layers using the same variable and exact transition semantics. Apply \(C_i^R\) to the restricted provisional layer and \(C_i^L\) to the relaxed provisional layer, then record objective-consistent arcs. The operators may select different states but must preserve \(\mathcal X(D_R)\subseteq X\subseteq\mathcal X(D_L)\). Stop after the terminal layer and return both path optima and their gap.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Compile restricted and relaxed diagrams in synchronized layers using common transitions but separate validity-preserving width-control operators.
assumptions_latex: Both compilers use the same variable order and exact transition semantics.
The two width-control operators preserve their respective set inclusions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: z_L\le z^*\le z_R\text{ throughout compilation whenever terminal path bounds are defined}.

notation.meaning: restricted width-control operator at layer i
relaxed width-control operator at layer i

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits the terminal container, but synchronized paired compilation and preservation of both represented-set inclusions are unsupported by any cited source. The supplied local inventory does not address decision-diagram compilation.

children.title: Joint Resource Allocation
children.top_down_role: Allocation of time, memory, plus width budgets between paired diagrams.

assumptions_latex: \(D^P(w_P)\) is a restricted primal diagram whose paths encode feasible solutions.
\(D^D(w_D)\) is a relaxed dual diagram whose paths yield valid bounds.
The compilation budget \(B\) and admissible width pairs \(\mathcal W\subseteq\mathbb Z_+^2\) are given.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((w_P^*,w_D^*)\) is the admissible allocation maximizing the prescribed joint diagram-quality criterion.

notation.meaning: quality scores of the restricted and relaxed diagrams

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: finite resource allocation over paired diagram compilations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite joint allocation of a compilation budget between paired restricted and relaxed diagrams.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given positive costs \(c_P,c_D\), compile each admissible pair \((w_P,w_D)\in\mathcal W\) satisfying \(c_Pw_P+c_Dw_D\le B\). Evaluate a prescribed monotone joint score \(\Phi(Q_P(D^P(w_P)),Q_D(D^D(w_D)))\), where larger \(Q_P\) means a better incumbent and larger \(Q_D\) means a tighter valid bound under fixed sign conventions. Return \[(w_P^*,w_D^*)\in\operatorname*{argmax}_{(w_P,w_D)\in\mathcal W,\ c_Pw_P+c_Dw_D\le B}\Phi(Q_P(D^P(w_P)),Q_D(D^D(w_D))).\] Ties are resolved by a fixed deterministic rule.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Allocate a finite compilation budget between restricted and relaxed diagrams by optimizing a specified joint measure of incumbent quality and bound strength.
knowledge_statements.title: Joint Resource Allocation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The exhaustive allocation algorithm is mathematically coherent and fits the leaf, but no inspectable source supports the paired restricted/relaxed diagram model or the proposed quality criterion.

children.title: Asymmetric Pairing Regimes
children.top_down_role: Policies using different widths or compilation effort on each approximation side.

assumptions_latex: The two diagrams approximate the same layered decision model.
Widths are positive integers and may vary independently by layer.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The pair is asymmetric exactly when its primal and dual width profiles differ on at least one layer.

notation.meaning: primal and dual width profiles over layers

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: asymmetry is expressed by unequal resource or compilation policies
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Asymmetry concerns unequal width profiles within a primal-dual diagram pair.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a model with layers \(1,\ldots,n\), a paired regime \((D^P,D^D)	ext{ is asymmetric if its width profiles }w^P,w^D\in\mathbb Z_+^n	ext{ satisfy }w^P
e w^D.\) Equivalently, \(w_i^P
e w_i^D\) for at least one layer \(i\). More generally, if compilation policies \(C_P\) and \(C_D\) include distinct merging, deletion, or refinement rules, the regime is policy-asymmetric when \(C_P
e C_D\), even if the numerical width profiles coincide.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A primal-dual diagram pair is asymmetric when its width profiles or compilation policies differ on at least one corresponding layer.

children.title: Diagram Path Calculus
children.top_down_role: Graph-optimization and path-analysis families for compiled diagrams.

knowledge_statements.title: Best-Path Optimization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Additive minimum-cost path optimization on a finite acyclic decision diagram.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize \(d(s)=0\) and \(d(v)=+\infty\) for every \(v\ne s\). Process vertices in topological order and set \[d(v)=\min_{a=(u,v)\in\delta^-(v)}\{d(u)+c(a)\}.\] Store an attaining predecessor whenever \(d(v)<+\infty\). After processing \(t\), trace predecessors from \(t\) to \(s\) and return the resulting path together with \(d(t)\). For maximization, replace \(\min\) by \(\max\), initialize unreachable vertices to \(-\infty\), and otherwise use the same recurrence and reconstruction procedure.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Compute an optimal source-to-terminal diagram path by dynamic programming in topological order, then recover the path through stored predecessors.
assumptions_latex: \(D=(V,A)\) is a finite directed acyclic graph with source \(s\), terminal \(t\), and arc weights \(c:A\to\mathbb R\).
At least one directed \(s\)-\(t\) path exists.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The returned predecessor chain is an \(s\)-\(t\) path of minimum total arc weight.

notation.meaning: best cost from the source to a vertex

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: shortest-path dynamic programming on a directed acyclic graph

assumptions_latex: \(D=(V,A)\) is a finite directed acyclic graph with source \(s\), terminal \(t\), and additive arc weights.
The selected min-plus or max-plus convention is used consistently.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For every arc \(a=(u,v)\), the best complete path using \(a\) has value \(F(u)+c(a)+B(v)\).

notation.meaning: best complete-path value constrained to use an arc

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: forward-backward decomposition of additive path values
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Forward-backward decomposition for additive path values in an acyclic diagram.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Under minimization, define \(F(s)=0\) and compute \(F(v)=\min_{(u,v)	ext{ in }A}\{F(u)+c(u,v)\}\) in topological order. Define \(B(t)=0\) and compute \(B(u)=\min_{(u,v)	ext{ in }A}\{c(u,v)+B(v)\}\) in reverse topological order. Then, for every arc \(a=(u,v)\), \[M(a)=F(u)+c(a)+B(v)\] is the minimum weight of an \(s\)-\(t\) path containing \(a\), with \(M(a)=+	ext{infinity}\) when either segment is unreachable.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Forward and backward dynamic programs give the best complete path through every arc by adding its best prefix, arc weight, and best suffix.
knowledge_statements.title: Forward–Backward Path Analysis

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The forward–backward identity is correct for additive path weights, including the unreachable-segment convention. It can serve as a representation of arc-conditioned path values, but no inspectable source is supplied.

children.title: Ranked Path Families
children.top_down_role: Collections of diagram paths organized by objective value or another priority.

knowledge_statements.title: Ranked Path Families
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite path families ordered by objective value with deterministic tie breaking.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Order \(\mathcal P(D)\) by declaring that \(P\) precedes \(Q\) when \(C(P)<C(Q)\), or when \(C(P)=C(Q)\) and \(P\prec_\tau Q\) under the fixed tie-breaking order \(\prec_\tau\). If the resulting enumeration is \(P^{(1)},\ldots,P^{(m)}\), then, for \(k\in\mathbb Z_+\), define \[\mathcal P_k(D)=\{P^{(j)}:1\le j\le\min\{k,m\}\}.\] For maximization, reverse the strict comparison of path scores while retaining the same tie-breaking order.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A ranked path family consists of the first k source-to-terminal paths ordered by score and a fixed rule for resolving ties.
assumptions_latex: \(D\) is a finite directed acyclic diagram with source \(s\) and terminal \(t\).
Each source-to-terminal path \(P\) has a real-valued score \(C(P)\).
A deterministic total tie-breaking order \(\prec_\tau\) on paths is fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal P_k(D)\) contains exactly the first \(\min\{k,|\mathcal P(D)|\}\) paths in the induced total order.

notation.meaning: all source-to-terminal paths in the diagram
family of the first k ranked paths
fixed total tie-breaking order on paths

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: order-statistic definition for a finite path set

children.title: Constrained Path Families
children.top_down_role: Diagram paths subject to additional path-level restrictions.

knowledge_statements.title: Constrained Path Families
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Path families filtered by resource or side-constraint feasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The constrained path family induced by \(K\) is \[\mathcal P_K(D)=\{P\in\mathcal P(D):R(P)\in K\}.\] If resources are additive, with arc consumptions \(r(a)\in\mathbb R^q\), then \(R(P)=\sum_{a\in P}r(a)\). A common budget form is \(K=\{z\in\mathbb R^q:z\le b\}\), where the inequality is componentwise. The definition also permits nonadditive resources provided \(R(P)\) is well-defined.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A constrained path family contains precisely those diagram paths whose accumulated resource or side-constraint values satisfy the prescribed admissibility set.
assumptions_latex: \(D\) is a finite source-to-terminal decision diagram.
Each path \(P\) has a resource vector \(R(P)\in\mathbb R^q\), and admissibility is specified by a set \(K\subseteq\mathbb R^q\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The constrained family is exactly the set of diagram paths whose accumulated resource vector lies in \(K\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: constrained paths are selected by an explicit path-level feasibility predicate

children.title: Constraint-Aware Path Ranking
children.top_down_role: Ranking regimes that incorporate path feasibility or side constraints.

assumptions_latex: \(D	ext{ is a finite acyclic diagram, and }\mathcal P_K(D)\) is its constrained path family.
Each feasible path has score \(C(P)	ext{, and a deterministic tie-breaking order is fixed.}
A correct constrained-path enumeration routine is available.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output lists the first \(\min\{k,|\mathcal P_K(D)|\}\) constrained paths in nondecreasing score order.
review_flags: exact enumeration implementation depends on constraint structure
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Ranking only paths that satisfy the prescribed path-level constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize an empty output list and a constrained-path enumerator keyed lexicographically by \((C(P),	au(P))\), where \(\tau\) is the fixed tie-break rank. Repeatedly extract the least-key unreported member of \(\mathcal P_K(D)\), append it, and update the enumerator according to its correctness-preserving deviation rule. Stop after \(k\) extractions or when no feasible path remains. Return \((P^{(1)},	ext{dots},P^{(ell)})\), where \(	ext{ell}=\min\{k,|\mathcal P_K(D)|\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Enumerate only constraint-feasible paths, returning up to k of them in score order with deterministic tie resolution.
knowledge_statements.title: Constraint-Aware Path Ranking

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The proposed procedure assumes a correct constrained-path enumerator and delegates all substantive work to an unspecified correctness-preserving deviation rule. It therefore does not state an implementable algorithm for this algorithm leaf, and the missing constraint structure prevents a reliable repair.

children.title: Path-Family Feasibility Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Constraint regimes that invalidate ordinary ranked-path interpretations.

knowledge_statements.title: Path-Family Feasibility Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact nonemptiness boundary for a path family filtered by side constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The constrained family is nonempty if and only if \[R(\mathcal P(D))\cap K\ne\emptyset.\] Thus feasibility is lost exactly when the attained resource set ceases to intersect the admissible set. For a scalar upper budget \(K(b)=\{z\in\mathbb R:z\le b\}\), define \[r^*=\min_{P\in\mathcal P(D)}R(P).\] Then \(\mathcal P_{K(b)}(D)\ne\emptyset\) exactly when \(b\ge r^*\), and \(\mathcal P_{K(b)}(D)=\emptyset\) when \(b<r^*\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A constrained path family is feasible exactly when some diagram path attains a resource vector in the admissible set; scalar feasibility begins at the minimum resource value.
assumptions_latex: \(D\) is a finite source-to-terminal diagram with at least one source-to-terminal path.
\(\mathcal P_K(D)=\{P\in\mathcal P(D):R(P)\in K\}\) is the constrained path family.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The constrained family is empty exactly when \(R(\mathcal P(D))\cap K=\emptyset\).

notation.meaning: set of resource vectors attained by diagram paths

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: exact nonemptiness boundary for a predicate-filtered finite family

children.title: Diagram-Derived Bounds
children.top_down_role: Node or subproblem bounds obtained from relaxed or exact diagrams.

assumptions_latex: The problem is a minimization problem over feasible set \(X\) with objective \(f\).
A relaxed diagram \(D^R	ext{ contains every encoding of every member of }X\).
Every root-to-terminal path has a well-defined objective value consistent with its encoded decisions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L(D^R)=\min_{P\in\mathcal P(D^R)}c(P)\) is a valid lower bound on \(f^*=\min_{x\in X}f(x)\).
review_flags: locator supports general bound validity rather than decision-diagram construction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Lower bounds for minimization obtained from relaxed decision diagrams.

source_refs.locator: Chapter 7. Cuts, Lower Bounds and Box Reduction p. 83
source_refs.source_title: Relaxation and Decomposition Methods for Mixed Integer Nonlinear Programming

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(L(D^R)=\min_{P\in\mathcal P(D^R)}c(P)\). Because every feasible solution \(x\in X\) has a representing path \(P_x\in\mathcal P(D^R)\) with \(c(P_x)=f(x)\), \[L(D^R)\le f^*=\min_{x\in X}f(x).\] Thus the best-path value of the relaxed diagram is a valid lower bound. For maximization, the analogous relaxed-diagram best-path value is a valid upper bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Optimizing over a relaxed diagram gives a valid bound because its path set contains representations of every feasible solution.
knowledge_statements.title: Diagram-Derived Bounds

source_witnesses.locator: Chapter 7. Cuts, Lower Bounds and Box Reduction p. 83
source_witnesses.source_title: Relaxation and Decomposition Methods for Mixed Integer Nonlinear Programming

children.title: Diagram-Derived Incumbents
children.top_down_role: Feasible solutions obtained from restricted diagrams or represented paths.

assumptions_latex: The problem is a minimization problem over feasible set \(X\).
Every source-to-terminal path of a restricted diagram \(D^P\) decodes to a member of \(X\).
At least one source-to-terminal path exists in \(D^P\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The decoded best path supplies a feasible incumbent with value \(U(D^P)\ge f^*\).
review_flags: locator supports primal incumbents rather than their decision-diagram derivation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Feasible incumbents for minimization extracted from restricted diagrams.

source_refs.locator: 2.7 Primal Bounds: Greedy and Local Search p. 34

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Choose \(P^*	ext{ in }\operatorname*{argmin}_{P\in\mathcal P(D^P)}f(x(P))\) and set \(U(D^P)=f(x(P^*))\). Since every path of \(D^P\) decodes to a feasible solution, \(x(P^*)\in X\) and \[f^*=\min_{x\in X}f(x)\le U(D^P).\] The path, its decoded decisions, and direct verification of the original constraints form a checkable incumbent certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The best path in a restricted diagram decodes to a feasible solution and therefore provides a verifiable incumbent objective value.
knowledge_statements.title: Diagram-Derived Incumbents

source_witnesses.locator: 2.7 Primal Bounds: Greedy and Local Search p. 34

children.title: Bound–Incumbent Gap Management
children.top_down_role: Use of paired bound plus incumbent information during exact search.

knowledge_statements.title: Bound–Incumbent Gap Management
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Absolute-gap management for minimization using valid diagram-derived bounds and incumbents.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Maintain \(L\le f^*\le U\), updating \(L\) only upward when a stronger valid lower bound is found and \(U\) only downward when a better feasible incumbent is found. The absolute gap \(g=U-L\) is nonnegative. If \(g\le\varepsilon\), then \[U-\varepsilon\le L\le f^*\quad\text{and hence}\quad U-f^*\le\varepsilon.\] In particular, \(g=0\) certifies global optimality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Maintain a valid lower bound and feasible upper incumbent monotonically; an absolute gap at most epsilon certifies epsilon-optimality.
assumptions_latex: For a minimization problem, \(L\) is a valid global lower bound and \(U\) is the value of a feasible incumbent.
A tolerance \(\varepsilon\ge0\) is fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The incumbent is globally \(\varepsilon\)-optimal whenever \(U-L\le\varepsilon\).

source_refs.source_title: Relaxation and Decomposition Methods for Mixed Integer Nonlinear Programming

source_witnesses.source_title: Relaxation and Decomposition Methods for Mixed Integer Nonlinear Programming

children.title: Search-Pruning Consequences
children.top_down_role: Pruning behavior induced by diagram-bound strength plus incumbent quality.

assumptions_latex: The problem is a minimization problem with incumbent value \(U\).
A search node \(N\) represents a subproblem with a valid lower bound \(L_N\).
A tolerance \(	ext{epsilon}\ge0\) is fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(L_N\ge U-	ext{epsilon}\), pruning \(N\) cannot remove a solution improving the incumbent by more than \(	ext{epsilon}\).

notation.meaning: valid lower bound for search node N

review_flags: decision-diagram origin of the node bound is a specialization of standard branch-and-bound pruning
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Branch-and-bound pruning using diagram-derived node bounds and a feasible incumbent.

source_refs.locator: 2.2.1 Outline of the general branch-and-bound method p. 15

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Every feasible completion represented below search node \(N\) has objective value at least \(L_N\). Therefore, if \[L_N\ge U-	ext{epsilon},\] no completion below \(N\) can have value strictly less than \(U-	ext{epsilon}\), and \(N\) may be pruned under an absolute \(	ext{epsilon}\)-optimality policy. With \(	ext{epsilon}=0\), the usual exact rule \(L_N\ge U\) discards nodes unable to improve the incumbent.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A search node can be pruned when its valid diagram-derived lower bound cannot improve the incumbent beyond the chosen tolerance.
knowledge_statements.title: Search-Pruning Consequences

source_witnesses.locator: 2.2.1 Outline of the general branch-and-bound method p. 15

knowledge_statements.title: Cutset-Based Search
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact search using a frontier cutset of a layered decision diagram.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a finite minimization problem represented by a rooted layered decision diagram and an incumbent value \(U\), initialize a queue with the root subproblem. For a queued subproblem, construct a valid relaxed diagram \(D\) with lower bound \(L(D)\). Discard it when \(L(D)\ge U\). Otherwise, update \(U\) using any feasible root-to-terminal path, choose a cutset \(C\) intersecting every unresolved root-to-terminal path exactly once, and enqueue the residual subproblem rooted at each \(v\in C\). Stop when the queue is empty; return the incumbent solution and value \(U\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeatedly bound a diagram, prune it against the incumbent, and branch on a cutset covering every unresolved path; exhaustion certifies the incumbent as optimal.
assumptions_latex: The feasible set is finite, and every feasible solution induces a root-to-terminal path.
Each relaxed-diagram bound is valid for its queued subproblem.
Cutset children partition or cover every unresolved feasible solution.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Upon queue exhaustion, \(U\) equals the global minimum.

notation.meaning: relaxed decision diagram for the current subproblem

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits the exact-search leaf, but no cited source supports the decision-diagram cutset construction, the meaning of residual subproblems at cutset nodes, or the coverage conditions needed for global optimality. These details cannot be certified from generic branch-and-bound sources in the supplied inventory.

knowledge_statements.title: Diagram State-Space Branching
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Branching on diagram nodes interpreted as sets of partial assignments.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D=(V,A)\) be a layered decision diagram whose root-to-terminal paths encode assignments. For a node \(v\) in layer \(i\), define \(S(v)\) as the set of length-\(i\) label sequences on root-to-\(v\) paths and \(F(v)\) as the feasible completions compatible with some sequence in \(S(v)\). Branching on nodes \(v_1,\ldots,v_k\) of a common frontier replaces the parent subproblem by the state subproblems \(F(v_j)\). If every unresolved feasible path meets the frontier, then \(F\subseteq\bigcup_{j=1}^k F(v_j)\); if the represented prefix sets are disjoint, this union is a partition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A diagram node denotes all feasible completions of its represented prefixes; branching on a covering frontier yields complete state-space children.
assumptions_latex: The diagram is layered and arc labels determine assignment prefixes.
The selected frontier meets every unresolved feasible root-to-terminal path.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The frontier state subproblems cover all unresolved feasible solutions and partition them when their prefix sets are disjoint.

notation.meaning: unresolved feasible set of the parent

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation kind fits the node-state interpretation, and the coverage/partition distinction is mathematically plausible. No source is cited for the decision-diagram frontier semantics, particularly when merged nodes represent multiple prefixes.

children.title: Diagram Peeling
children.top_down_role: Extraction of diagram regions or paths into separate search subproblems.

assumptions_latex: The input diagram is finite, rooted, terminal-directed, and layered.
Shared prefixes are duplicated before paths are assigned to the two outputs.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The peeled and residual diagrams form a disjoint partition of the input path copies.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Path-partitioning peel operation for a layered decision diagram.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a layered diagram \(D=(V,A)\), rooted at \(r\), a selected node \(v\), and the root-to-\(v\) prefix subgraph. Duplicate any shared ancestors and arcs needed to separate paths reaching \(v\). Form the peeled diagram \(P_v\) from exactly those root-to-terminal paths whose separated prefix reaches \(v\), and delete their separated copies from the residual diagram \(R_v\). Remove nodes and arcs lying on no root-to-terminal path. Output \((P_v,R_v)\). With path copies distinguished, the path family satisfies \(\mathcal P(D)=\mathcal P(P_v)\mathbin{\dot\cup}\mathcal P(R_v)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Peeling separates all paths passing through a selected state into one diagram and leaves the remaining paths in a residual diagram.
knowledge_statements.title: Diagram Peeling

children.title: Peel-Derived Bounds
children.top_down_role: Bounds associated with residual or extracted diagram regions.

knowledge_statements.title: Peel-Derived Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bounds obtained after partitioning a relaxation by diagram peeling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider minimization and let the peeled and residual diagrams represent relaxations of disjoint feasible subsets \(F_P\) and \(F_R\), with valid lower bounds \(L_P\le\min_{x\in F_P} f(x)\) and \(L_R\le\min_{x\in F_R} f(x)\). If \(F=F_P\mathbin{\dot\cup}F_R\), then \(L=\min\{L_P,L_R\}\) is a valid lower bound for the parent problem. Given incumbent value \(U\), any component with bound at least \(U\) may be discarded. If both component bounds are at least \(U\), the entire parent subproblem is fathomed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The minimum of valid bounds for peeled and residual pieces bounds their parent; either piece is prunable when its bound reaches the incumbent.
assumptions_latex: The problem is a finite minimization problem.
Peeling partitions the parent feasible set into peeled and residual subsets.
Each component bound is valid for its represented subset.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The parent lower bound is \(\min\{L_P,L_R\}\), and components satisfying \(L_P\ge U\) or \(L_R\ge U\) are safely pruned.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The property kind fits a bounds leaf, and taking the minimum of component lower bounds is valid for a nonempty partition. A peel-specific source is absent, and the statement does not specify how an empty peeled or residual component is handled, so the formula cannot yet be accepted as the general leaf statement.

children.title: Peel Selection Policies
children.top_down_role: Policies for choosing diagram portions to extract during search.

knowledge_statements.title: Peel Selection Policies
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Admissible score-based selection of the next diagram peel.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a current diagram \(D\), a finite eligible set \(E(D)\) of peel objects, a deterministic score \(s:E(D)\to\mathbb R\), and a stopping predicate. While the predicate is false and \(E(D)\ne\varnothing\), select \(e\in\operatorname*{argmax}_{q\in E(D)}s(q)\), break ties by a fixed rule, peel \(e\) from \(D\), compute bounds for the peeled and residual diagrams, prune any dominated component, and recompute eligibility and affected scores. Stop when no eligible object remains, the stopping predicate holds, or the current subproblem is fathomed; output the retained components and their bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A peel policy scores eligible states, peels a highest-scoring choice, updates affected bounds and scores, and stops under an explicit termination rule.
assumptions_latex: The eligible set is finite at every iteration.
Peeling preserves coverage of unresolved feasible solutions.
Scores and tie-breaking are deterministic for a fixed diagram.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The algorithm returns valid bounded components covering every unresolved feasible solution.

notation.meaning: eligible peel objects in diagram D

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: An algorithmic policy is compatible with the leaf, but this particular deterministic argmax template is only one possible peel-selection family. No source establishes it as the intended policy framework or supports the claimed coverage conclusion.

children.title: Weak-Peel Regimes
children.top_down_role: Cases where extracted regions provide limited pruning or decomposition benefit.

knowledge_statements.title: Weak-Peel Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Regimes where peeling preserves validity but yields negligible search reduction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D_n\) contain \(2^n\) feasible root-to-terminal paths with identical relaxation bound \(L<U\). Suppose every permitted peel separates at most one path and leaves a residual diagram whose bound remains \(L\), while no peeled path improves the incumbent \(U\). After \(k\) peels, at least \(2^n-k\) unresolved paths remain and neither the residual nor any unprocessed component is fathomed by bound. Consequently, any method restricted to these peels requires at least \(2^n\) peel or terminal-processing steps to exhaust the subproblem.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If each peel isolates only one path and never improves either bound or incumbent, valid peeling degenerates to exponential enumeration.
assumptions_latex: The diagram has \(2^n\) feasible paths.
Every allowed peel removes at most one unresolved path.
All residual bounds stay strictly below the incumbent.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Exhaustion requires at least \(2^n\) peel or terminal-processing steps in this regime.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary kind fits the leaf. The constructed exponential regime is plausible, but the lower bound counts both peel and terminal-processing steps without defining the latter or stating that each such step resolves at most one path. A source or a more fully specified construction is required.

children.top_down_role: Filtering and consistency families using exact or relaxed multivalued decision diagrams.
