children.title: MDD Consistency Regimes
children.top_down_role: Consistency strengths supported by multivalued decision diagrams.

knowledge_statements.title: MDD Consistency Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exactness conditions governing consistency obtained from MDD path support.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For variables \(x_1,\ldots,x_n\) with current domains \(D_1,\ldots,D_n\), a layered MDD is domain-consistent for constraint \(C\) precisely when, for every \(i\) and \(a\in D_i\), an arc labeled \(a\) occurs at layer \(i\) on a root-to-terminal path if and only if there exists \(x\in C\cap\prod_{j=1}^n D_j\) with \(x_i=a\). An exact MDD satisfies both directions. A relaxation containing all feasible paths guarantees only that deleting labels absent from every MDD path is sound; retained labels need not possess feasible support.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact MDD paths characterize every supported domain value; relaxed MDDs permit sound deletion of absent labels but may retain unsupported ones.
assumptions_latex: The MDD has one decision layer per variable.
Every feasible assignment in the current domains is represented by a root-to-terminal path.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Path-based filtering enforces domain consistency exactly for an exact MDD and is generally incomplete for a proper relaxation.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition kind fits a regimes leaf, and the exact-versus-relaxed distinction is coherent. No MDD consistency source is supplied, so the terminology and the claimed equivalence with domain consistency remain unverified.

children.title: MDD Domain Filtering
children.top_down_role: Removal of unsupported variable values using diagram structure.

knowledge_statements.title: MDD Domain Filtering
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Domain-value deletion by root-to-terminal path support in an MDD.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a layered MDD \(D=(V,A)\) for variables \(x_1,\ldots,x_n\) and current domains \(D_i\). First delete every arc at layer \(i\) whose label is not in \(D_i\). Repeatedly delete each nonroot node with no incoming root-reachable arc, each nonterminal node with no terminal-reaching outgoing arc, and all incident arcs. For every \(i\), replace \(D_i\) by the labels of surviving layer-\(i\) arcs. Stop when no arc or domain changes; output the reduced MDD and domains. Every retained value then lies on a surviving root-to-terminal path.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Remove arcs disallowed by current domains, trim nodes outside root-to-terminal paths, and delete every domain value lacking a surviving labeled arc.
assumptions_latex: The MDD is finite, layered, and contains every feasible assignment allowed before filtering.
Layer \(i\) arc labels assign variable \(x_i\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output preserves all feasible assignments and every retained value has MDD path support.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits the filtering leaf. The trimming procedure and its preservation claim are standard-looking, but no inspectable MDD propagation citation is present; the unrelated local source inventory cannot support them.

children.title: Consistency-Driven Filtering
children.top_down_role: Correspondence between selected MDD consistency levels plus filtering outcomes.

knowledge_statements.title: Consistency-Driven Filtering
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fixed-point characterization of filtering by MDD path support.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(T\) map current domains to the domains obtained by retaining exactly the labels occurring on root-to-terminal paths of the domain-restricted MDD. Then \(T(D_1,\ldots,D_n)\subseteq(D_1,\ldots,D_n)\), and domain restriction is monotone: if \(E_i\subseteq D_i\) for all \(i\), then \(T(E)_i\subseteq T(D)_i\). Iterating \(T\) therefore reaches a fixed point in finitely many deletions. If the MDD exactly represents the constraint under the current domains, that fixed point is domain-consistent; for a relaxed MDD it is only path-consistent with the relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Path-support filtering is contracting and monotone, reaches a finite fixed point, and enforces domain consistency only when the MDD is exact.
assumptions_latex: All variable domains and the MDD are finite.
Filtering deletes labels but introduces no new domain values.
The same constraint MDD is restricted after each deletion.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Iteration terminates at the greatest path-supported subdomain below the input domains; exactness makes this fixed point domain-consistent.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The property kind fits the fixed-point statement. Contraction, monotonicity, finite termination, and the exact-MDD consistency conclusion are plausible, but the stronger greatest-fixed-point characterization has no supporting citation.

children.title: Incomplete Filtering Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Diagram or propagation regimes that leave unsupported values in variable domains.

knowledge_statements.title: Incomplete Filtering Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A relaxed MDD can retain a value having no feasible constraint support.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Take the constraint \(C=\{(x_1,x_2)\in\{0,1\}^2:x_1=x_2\}\) with current domains \(D_1=\{0\}\) and \(D_2=\{0,1\}\). The only feasible assignment is \((0,0)\), so value \(1\in D_2\) has no support. Consider a relaxed two-layer MDD accepting every pair in \(D_1\times D_2\). It contains the spurious path labeled \((0,1)\); hence ordinary path-support filtering retains \(1\) in \(D_2\). Thus completeness fails whenever relaxation paths need not correspond to feasible assignments.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For equality with the first variable fixed to zero, a universal relaxed MDD retains the unsupported second-variable value one through a spurious path.
assumptions_latex: Filtering tests support only by existence of a root-to-terminal MDD path.
The MDD is permitted to be a proper relaxation of the constraint.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Path-support filtering on a proper relaxed MDD need not establish domain consistency.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The counterexample kind exactly fits the failure-boundary leaf, and the example is internally valid under the stated path-support semantics. Nevertheless, the record provides neither a citation nor an explicit standard-field rationale, so its intended relaxed-MDD semantics lack admissible evidence.

knowledge_statements.title: Cost-Based MDD Filtering
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Incumbent-based deletion using minimum-cost paths through MDD arcs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a finite acyclic layered MDD with arc costs, current domains, and minimization cutoff \(U\). Restrict arcs to current-domain labels. Compute \(d_r(v)\), the minimum root-to-\(v\) cost, and \(d_t(v)\), the minimum \(v\)-to-terminal cost. Delete an arc \(a=(u,v)\) whenever \(d_r(u)+c(a)+d_t(v)\ge U\), then trim nodes outside all root-to-terminal paths and delete domain labels having no surviving arc. Recompute distances after deletions until stable. Output the reduced MDD and domains; every removed arc is incapable of belonging to a represented solution improving \(U\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Shortest-path prefix and suffix costs identify arcs that cannot improve the incumbent; deleting them also removes unsupported domain values.
assumptions_latex: The MDD is acyclic and contains every feasible assignment under consideration.
Each represented path cost equals or lower-bounds its assignment objective consistently.
Only solutions with objective strictly below \(U\) are sought.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Deleting every arc with \(d_r(u)+c(a)+d_t(v)\ge U\) preserves all represented paths whose cost is less than \(U\).

notation.meaning: minimum prefix and suffix path costs

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits cost-based filtering. The shortest-path deletion test is coherent for additive path costs, but the weaker alternative that path cost merely lower-bounds assignment objective requires a precise path-to-assignment cost relationship. No source supports those semantics or the filtering procedure.

knowledge_statements.title: Incremental MDD Propagation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Event-driven maintenance of MDD reachability after domain deletions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a reduced layered MDD, current domains, and a queue containing newly deleted values or arcs. Delete every queued value's labeled arcs. Maintain for each node counts of surviving root-reachable incoming arcs and terminal-reaching outgoing arcs. Whenever either required count becomes zero, delete the node's incident arcs and enqueue the resulting count changes. Whenever a layer label loses its last surviving root-to-terminal arc, delete that label from the corresponding domain and notify dependent constraints. Stop when the queue is empty or a domain becomes empty; output the updated MDD, domains, and failure status.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Incremental propagation processes only arcs and reachability counts affected by domain events, cascading deletions until a fixed point or failure.
assumptions_latex: The maintained MDD and reachability counts were correct before the queued events.
Domain updates are deletions only between rebuilds.
Every feasible assignment is represented before propagation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: At termination, the output equals full reachability trimming after the same deletions; an empty domain or missing root-to-terminal path certifies failure.

notation.meaning: queue of deletion and reachability events

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits incremental propagation. The event-driven deletion mechanism is plausible, but no source supports the reachability-count invariant or the assertion that termination exactly matches full trimming after the same deletions.

children.title: Multiple-Constraint Propagation
children.top_down_role: Propagation across several constraints represented by diagrams.

knowledge_statements.title: Multiple-Constraint Propagation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fair fixpoint propagation of several constraints represented on one finite layered decision diagram.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D=(V,A)\) be a finite layered acyclic decision diagram, let \(\mathcal P(E)\) denote the assignments encoded by the source-to-terminal paths of a subdiagram \(E\subseteq D\), and let \(C_1,\ldots,C_m\) be sets of assignments. For each \(i\), let \(F_i\) be contracting and sound in the sense that \(\mathcal P(E)\cap C_i\subseteq\mathcal P(F_i(E))\subseteq\mathcal P(E)\) for every reachable subdiagram \(E\). Starting from \(D^0=D\), apply the filters according to a fair schedule and trim nodes not lying on a source-to-terminal path. Because only finitely many arcs can be deleted, the process reaches a common fixpoint \(D^*\), and \(\mathcal P(D)\cap\bigcap_{i=1}^m C_i\subseteq\mathcal P(D^*)\). If, in addition, each filter enforces its constraint exactly, so that \(\mathcal P(F_i(E))=\mathcal P(E)\cap C_i\), then \(\mathcal P(D^*)=\mathcal P(D)\cap\bigcap_{i=1}^m C_i\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Apply contracting sound filters fairly until no filter changes the finite diagram. The fixpoint preserves every represented assignment satisfying all constraints, but it may retain violating assignments. It is exact when each filter exactly intersects the current path set with its constraint.
assumptions_latex: \(D\) is finite, layered, and acyclic.
Each \(F_i\) is contracting and sound on every reachable subdiagram.
The filter schedule is fair.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The process terminates with \(\mathcal P(D)\cap\bigcap_i C_i\subseteq\mathcal P(D^*)\); equality holds under exact enforcement by every filter.

notation.meaning: assignments encoded by source-to-terminal paths of subdiagram E
set of assignments satisfying constraint i

children.title: Sequence-Constraint Propagation
children.top_down_role: Diagram propagation for constraints over ordered decision sequences.

knowledge_statements.title: Sequence-Constraint Propagation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Propagation of a sequence constraint by synchronizing a diagram with an automaton.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D=(V,A)\) be a layered decision diagram whose arc labels form words of length \(n\), and let \(M=(Q,\Sigma,\delta,q_0,Q_F)\) recognize the permitted sequences. Construct the product diagram with states \((v,q)\). For every arc \(a=(v,w)\) labeled \(\ell(a)\), add \(((v,q),(w,\delta(q,\ell(a))))\) whenever the transition is defined. Retain only product states reachable from \((r,q_0)\) and able to reach some \((t,q_f)\) with \(q_f\in Q_F\). Project the surviving product arcs onto \(D\). The retained source-to-terminal paths are exactly those whose label sequences are accepted by \(M\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Intersect the decision diagram with an automaton for the sequence constraint, trim unreachable states, and project back. Exactly the accepted diagram paths survive.
assumptions_latex: \(D\) is a finite layered diagram with source \(r\) and terminal \(t\).
\(M\) recognizes precisely the allowed label sequences.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A path survives if and only if its label word belongs to \(L(M)\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The automaton-product construction and exact language-intersection conclusion are mathematically coherent and fit the algorithm leaf, but no inspectable source is supplied.

children.title: Cross-Constraint Propagation
children.top_down_role: Exchange of domain or state information among multiple diagram constraints.

knowledge_statements.title: Cross-Constraint Propagation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Information exchange between constraint-specific diagrams through shared variable domains.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let constraints \(C_1,\ldots,C_m\) have decision diagrams \(D_1,\ldots,D_m\) over possibly overlapping variable sets. For each variable \(x_j\), let \(S_{ij}\) be the values occurring on some source-to-terminal path of \(D_i\). A cross-constraint propagation round replaces the shared domain by \(S_j=\bigcap_{i:\,x_j\in C_i}S_{ij}\), deletes from every \(D_i\) arcs assigning \(x_j\notin S_j\), and trims disconnected nodes. Repeating these operations to a fixpoint is sound: no assignment satisfying all constraints is deleted. Domain consistency of every individual diagram does not, in general, imply global consistency of their conjunction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Intersect supported values across diagrams sharing a variable, delete unsupported arcs, and iterate. This is sound, but separate domain consistency need not establish global consistency.
assumptions_latex: Each \(D_i\) exactly represents the assignments satisfying \(C_i\) over its variables.
Arc deletion and trimming preserve every path using retained values.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Fixpoint propagation preserves every assignment in \(\bigcap_i C_i\), but may retain values having no globally compatible assignment.

notation.meaning: values of a shared variable supported by diagram i

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The principle correctly distinguishes sound shared-domain propagation from global consistency, but the record has no citation supporting its decision-diagram formulation or consistency limitation.

children.title: Combined-Propagation Scalability
children.top_down_role: Width, memory, plus propagation-cost regimes for coupled constraints.

knowledge_statements.title: Combined-Propagation Scalability
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Work bounds for monotone arc-deletion propagation under explicit queue and scan disciplines.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D=(V,A)\) be a finite diagram and let \(F_1,\ldots,F_m\) be contracting arc-deletion filters. Suppose an incremental worklist notifies each filter at most once for each deleted arc, and processing the notification of one deletion by \(F_i\) costs at most \(c_i\). Since an arc is deleted at most once, there are at most \(|A|\) deletion events and at most \(|A|m\) filter notifications, giving propagation work \(O\!\left(|A|\sum_{i=1}^m c_i\right)\), in addition to initialization and final termination checks. Alternatively, if one complete round invokes every filter at costs \(T_i(|V|,|A|)\), every nonfinal round deletes at least one new arc, and the algorithm stops after the first deletion-free round, then its work is \(O\!\left((|A|+1)\sum_{i=1}^m T_i(|V|,|A|)\right)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under a worklist that charges each deleted arc to each filter at most once, incremental propagation costs the number of initial arcs times the aggregate per-notification cost. Repeated complete scans have a corresponding bound when every nonfinal round deletes an arc and the first deletion-free round terminates the process.
assumptions_latex: Filters only delete arcs and never restore them.
Each deleted arc generates at most one notification to each filter.
For the full-scan bound, every nonfinal complete round deletes at least one previously present arc.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The incremental work is \(O\!\left(|A|\sum_i c_i\right)\), while disciplined complete scans cost \(O\!\left((|A|+1)\sum_i T_i(|V|,|A|)\right)\).

notation.meaning: number of arcs in the initial diagram
cost to filter i of processing one deletion notification
cost of one complete scan by filter i

children.title: Diagram-Guided Solution-Space Methods
children.top_down_role: Feasible-solution extraction, neighborhood search, enumeration, and post-optimality analysis using diagram structure.

top_down_textbook_witnesses.source: Decision Diagrams for Discrete Optimization: A Survey of Recent Advances
top_down_textbook_witnesses.locator: Solution Extraction; Solution-Space Analysis
top_down_textbook_witnesses.source_title: Decision Diagrams for Discrete Optimization: A Survey of Recent Advances

knowledge_statements.title: Restricted-Diagram Primal Heuristics
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Feasible-solution extraction from an under-approximating decision diagram.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a minimization problem with feasible set \(X\) and objective \(f\), construct a restricted decision diagram \(D_R\) such that every source-to-terminal path decodes to an element of \(X\), although some elements of \(X\) may be absent. Assign each arc its objective contribution when \(f\) is path-additive, compute a minimum-weight source-to-terminal path by dynamic programming, and decode it as \(\hat x\). If no terminal is reachable, return no candidate. Otherwise \(\hat x\in X\), and \(f(\hat x)\) is an incumbent upper bound on \(\min_{x\in X}f(x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Optimize over an under-approximating diagram. Any returned path is feasible and supplies an incumbent, but omitted paths prevent a global optimality guarantee.
assumptions_latex: Every path in \(D_R\) decodes to a feasible solution.
The objective is represented exactly by path weights.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If a terminal path exists, its minimum-weight decoding \(\hat x\) is feasible and satisfies \(f(\hat x)\geq \min_{x\in X}f(x)\).

notation.meaning: incumbent decoded from the best retained path

source_refs.locator: 2.7 Primal Bounds: Greedy and Local Search p. 34

source_witnesses.locator: 2.7 Primal Bounds: Greedy and Local Search p. 34

knowledge_statements.title: Diagram-Guided Neighborhood Search
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local search over a neighborhood encoded by a restricted decision diagram.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given an incumbent \(x\in X\), a neighborhood \(N(x)\subseteq X\), and a diagram \(D_x\) whose source-to-terminal paths encode exactly \(N(x)\), minimize the path representation of \(f\) over \(D_x\) and decode an optimizer \(y\). If \(f(y)<f(x)\), replace \(x\) by \(y\), rebuild the neighborhood diagram, and repeat; otherwise stop and return \(x\). When every neighborhood diagram is exact and solved exactly, termination occurs after finitely many strict improvements and the output satisfies \(f(x)\leq f(z)\) for every \(z\in N(x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Encode each incumbent’s neighborhood as a diagram, optimize over it, and accept strict improvement. Exact neighborhood diagrams yield a neighborhood-local optimum on termination.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is finite.
Each \(D_x\) exactly encodes \(N(x)\).
Path optimization represents \(f\) exactly.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The algorithm terminates at an \(N\)-local optimum after finitely many accepted moves.

source_refs.locator: 2.7 Primal Bounds: Greedy and Local Search p. 34

source_witnesses.locator: 2.7 Primal Bounds: Greedy and Local Search p. 34

children.title: Solution Enumeration
children.top_down_role: Enumeration of feasible solutions represented by diagram paths.

knowledge_statements.title: Solution Enumeration
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Duplicate-free enumeration of assignments represented by a decision diagram.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D=(V,A)\) be a finite acyclic decision diagram with source \(r\), terminal \(t\), and arc labels encoding successive decisions. Perform depth-first traversal from \(r\), maintaining the labels on the current path. Whenever \(t\) is reached, output the decoded assignment and backtrack; discard nodes and arcs that cannot reach \(t\). If distinct source-to-terminal paths decode to distinct assignments, the procedure outputs every represented solution exactly once, uses \(O(h+|V|)\) working memory with reachability marks, and has delay \(O(h+|A|)\) under a direct traversal implementation, where \(h\) is the number of layers.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Depth-first traversal outputs every terminal path’s assignment. With a one-path-per-assignment representation, enumeration is complete and duplicate-free.
assumptions_latex: \(D\) is finite and acyclic.
Each represented assignment has exactly one source-to-terminal path.
Path decoding takes time linear in the path length.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: All represented assignments are output exactly once with polynomial delay in the diagram size.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Duplicate-free path enumeration is standard, but the cited partial-enumeration section does not directly support the decision-diagram memory and delay bounds. A diagram-enumeration source with a precise traversal model is needed.

children.title: Pareto-Set Enumeration
children.top_down_role: Enumeration of nondominated solutions in multiobjective diagram models.

knowledge_statements.title: Pareto-Set Enumeration
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Enumeration of nondominated objective vectors and their diagram paths.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let each source-to-terminal path \(P\) of an acyclic diagram have additive objective vector \(c(P)\in\mathbb{R}^p\), to be minimized. In topological order, maintain at every node \(v\) a set \(L(v)\) of pairwise nondominated labels, each storing an objective vector and predecessor pointer. Extend every label across each outgoing arc, and delete a new or existing label only when its vector is dominated at the same node. At the terminal, backtrack every label in \(L(t)\). The resulting vectors are exactly the nondominated vectors represented by the diagram; retaining all tied predecessor pointers enumerates every represented Pareto-optimal path.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Propagate nondominated objective labels through the acyclic diagram. Terminal labels give all represented Pareto vectors, while retained predecessor ties recover all Pareto-optimal paths.
assumptions_latex: Arc objective vectors combine additively.
All objectives are minimized.
Dominance is componentwise and label extension is order-preserving.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L(t)=\operatorname{Min}_{\leq}\{c(P):P\text{ is an }r\text{-}t\text{ path}\}\).

notation.meaning: nondominated labels stored at node v

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The nondominated-label dynamic program is coherent under additive, extension-compatible objectives, but no source supports the exact Pareto-vector and tied-predecessor enumeration claims.

children.title: Dominance-Aware Enumeration
children.top_down_role: Use of dominance relations to organize or limit enumerated outcomes.

knowledge_statements.title: Dominance-Aware Enumeration
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Safe pruning of partial paths using extension-compatible dominance, with explicit treatment of equal-objective solutions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For partial paths ending at the same diagram node \(v\), let labels \(a\) and \(b\) contain every quantity affecting feasible continuations and final objective values. Write \(a\preceq_v b\) if every feasible continuation of \(b\) is feasible for \(a\) and the completion from \(a\) is componentwise no worse than the completion from \(b\) for every such continuation. A traversal may discard \(b\) when a retained label \(a\preceq_v b\) exists without losing any nondominated objective vector. To enumerate every nondominated represented assignment rather than only its objective vector, labels with equal attainable objective vectors must retain all distinct predecessor or path provenance; otherwise dominance pruning guarantees only one representative per nondominated vector.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A partial path may be pruned when another label can realize every continuation with no worse objectives. This preserves all nondominated objective vectors, but enumerating every distinct Pareto-optimal assignment also requires retaining provenance for objective ties.
assumptions_latex: Labels contain every state component affecting feasible continuation and final objectives.
The relation \(\preceq_v\) satisfies the stated extension condition.
All objectives use a fixed componentwise minimization order.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Dominance pruning preserves every nondominated attainable objective vector; preserving every distinct nondominated assignment additionally requires retaining tied provenance.

notation.meaning: labels of partial paths ending at a common node
extension-compatible componentwise dominance at node v

children.title: Output-Sensitive Enumeration Regimes
children.top_down_role: Enumeration behavior governed by represented output size plus diagram sharing.

knowledge_statements.title: Output-Sensitive Enumeration Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Polynomial-delay and output-sensitive bounds for traversing an explicit diagram.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D=(V,A)\) be an explicit acyclic diagram of height \(h\) representing \(K\) distinct assignments, one per source-to-terminal path. After \(O(|V|+|A|)\) preprocessing to mark nodes that reach the terminal, depth-first traversal outputs all assignments in \(O(|V|+|A|+Kh)\) time and \(O(|V|+h)\) working memory. Consequently the enumeration is output-sensitive and has \(O(h+|A|)\) worst-case delay under direct adjacency-list traversal. For dominance-aware enumeration, the same regime holds only when label comparison and the number of retained labels per node are polynomially bounded.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Explicit acyclic diagrams permit preprocessing plus time proportional to total output length. Dominance-aware variants retain polynomial delay only when label sets and comparisons remain polynomially bounded.
assumptions_latex: Assignments correspond bijectively to terminal paths.
Each path has length at most \(h\).
The diagram is stored by adjacency lists.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Enumeration time is \(O(|V|+|A|+Kh)\), with polynomial delay in the explicit diagram size.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The output-sensitive total-time claim is plausible for the stated explicit acyclic representation, but the precise preprocessing, delay, and dominance-aware qualifications require a cited enumeration result and traversal model.

children.title: Post-Optimality Analysis
children.top_down_role: Behavior of optimal outcomes under objective or parameter changes.

knowledge_statements.title: Post-Optimality Analysis
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact cost-expanded representation of solutions within a prescribed additive optimality tolerance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let an exact acyclic decision diagram \(D\) represent a finite feasible set \(X\), let its additive path costs equal \(f(x)\), and let \(z^*=\min_{x\in X}f(x)\). For \(\varepsilon\geq0\), construct a cost-expanded diagram whose states \((v,g)\) record an original node \(v\) and the exact accumulated path cost \(g\). Retain terminal states \((t,g)\) with \(g\leq z^*+\varepsilon\), together with precisely the expanded states and arcs lying on source-to-retained-terminal paths. The resulting expanded diagram represents exactly \(X_\varepsilon=\{x\in X:f(x)\leq z^*+\varepsilon\}\). Exhaustive path aggregation on this expanded diagram therefore gives exact statistics for \(X_\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Expand diagram states by exact accumulated cost and retain only paths ending within the additive optimality threshold. This expanded diagram represents exactly the near-optimal solutions, so exhaustive path aggregation gives exact statistics for that set.
assumptions_latex: \(D\) exactly and finitely represents \(X\).
Path costs represent \(f\) exactly and additively.
The cost expansion distinguishes all accumulated costs needed for exact threshold enforcement.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The retained cost-expanded diagram represents exactly \(X_\varepsilon=\{x\in X:f(x)\leq z^*+\varepsilon\}\).

notation.meaning: cost-expanded state with accumulated cost g at original node v
set of solutions within the additive threshold

children.title: Solution-Space Analysis
children.top_down_role: Structural analysis of feasible paths, alternatives, plus decision patterns.

knowledge_statements.title: Solution-Space Analysis
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Path-aggregation representation of structural statistics over a diagram-encoded solution set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let an exact acyclic decision diagram \(D\) represent a finite set \(S\) bijectively by its source-to-terminal paths. Define forward counts \(p(r)=1\) and \(p(v)=\sum_{(u,v)\in A}p(u)\), and backward counts \(q(t)=1\) and \(q(u)=\sum_{(u,v)\in A}q(v)\). Then \(|S|=p(t)\), and the number of represented solutions using an arc \(a=(u,v)\) equals \(p(u)q(v)\). Summing these arc counts by variable-value label yields exact marginal frequencies under the uniform distribution on \(S\); analogous semiring-valued recurrences compute additive aggregates.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Forward and backward path counts give the solution-set size and exact usage frequency of each decision arc. Grouping arcs yields variable-value marginals.
assumptions_latex: \(D\) is finite and acyclic.
Each element of \(S\) corresponds to exactly one source-to-terminal path.
Arc labels identify the represented variable decisions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(|S|=p(t)\) and every arc \((u,v)\) occurs in exactly \(p(u)q(v)\) represented solutions.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The forward/backward path-count identities and uniform marginal construction are mathematically precise and fit the representation leaf, but no inspectable decision-diagram or DAG path-aggregation source is supplied.

children.title: Near-Optimal Solution Structure
children.top_down_role: Diagram-supported analysis of solutions near the optimal value.

assumptions_latex: \(D\) is finite and acyclic.
Every represented solution corresponds to an \(r\)-to-\(t\) path.
Path cost is additive over arcs.

notation.meaning: Shortest prefix and suffix costs at vertex v, with value positive infinity when no corresponding path exists.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characterizes arcs that occur in near-optimal paths of a weighted exact decision diagram.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D=(V,A)\) be a finite acyclic decision diagram with root \(r\), terminal \(t\), and arc costs \(c_a\). Let \(d^+(v)\) and \(d^-(v)\) be the shortest-path costs from \(r\) to \(v\) and from \(v\) to \(t\), respectively, with value \(+\infty\) when the corresponding path does not exist, and let \(z^*=d^+(t)\). For \(\varepsilon\ge 0\), an arc \(a=(u,v)\) belongs to some root-to-terminal path of cost at most \(z^*+\varepsilon\) exactly when \[d^+(u)+c_a+d^-(v)\le z^*+\varepsilon.\] Retaining all such arcs preserves every path of cost at most \(z^*+\varepsilon\), but the retained subdiagram can also contain more expensive paths created by recombining retained prefixes and suffixes.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An arc occurs in a near-optimal path exactly when its shortest prefix-plus-arc-plus-suffix cost is within epsilon of the optimum; retaining all such arcs can also retain paths that are not near-optimal.
knowledge_statements.title: Near-Optimal Solution Structure

children.title: Representation-Limited Sensitivity
children.top_down_role: Sensitivity questions unresolved by the states, values, or paths retained in the diagram.

knowledge_statements.title: Representation-Limited Sensitivity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sensitivity conclusions are restricted to solutions retained by the diagram.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S_D\subseteq S\subseteq\mathbb R^n\), where a decision diagram represents exactly \(S_D\). For a perturbed minimization objective \((c+\Delta)^{\mathsf T}x\), the diagram computes \(v_D(\Delta)=\min_{x\in S_D}(c+\Delta)^{\mathsf T}x\), so \(v_D(\Delta)\ge v(\Delta)=\min_{x\in S}(c+\Delta)^{\mathsf T}x\). Equality holds exactly when \(S_D\) contains a perturbed global minimizer. The limitation can occur under arbitrarily small perturbations: for \(S=\{0,1\}\), \(S_D=\{0\}\), \(c=\eta>0\), and \(\Delta=-2\eta\), the represented optimum is \(0\) while the true optimum is attained at \(1\), for every \(\eta>0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A restricted diagram gives correct sensitivity results only while it retains a globally optimal solution for the perturbed objective.
assumptions_latex: \(S_D\subseteq S\) are nonempty finite sets.
The optimization problem is a minimization problem.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(v_D(\Delta)=v(\Delta)\iff \operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in S}(c+\Delta)^{\mathsf T}x\cap S_D\ne\varnothing.\)

notation.meaning: Solutions represented by the decision diagram.
Perturbed optimum restricted to represented solutions.
True perturbed optimum over all feasible solutions.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D=(V,A)\) be a finite acyclic diagram with root \(r\), terminal \(t\), and label vector \(\ell_a\in\mathbb R^n\) on each arc. Introduce \(y_a\ge0\) and impose \[\sum_{a\in\delta^+(v)}y_a-\sum_{a\in\delta^-(v)}y_a=\begin{cases}1,&v=r,\\-1,&v=t,\\0,&v\in V\setminus\{r,t\}.\end{cases}\] Let \(B\) denote the node-arc incidence matrix under this outgoing-minus-incoming convention, so the balance equations are \(By=e_r-e_t\). Link the original variables by \(x=\sum_{a\in A}\ell_a y_a\). The resulting polyhedron is the linear image of the unit root-to-terminal flow polytope, and its integral flow points are incidence vectors of represented paths.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A decision diagram becomes an extended formulation by sending one unit of flow through it and linking arc flow to original variables.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be finite, and let a finite acyclic decision diagram have root-to-terminal path-label sums exactly equal to the points of \(S\). Let \(Q_D\) be its unit-flow formulation with linking equation \(x=\sum_{a\in A}\ell_a y_a\). Then \[\operatorname{proj}_x(Q_D)=\operatorname{conv}(S).\] Consequently, optimizing any linear function of \(x\) over \(Q_D\) has the same value as optimizing it over \(S\), without integrality restrictions on \(y\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The continuous unit-flow formulation of an exact decision diagram projects precisely onto the convex hull of its represented feasible solutions.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be the feasible set and let \(R_D\) be the set of label sums of all root-to-terminal paths in a relaxed decision diagram, with \(S\subseteq R_D\). If \(Q_D\) is the linked unit-flow formulation, then \[\operatorname{conv}(S)\subseteq\operatorname{proj}_x(Q_D)=\operatorname{conv}(R_D).\] Hence, for every linear minimization objective \(c^{\mathsf T}x\), the diagram relaxation value is no greater than the true value. The inclusion is strict precisely when some point of \(\operatorname{conv}(R_D)\) lies outside \(\operatorname{conv}(S)\); spurious paths need not cause strictness if their labels already belong to \(\operatorname{conv}(S)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A relaxed diagram projects to the convex hull of all its path labels, yielding an outer approximation of the true feasible hull.

children.title: Diagram Formulation Linking

knowledge_statements.title: Diagram Formulation Linking
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines the linear map connecting diagram flow to original variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a labeled diagram with arc-flow vector \(y\in\mathbb R_+^A\), a diagram formulation linking system is a collection of linear equations that makes original variables \(x\in\mathbb R^n\) equal to the aggregate labels of the flow. In the canonical additive form it is \[x_i=\sum_{a\in A}\ell_{ai}y_a\quad(i=1,\ldots,n),\] equivalently \(x=L y\). For an integral root-to-terminal path flow \(\chi^p\), compatibility with the diagram semantics requires \(L\chi^p\) to equal the solution encoded by path \(p\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Linking equations recover each original variable by summing its label contributions over the diagram flow.
assumptions_latex: Arc labels are additive along paths.
\(y\) satisfies the diagram unit-flow constraints.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x=Ly\), with \(L\chi^p\) equal to the point encoded by every path \(p\).

knowledge_statements.title: Diagram Formulation Projection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines elimination of diagram-flow variables from an extended formulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F_D=\{y\in\mathbb R_+^A:By=b\}\) be a diagram-flow polytope and let \(x=Ly\) be its linking system. The diagram formulation projected into the original variable space is \[P_D=\operatorname{proj}_x\{(x,y):y\in F_D,\ x=Ly\}=\{Ly:y\in F_D\}.\] If additional original-space constraints \(Hx\le h\) are imposed, the projected formulation is \(P_D\cap\{x:Hx\le h\}\). Projection removes the auxiliary arc-flow variables while preserving exactly the original-variable vectors admitted by some feasible diagram flow.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Projection eliminates arc-flow variables and retains exactly the original-variable points generated by feasible diagram flows.
assumptions_latex: \(F_D\) is a nonempty diagram-flow polyhedron.
The linking map \(L\) is linear.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P_D=\{x:\exists y\in F_D,\ x=Ly\}=L(F_D).\)

notation.meaning: Original-space projection of the linked formulation.

children.title: Linking–Projection Compatibility
children.top_down_role: Interaction between linking choices plus projected formulation structure.

knowledge_statements.title: Linking–Projection Compatibility
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact compatibility criterion for path labels, linking, and projection.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal P_D\) be the root-to-terminal paths of a finite acyclic diagram, let \(F_D\) be its unit-flow polytope, and let \(L\) be the linking map. For a target finite set \(S\subseteq\mathbb R^n\), linking and projection are convex-hull compatible exactly when \[\operatorname{conv}\{L\chi^p:p\in\mathcal P_D\}=\operatorname{conv}(S).\] Because \(F_D=\operatorname{conv}\{\chi^p:p\in\mathcal P_D\}\), this condition is equivalent to \(L(F_D)=\operatorname{conv}(S)\). Pathwise exactness, \(\{L\chi^p:p\in\mathcal P_D\}=S\), is sufficient but not necessary for convex-hull compatibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Linking and projection are compatible when the convex hull of linked path images equals the intended feasible convex hull.
assumptions_latex: The diagram is finite and acyclic.
\(F_D\) is its unit root-to-terminal flow polytope.
\(L\) maps arc flows into the original variable space.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L(F_D)=\operatorname{conv}(S)\iff\operatorname{conv}\{L\chi^p:p\in\mathcal P_D\}=\operatorname{conv}(S).\)

notation.meaning: Linking map from flow space to original space.

children.title: Projection Strength Loss
children.top_down_role: Regimes where projection obscures structural or relaxation strength present in the extended formulation.

knowledge_statements.title: Projection Strength Loss
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A spurious path can make the projected relaxation strictly weaker.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider the feasible set \(S=\{(0,0),(1,1)\}\subseteq\{0,1\}^2\). Its convex hull is \(\{x\in[0,1]^2:x_1=x_2\}\). A relaxed two-layer diagram that permits both binary choices independently has path-label set \(R_D=\{0,1\}^2\), so its linked unit-flow projection is \(P_D=[0,1]^2\). Therefore \(\operatorname{conv}(S)\subsetneq P_D\). For the objective \(x_1-x_2\), minimization over \(S\) has value \(0\), whereas minimization over \(P_D\) has value \(-1\), attained at \((0,1)\). Thus merging states that forget the equality relation causes a strict projection-strength loss.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Forgetting the relation between two equal binary variables enlarges their exact diagonal hull to the unit square and weakens the bound.
assumptions_latex: The relaxed diagram permits every pair in \(\{0,1\}^2\).
Arc labels recover the two binary coordinates.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{conv}(S)=\{x\in[0,1]^2:x_1=x_2\}\subsetneq[0,1]^2=P_D.\)

knowledge_statements.title: Diagram-Based Cut Separation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Farkas separation over a diagram extended formulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P_D=\{x:\exists y\ge0,\ Ay+Bx\le b\}\), and let \(\bar x\) be a candidate point. Solve \[\max_{\lambda}\ \lambda^{\mathsf T}(B\bar x-b)\quad\text{subject to}\quad \lambda\ge0,\ A^{\mathsf T}\lambda\ge0,\ \mathbf1^{\mathsf T}\lambda\le1.\] If the optimal value is positive, output the valid inequality \(\lambda^{\mathsf T}Bx\le\lambda^{\mathsf T}b\), which is violated by \(\bar x\). If the value is zero, no certificate of this normalized Farkas form separates \(\bar x\) from \(P_D\); equivalently, \(\bar x\in P_D\) when the displayed system gives a complete description of the diagram extension.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Separate a point from the diagram projection by solving a normalized Farkas problem and returning its violated projected inequality.
assumptions_latex: \(P_D\) is exactly the projection of the displayed linear system.
All data are finite-dimensional and rational.
The separation problem is solved to optimality.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\lambda^{\mathsf T}(B\bar x-b)>0\implies \lambda^{\mathsf T}Bx\le\lambda^{\mathsf T}b\text{ separates }\bar x\text{ from }P_D.\)

notation.meaning: Projection of the diagram extended formulation.

knowledge_statements.title: Decision Diagrams as Pricing Oracles
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Shortest-path pricing when reduced costs decompose over diagram arcs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a restricted master dual vector \(\pi\), suppose every column corresponds to a root-to-terminal path \(p\) and its reduced cost decomposes as \[\bar c_p=c_p-\pi^{\mathsf T}a_p=\sum_{a\in p}w_a(\pi).\] Assign weight \(w_a(\pi)\) to each diagram arc and compute a shortest root-to-terminal path by processing vertices in topological order. If its weight is negative, return the associated path column to the master problem. If the minimum weight is nonnegative, stop: no represented column has negative reduced cost. Exact pricing over the full column set requires the diagram to represent every admissible column.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Pricing reduces to a shortest-path computation when each represented column's reduced cost is the sum of its diagram arc weights.
assumptions_latex: The decision diagram is finite and acyclic.
Columns and root-to-terminal paths correspond.
Reduced cost is additive over path arcs.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\min_p\bar c_p=\min_{p}\sum_{a\in p}w_a(\pi)\), and a negative shortest path is an improving column.

notation.meaning: Current dual vector of the restricted master problem.
Master constraint column encoded by path p.
Dual-adjusted reduced-cost contribution of arc a.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The shortest-path pricing procedure is mathematically coherent, clearly distinguishes represented-column pricing from exact full pricing, and algorithm fits the terminal container. No source is supplied for the column-generation decision-diagram specialization.

knowledge_statements.title: Decision Diagrams as Decomposition Subproblems
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Diagram shortest paths evaluate a discrete Lagrangian subproblem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(\min\{c^{\mathsf T}x+d^{\mathsf T}s:Ax+Bs\ge b,\ x\in X,\ s\in S\}\), where a decision diagram represents \(S\). For a multiplier \(\lambda\ge0\), assign arc weights so that every path encoding \(s\) has weight \((d-B^{\mathsf T}\lambda)^{\mathsf T}s\). Compute a shortest root-to-terminal path and set \(s(\lambda)\) to its encoded solution. Together with minimizing \((c-A^{\mathsf T}\lambda)^{\mathsf T}x\) over \(X\), this evaluates the Lagrangian bound \[g(\lambda)=\lambda^{\mathsf T}b+\min_{x\in X}(c-A^{\mathsf T}\lambda)^{\mathsf T}x+\min_{s\in S}(d-B^{\mathsf T}\lambda)^{\mathsf T}s.\] Update \(\lambda\) by a dual method and retain the best bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A decision diagram solves the discrete block of a Lagrangian decomposition by shortest path under multiplier-adjusted arc costs.
assumptions_latex: The diagram represents exactly \(S\).
The discrete block objective decomposes additively over arcs.
The original problem is a minimization problem with coupling constraints \(Ax+Bs\ge b\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(g(\lambda)\) is a valid lower bound, and its discrete minimum is obtained by a shortest diagram path.

notation.meaning: Nonnegative multiplier for the coupling constraints.
Discrete feasible set represented by the diagram.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The multiplier signs and lower-bound direction are correct for a minimization problem with greater-than coupling constraints, and the diagram shortest path correctly evaluates the discrete block under additive arc costs. Algorithm fits the terminal container, but no source supports the decision-diagram decomposition specialization.
