children.title: Constraint-Handler Interfaces
children.top_down_role: Decision-diagram integration through constraint-handler callbacks, lifecycle hooks, enforcement contexts, and solver events.

knowledge_statements.title: Constraint-Handler Interfaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Abstract semantic contract; callback names and solver-specific result codes are intentionally omitted.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A constraint-handler interface is a map \(H\) that, for an active constraint \(c\), solver state \(s\), and inspected candidate \(x\), returns one of: feasible, infeasible, domain reduction, valid separating inequality, or branching request. If \(H(c,s,x)\) reports feasible, then \(x\in F(c)\). If it reports infeasible, then \(F(s)\cap F(c)=\varnothing\). Every returned domain reduction or inequality must preserve \(F(s)\cap F(c)\), and every branching request must produce child regions whose union contains \(F(s)\cap F(c)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A constraint handler inspects an active constraint and candidate and may accept, reject, reduce domains, separate, or branch, but every action must preserve all assignments feasible for the current state and constraint.
assumptions_latex: The current solver state is \(s\), the active constraint is \(c\), and the inspected candidate is \(x\).
The assignments compatible with \(s\) form \(F(s)\), and those satisfying \(c\) form \(F(c)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every returned enforcement action is sound for \(F(s)\cap F(c)\).

notation.meaning: Assignments compatible with the current state

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: abstract soundness contract for constraint-handler callbacks

children.title: Propagator Interfaces
children.top_down_role: Decision-diagram integration for domain filtering, propagation timing, explanation support, and solver-state access.

assumptions_latex: Each variable \(x_i\) has a current domain \(D_i\), and \(D=\prod_i D_i\).
The constraint system represented by the decision diagram has feasible set \(F\subseteq D\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A propagation response contracts domains without deleting any point of \(F\).

notation.meaning: Feasible assignments represented by the constraint system

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Domain-propagation semantics for a decision-diagram plugin, independent of a particular solver API.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A propagator interface implements an operator \(P\) on product domains. Given \(D\), it returns either infeasible or a contracted domain \(D'=P(D)\). Soundness requires \(D'\subseteq D\) and \(F\cap D'=F\cap D\). An infeasible response is permitted only when \(F\cap D=\varnothing\). The interface may additionally return reasons for removed values; each reason must imply the corresponding exclusion under the current state. Repeated invocation is allowed until no domain changes occur, without requiring a single invocation of \(P\) to reach a fixed point.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A propagator removes domain values while preserving every feasible assignment, reports infeasibility only for an empty feasible domain, and may attach valid reasons.
knowledge_statements.title: Propagator Interfaces

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition fits the propagator-interface leaf and its solution-preserving contraction contract is mathematically coherent, but no inspectable source supports the asserted interface and reason semantics.

children.title: Handler–Propagator Coordination Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Responsibility division, shared state, callback ordering, and duplicated-work risks across the two plugin roles.

assumptions_latex: The handler owns enforcement of a decision-diagram constraint.
The propagator owns solution-preserving domain contraction.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Coordination is sound when exchanged deductions are validated and neither component silently assumes the other's obligations.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: modular ownership and sound handoff condition
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Ownership boundary between enforcement callbacks and domain-propagation callbacks.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A handler-propagator boundary is well formed when: the handler alone creates, transforms, activates, deactivates, and deletes handler-owned constraint state \(S_H\); the propagator changes the shared domain \(D\) only through solver-approved deductions; and diagram caches in \(S_P\) are rebuilt or invalidated whenever a relevant constraint or domain version changes. A deduction proposed by either component may be consumed by the other only after it has entered the shared solver state. Infeasibility, cutoff, and success statuses must describe completed effects, not merely requested effects.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Handlers own constraint enforcement, propagators own domain deductions, and both coordinate only through validated solver state with explicit cache invalidation and result ownership.
knowledge_statements.title: Handler–Propagator Coordination Boundaries

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition kind fits a coordination-boundary leaf, but ownership, cache invalidation, shared-state handoff, and status semantics are solver-specific claims without cited support.

children.title: Relaxator Interfaces
children.top_down_role: Interfaces exposing diagram-derived relaxations, dual information, bounds, and execution timing.

assumptions_latex: At a search node \(u\), the original feasible region is \(F_u\) and the objective is \(c^\top x\).
The decision-diagram relaxation represents a set \(R_u\supseteq F_u\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The returned value \(L_u\) is a valid node lower bound: \(L_u\leq\min\{c^\top x:x\in F_u\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimization convention with a decision-diagram outer relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A relaxator interface receives node \(u\) and returns a status, a bound \(L_u\), and optionally a relaxed solution \(\bar x_u\in R_u\). On successful exact evaluation of the supplied relaxation, \(L_u=\min\{c^\top x:x\in R_u\}\); hence \(L_u\leq\min\{c^\top x:x\in F_u\}\). If only a certified lower estimate is computed, the interface must still guarantee the displayed inequality. It may report relaxation infeasibility only when \(R_u=\varnothing\), which also certifies \(F_u=\varnothing\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A relaxator evaluates an outer decision-diagram region and returns a certified lower bound, an optional relaxed solution, or a sound infeasibility result.
knowledge_statements.title: Relaxator Interfaces

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition fits the relaxator-interface leaf, but the interface contract lacks a source and uses attained minima without assumptions ensuring nonemptiness and attainment on successful evaluation.

children.title: Separator Interfaces
children.top_down_role: Interfaces exposing diagram-derived inequalities, cut pools, separation contexts, and efficacy controls.

assumptions_latex: The feasible set at node \(u\) is \(F_u\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\).
The point supplied for separation is \(\bar x\in\mathbb{R}^n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every returned cut is valid for \(F_u\) and violated by \(\bar x\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Linear separation of a relaxation point from the node feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A separator interface receives \(u\) and \(\bar x\) and returns either no cut or an inequality \(a^\top x\leq\beta\). A returned inequality must satisfy \(a^\top x\leq\beta\) for every \(x\in F_u\) and \(a^\top\bar x>\beta\), up to declared numerical tolerances. If the inequality is local, its validity domain must be recorded as the subtree rooted at \(u\); otherwise it must be globally valid. A no-cut response asserts only that this invocation found no admissible violated inequality, not that none exists.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A separator returns a valid inequality violated by the current relaxation point, records whether it is local or global, or reports that it found none.
knowledge_statements.title: Separator Interfaces

children.title: Relaxation–Separation Coordination
children.top_down_role: Shared diagram state, information exchange, scheduling conflicts, and redundant-processing boundaries.

assumptions_latex: The solver minimizes \(c^\top x\) over node feasible set \(F_u\).
All accepted cuts are valid for \(F_u\) and retained during the coordination round.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The sequence of relaxation bounds is nondecreasing and every bound remains valid for \(F_u\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Iterative relaxation and separation at one branch-and-bound node.

source_refs.source_title: Relaxation and Decomposition Methods for Mixed Integer Nonlinear Programming

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize \(R_u^0\supseteq F_u\). At round \(k\), the relaxator computes \(L_u^k=\min\{c^\top x:x\in R_u^k\}\) and a minimizer \(\bar x^k\), or certifies \(R_u^k=\varnothing\). The separator returns valid cuts \(C^k\) violated by \(\bar x^k\). If \(C^k=\varnothing\), stop and output \((L_u^k,\bar x^k)\); otherwise set \(R_u^{k+1}=R_u^k\cap\bigcap C^k\) and repeat. Since \(F_u\subseteq R_u^{k+1}\subseteq R_u^k\), each \(L_u^k\) is valid and \(L_u^{k+1}\geq L_u^k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeatedly solve the diagram relaxation, separate its solution, and retain valid cuts until no cut is found; the resulting lower bounds cannot decrease.
knowledge_statements.title: Relaxation–Separation Coordination

source_witnesses.source_title: Relaxation and Decomposition Methods for Mixed Integer Nonlinear Programming

children.title: Branching Interfaces
children.top_down_role: Diagram-informed branching candidates, branch scoring, child-state transfer, and branching-context access.

assumptions_latex: The current search node has feasible region \(F_u\).
A branching response creates finitely many child regions \(B_1,\ldots,B_m\) with \(m\geq2\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Sound branching requires \(F_u\subseteq\bigcup_{j=1}^m B_j\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Semantic branching contract for decisions derived from a decision diagram.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A branching interface receives the current node state and returns either no branch or child descriptions \(B_1,\ldots,B_m\). A valid branch must cover the parent feasible region, \(F_u\subseteq\bigcup_{j=1}^m B_j\), so that no feasible assignment is lost. Each child must impose a solver-representable restriction, and the child descriptions must exclude the current unresolved state sufficiently to ensure search progress. Pairwise disjointness is desirable but not required for correctness. Any diagram-derived scores used to choose the branch affect search order only and do not replace the coverage condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A branching plugin creates solver-representable children covering every parent-feasible assignment and ensuring progress; diagram scores may guide the choice but not correctness.
knowledge_statements.title: Branching Interfaces

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition fits the branching-interface leaf and the coverage condition is standard, but the solver-representability and progress requirements are uncited and the latter is not stated as a checkable condition.

children.title: Node-Selection Interfaces
children.top_down_role: Diagram-derived node priorities, search-state metadata, queue interaction, and selection overhead.

assumptions_latex: The open-node set is a finite set \(Q\).
Each \(u\in Q\) carries solver state and a selection key.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A valid invocation returns an element of \(Q\) or reports that \(Q=\varnothing\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Search-node selection using diagram-derived or solver-derived priorities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A node-selection interface is a rule \(N\) that, given the nonempty open-node set \(Q\), returns one node \(N(Q)\in Q\). It may compute a key \(\kappa(u)\) from bounds, depth, diagram width, or other state and select an extremal key according to a declared tie rule. If \(Q=\varnothing\), it returns no node. For a complete finite search, the policy must not permanently starve an open node unless that node is pruned by a valid solver certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A node selector chooses an existing open node using a declared priority and tie rule, while a complete search must not leave an unpruned node permanently unselected.
knowledge_statements.title: Node-Selection Interfaces

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition fits the node-selection-interface leaf, but the permanent-starvation condition is a global scheduling property rather than a single-invocation interface condition and lacks authoritative support.

children.title: Primal-Heuristic Interfaces
children.top_down_role: Diagram-supported feasible-solution extraction, heuristic timing, incumbent submission, and search guidance.

assumptions_latex: The original problem has feasible set \(F\) and objective \(c^\top x\).
The incumbent value is \(U\), with \(U=+\infty\) when no incumbent exists.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: An accepted heuristic candidate belongs to \(F\) and may replace the incumbent only when \(c^\top\hat x<U\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: primal-heuristic feasibility and incumbent contract
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Primal heuristic consuming decision-diagram information in a minimization solver.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A primal-heuristic interface receives current solver and diagram state and returns failure or a complete candidate \(\hat x\). Before acceptance, the solver must verify \(\hat x\in F\), including integrality and all original constraints within declared tolerances. If verified and \(c^\top\hat x<U\), the candidate becomes the incumbent and \(U\) is updated to \(c^\top\hat x\); otherwise the incumbent is unchanged. Failure to produce a candidate carries no infeasibility implication. Partial diagram paths must be completed and checked before they are submitted as solutions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A primal heuristic may propose a diagram-derived solution, but it updates the incumbent only after complete feasibility, integrality, and objective improvement are verified.
knowledge_statements.title: Primal-Heuristic Interfaces

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition fits the primal-heuristic-interface leaf and distinguishes candidate generation from verified acceptance, but its solver-specific feasibility and incumbent-update contract has no cited source.

knowledge_statements.title: Pricer Interfaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact reduced-cost pricing, potentially implemented by shortest paths in a decision diagram.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A pricer interface receives an optimal restricted-master dual vector \(\pi\) and either returns one or more admissible columns \(j\in\mathcal J\) with reduced cost \(\bar c_j=c_j-\pi^\top a_j<0\), subject to the declared tolerance, or returns a completeness certificate. The certificate is valid only if pricing has been solved over all of \(\mathcal J\) and establishes \(\min_{j\in\mathcal J}\bar c_j\geq0\). When the restricted master has an optimal primal-dual pair and the full master is feasible and bounded, this certificate establishes optimality of the restricted-master solution for the full master linear program. A heuristic no-column response is not a completeness certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A pricer supplies negative-reduced-cost columns or, after exhaustive pricing from an optimal restricted-master dual solution, certifies that none exists; heuristic failure is not an optimality certificate.
assumptions_latex: The restricted master linear program is feasible and bounded and has an optimal primal-dual pair whose dual vector is \(\pi\).
Each admissible column \(j\in\mathcal J\) has objective coefficient \(c_j\), master column \(a_j\), and reduced cost \(\bar c_j=c_j-\pi^\top a_j\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A complete pricing certificate establishes \(\bar c_j\geq0\) for every \(j\in\mathcal J\), and under the stated assumptions certifies full-master LP optimality.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard column-generation pricing interface and completeness certificate

children.title: Diagram State Across the Solver Lifecycle
children.top_down_role: Diagram maintenance at presolve and search nodes, including reuse and synchronization with solver state.

top_down_textbook_witnesses.locator: Propagator timing; relaxation-handler execution; branching candidates; plugin lifecycle

children.title: Presolve Integration
children.top_down_role: Diagram maintenance under variable elimination, constraint reduction, coefficient changes, and presolver events.

assumptions_latex: The original formulation has feasible set \(F\), and presolve produces a transformed feasible set \(F'\).
Presolve supplies transformations sufficient to map solutions between the two formulations.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Diagram state used after presolve must represent \(F'\) or a declared relaxation of \(F'\), not stale original domains.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Consistency of decision-diagram data with a presolved formulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Presolve integration is sound when every transformed feasible solution \(y\in F'\) lifts through \(T\) to an original feasible solution \(T(y)\in F\), and every original solution relevant to optimization has a corresponding transformed representative with the same objective value after accounting for fixed offsets. Any presolve operation that fixes, aggregates, substitutes, deletes, or changes the domain of a diagram variable must update its diagram representation or invalidate that representation. A diagram may be reused after presolve only when its recorded variables, domains, constraints, and objective data match the transformed formulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Presolve must preserve solution correspondence and must update or invalidate every diagram affected by variable, domain, constraint, or objective transformations.
knowledge_statements.title: Presolve Integration

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition kind fits the presolve-integration leaf, but the required correspondence, objective offsets, and diagram invalidation rules are uncited, and 'relevant to optimization' is not a precise quantifier.

children.title: Domain Initialization
children.top_down_role: Initial variable domains, root-state construction, feasibility filtering, and diagram-state allocation.

knowledge_statements.title: Domain Initialization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Initialization from finite presolved domains into a layered decision diagram.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given finite domains \(D_1,\ldots,D_n\), create a root at layer \(0\) and a terminal at layer \(n\). At layer \(i\), permit only arcs labeled by values in \(D_i\), and construct or merge states according to a declared exact or relaxed decision-diagram procedure. Remove nodes and arcs lying on no root-to-terminal path. Output the diagram \(G\), its variable-to-layer map, and its construction status. The procedure may declare exact initialization only after establishing \(P(G)=F'\); it may declare relaxed initialization only after establishing \(F'\subseteq P(G)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Initialize diagram layers from the finite presolved domains, remove structure on no complete path, and declare exact or relaxed status only when the corresponding path-set invariant has been established.
assumptions_latex: The presolved variables are ordered \(x_1,\ldots,x_n\) with finite domains \(D_1,\ldots,D_n\).
The diagram is layered in that variable order, and \(F'\subseteq\prod_{i=1}^n D_i\) is the intended transformed feasible set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Initialization produces a diagram satisfying either \(P(G)=F'\) with exact status or \(F'\subseteq P(G)\) with relaxed status.

notation.meaning: Assignments encoded by root-to-terminal paths of G

children.title: Presolve-to-Initialization Handoff
children.top_down_role: Transfer of transformed model data into initial diagram domains, states, layers, and metadata.

knowledge_statements.title: Presolve-to-Initialization Handoff
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sound handoff from a presolved discrete model to initial decision-diagram domains and state.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let presolve transform a model with feasible assignments \(F\) into a reduced model with feasible assignments \(F'\), together with a reconstruction map \(r:F'\to F\). For each surviving variable \(x_i\), initialize its diagram domain to the presolved domain \(D_i'\). Compile an initial diagram \(G_0\) in the prescribed variable order, and require \(F'\subseteq P(G_0)\) for a relaxation or \(F'=P(G_0)\) for an exact diagram. Transfer fixed values, objective offsets, and reconstruction data without reinterpretation. Output \((G_0,(D_i')_i,r)\); reject the handoff if a transferred restriction can exclude an assignment in \(F'\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Initialize the diagram from presolved domains and metadata, preserving every reduced feasible assignment and the ability to reconstruct an original feasible solution.
assumptions_latex: \(r(F')\subseteq F\) and every original feasible solution retained by presolve has a representative in \(F'\).
The diagram compiler uses the presolved variable identities and ordering.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F'\subseteq P(G_0)\) and \(r(P(G_0)\cap F')\subseteq F\).

notation.meaning: Assignments encoded by root-to-terminal paths of diagram G.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: sound presolve interfaces preserve feasible assignments and reconstruction metadata
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm fits the handoff container and is internally coherent, but no inspectable source supports the decision-diagram-specific transfer, reconstruction, and rejection requirements. Standard-field rationale alone is insufficient to establish this operational interface.

children.title: Local Diagram State
children.top_down_role: Node-specific domains, conditional diagram fragments, reversible modifications, and subtree validity.

knowledge_statements.title: Local Diagram State
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Node-specific diagram state in a branch-and-bound or search subtree.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At a search node \(B\), a local diagram state is a tuple \(S_B=(D_B,\Delta_B,\ell_B,\nu_B)\), where \(\Delta_B\) records the domains implied by the root-to-\(B\) decisions, \(D_B\) is an exact or relaxed diagram for the conditioned subproblem, \(\ell_B\) is a valid lower bound for minimization, and \(\nu_B\) is its state version. If \(F_B\) is the conditioned feasible set, validity requires \(F_B=P(D_B)\) for an exact diagram or \(F_B\subseteq P(D_B)\) for a relaxation, together with \(\ell_B\leq\inf\{c(x):x\in F_B\}\). The tuple may be discarded when the subtree rooted at \(B\) closes.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Local state contains the conditioned domains, diagram, valid subtree bound, and version belonging to one search node.
assumptions_latex: The optimization problem is a minimization problem with objective \(c\).
\(F_B\) denotes the feasible assignments consistent with the path to \(B\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(S_B\) is local to \(B\) and remains valid only while its conditioning restrictions remain active.

notation.meaning: Valid lower bound for the conditioned subproblem.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: local search state is conditioned by the active node domains
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition matches the local-state leaf and introduces its principal objects, but the particular tuple, version semantics, lifecycle condition, and diagram-validity requirements have no cited source.

children.title: Global Diagram State
children.top_down_role: Solver-wide diagram structures, globally valid reductions, shared caches, and persistent metadata.

knowledge_statements.title: Global Diagram State
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Solver-wide diagram information valid independently of any single open search node.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A global diagram state is a versioned tuple \(S_G=(D_G,\Theta_G,U,\nu_G)\), where \(D_G\) and metadata \(\Theta_G\) are valid under all globally active model restrictions, \(U\) is the objective value of a verified feasible incumbent for minimization, and \(\nu_G\) identifies the model version. Writing \(F_G\) for the globally feasible set, an exact global diagram satisfies \(P(D_G)=F_G\), while a global relaxation satisfies \(F_G\subseteq P(D_G)\). Every open search node may derive local state by additionally restricting \(S_G\), but no node-specific assumption is part of \(S_G\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Global state contains versioned diagram information and an incumbent valid across every open search subtree.
assumptions_latex: All solver-wide presolve reductions and globally valid deductions are included in \(F_G\).
If finite, \(U=c(\bar x)\) for a verified point \(\bar x\in F_G\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For every open node \(B\), \(F_B\subseteq F_G\subseteq P(D_G)\) when \(D_G\) is relaxed.

notation.meaning: Feasible set under globally active restrictions.
Global incumbent upper bound for minimization.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: global solver state must be independent of node-local assumptions
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition is locally appropriate and distinguishes global from node-conditioned state, but the selected tuple and solver-wide derivation semantics are unsupported by an inspectable citation.

children.title: Local-to-Global State Promotion
children.top_down_role: Validity checks, ownership transfer, persistence boundaries, and contamination risks for promoted information.

knowledge_statements.title: Local-to-Global State Promotion
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validity condition for promoting a locally derived diagram fact to solver-wide state.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a fact \(q\) be derived from local state \(S_B\) under node assumptions \(A_B\), and let \(A_G\) denote the globally active assumptions. Promotion of \(q\) to global state is sound exactly when \(A_G\models q\); derivability only from \(A_G\land A_B\) is insufficient. For a domain deletion \(x_i\neq a\), this requires that no point in the global feasible set \(F_G\) has \(x_i=a\). For a bound \(\ell\), it requires \(\ell\leq\inf\{c(x):x\in F_G\}\). On promotion, increment the global version and invalidate local states whose cached semantics conflict with \(q\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Promote a local deduction only when it follows from global assumptions alone, then version the change and invalidate conflicting caches.
assumptions_latex: Local derivation is sound under \(A_G\land A_B\).
The promoted fact changes diagram semantics, domains, or bounds.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Promotion is sound if and only if \(A_G\models q\).

notation.meaning: Assumptions specific to search node B.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: globally stored deductions must be valid without branch-local assumptions
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The entailment condition expresses the intended local-to-global validity boundary, and content_kind condition is appropriate. A source is still required for the solver-integration claims concerning version increments and invalidation of conflicting local caches.

children.title: Incremental Diagram Recompilation
children.top_down_role: Partial rebuilding after domain changes, model edits, state refinement, or solver-node transitions.

knowledge_statements.title: Incremental Diagram Recompilation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Partial recompilation after a localized change to diagram domains or transition semantics.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a layered diagram \(G=(V,A)\), its compilation signature, and a change set \(C\), first identify the earliest affected layer \(k\). Preserve layers and arcs whose states and transition semantics do not depend on \(C\); invalidate every state at or after \(k\) reachable through an affected dependency. Recompute invalidated states in layer order, merge states only under the compiler's valid equivalence relation, and rebuild outgoing arcs. Stop when the rebuilt frontier is semantically identical to a cached frontier, or at the terminal layer. Output \(G'\) only after checking that its path set has the required exact or relaxed relation to the updated feasible set \(F'\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Rebuild only the dependency closure of changed diagram states, stopping at an equivalent cached frontier while preserving the required path semantics.
assumptions_latex: The compiler records dependencies from model data to diagram states and arcs.
State equivalence is sufficient to preserve all downstream transitions and objective contributions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P(G')=F'\) for exact compilation, or \(F'\subseteq P(G')\) for relaxed compilation.

notation.meaning: Set of changed domains, constraints, costs, or transitions.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: dependency-directed incremental compilation preserves unaffected states
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm belongs in this leaf, but no source establishes that the stated dependency closure and frontier-equivalence test are sufficient for the asserted exactness or relaxation guarantee. The final semantic check otherwise makes that guarantee partly procedural rather than derived.

children.title: Compiled-Diagram Reuse
children.top_down_role: Reuse across search nodes, repeated subproblems, solver rounds, or related model instances.

knowledge_statements.title: Compiled-Diagram Reuse
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Semantic preconditions under which a compiled diagram may be reused safely.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G\) be compiled under signature \(\sigma=(M,\pi,\tau,\mu)\), recording model semantics \(M\), variable order \(\pi\), transition rules \(\tau\), and state-merging policy \(\mu\). The compiled structure may be reused without recompilation for a solver state with the same signature. If only current domains are tightened, reuse by deleting inconsistent arcs and unreachable nodes is sound: for an exact diagram the surviving paths equal the old path set restricted to those domains, and for a relaxed diagram they still contain every currently feasible assignment. Cached objective values may be reused only when all arc costs and aggregation rules are unchanged.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A diagram is reusable when its semantic signature is unchanged; domain tightening may be handled by pruning inconsistent paths.
assumptions_latex: The cached diagram was sound for its recorded signature.
Pruning removes exactly arcs inconsistent with the tightened domains.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(\sigma'=\sigma\), structural reuse preserves the cached diagram's exactness or relaxation guarantee.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: compiled artifacts are reusable under an unchanged semantic signature
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: A source is needed to define the compilation signature and justify pruning-based reuse. It is also unclear whether current domains are part of model semantics M: if they are, domain tightening contradicts the same-signature premise; if they are not, that exclusion must be sourced and stated explicitly.

children.title: Reuse Invalidation Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Structural changes, stale domains, altered objectives, and context shifts that invalidate cached diagram artifacts.

knowledge_statements.title: Reuse Invalidation Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Changes beyond which cached diagram structure or annotations cannot be reused without validation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Reuse without recompilation is invalid whenever an unaccounted change can alter the meaning of a cached node, arc, path, or annotation. Such changes include modifications to constraint semantics, variable ordering, transition rules, state equivalence, objective arc costs, or presolve reconstruction. Formally, if two model versions have signatures \(\sigma\neq\sigma'\) and there exists an assignment \(x\) for which path acceptance or accumulated cost differs, then treating a diagram compiled under \(\sigma\) as compiled under \(\sigma'\) can lose feasible assignments, admit invalid assignments, or report an invalid bound. Reuse is permitted only after recompiling or certifying the changed components as semantically irrelevant.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Invalidate reuse when changed semantics can alter path acceptance, state equivalence, reconstruction, or accumulated cost.
assumptions_latex: The cached artifact was compiled under signature \(\sigma\).
The current model uses signature \(\sigma'\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If some \(x\) has different acceptance or cost under \(\sigma\) and \(\sigma'\), unchecked reuse is unsound.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: cache validity ends when semantic dependencies change
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary role is appropriate, but no source supports the proposed signature boundary. Moreover, a changed acceptance or cost for some assignment does not by itself make every reuse unsound if that assignment and affected annotation are irrelevant to the current feasible region or requested computation; a source-backed relevance condition is required.

children.title: Bound Synchronization
children.top_down_role: Transfer of diagram-derived bounds across solver components, search nodes, and relaxation rounds.

assumptions_latex: The objective is minimized.
Each imported \(\ell_B^{S}\) and \(\ell_B^{D}\) is valid for the same conditioned subproblem at \(B\).
Every globally feasible solution that could improve the incumbent belongs to at least one subproblem indexed by \(\mathcal O\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For every \(B\in\mathcal O\), \(\ell_B\leq z_B^*\); moreover, \(\widehat L\leq z^*\), and pruning \(B\) when \(\ell_B\geq U\) is sound.

notation.meaning: Optimal value of the subproblem at B.
Certified global lower bound, including the incumbent case.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Synchronization of valid diagram-derived lower bounds in a minimization search.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each open search node \(B\), let \(\ell_B^{S}\) be the solver's valid lower bound and \(\ell_B^{D}\) a valid bound produced by its diagram state for the same node and model versions. Atomically set \(\ell_B\leftarrow\max\{\ell_B^{S},\ell_B^{D}\}\). If \(\mathcal O\) is the set of open nodes and \(U\) is the value of a verified feasible incumbent, publish \(\widehat L=\min\bigl(\{U\}\cup\{\ell_B:B\in\mathcal O\}\bigr)\). A stale bound may be imported only if its validity survives every intervening model change. Prune \(B\) when \(\ell_B\geq U\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Combine version-compatible node lower bounds by maximum, include the feasible incumbent when forming the global lower bound, and prune nodes whose lower bound cannot improve the incumbent.
knowledge_statements.title: Bound Synchronization

children.title: Incumbent Synchronization
children.top_down_role: Propagation of incumbent values, feasible paths, objective cutoffs, and solution metadata into diagram state.

knowledge_statements.title: Incumbent Synchronization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Verification and solver-wide publication of diagram-generated incumbent solutions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: When a diagram produces a candidate assignment \(x\), reconstruct eliminated variables, verify \(x\in F_G\), and evaluate its objective \(c(x)\) in the current model version. For minimization with incumbent \((\bar x,U)\), atomically replace it by \((x,c(x))\) exactly when \(c(x)<U\), with a deterministic tie rule if required. Broadcast the new value to all active diagram and search states; receivers may use it only for objective cutoff or pruning. A candidate path from a relaxed diagram is not an incumbent until full-model feasibility has been verified.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Verify and reconstruct diagram candidates before atomically publishing an improving incumbent and broadcasting its cutoff value.
assumptions_latex: The objective is minimized.
Incumbent acceptance and objective evaluation use the current global model version.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: After acceptance, \(\bar x\in F_G\), \(U=c(\bar x)\), and \(U\) is nonincreasing.

notation.meaning: Candidate assignment returned by a diagram.

source_refs.locator: 2.7 Primal Bounds: Greedy and Local Search p. 34

source_witnesses.locator: 2.7 Primal Bounds: Greedy and Local Search p. 34

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The cited primal-bounds section plausibly supports feasible incumbents, but it does not inspectably support reconstruction, model-version validation, atomic publication, or broadcast behavior for diagram-generated candidates. Those claims require a solver-integration source.

children.title: Synchronization Consistency Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Stale cutoffs, delayed updates, conflicting validity scopes, and asynchronous state hazards.

knowledge_statements.title: Synchronization Consistency Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Safety invariants delimiting valid asynchronous bound and incumbent synchronization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For minimization, synchronization is consistent only while every node lower bound satisfies \(\ell_B\leq z_B^*\) and every finite incumbent satisfies \(U=c(\bar x)\) for some globally feasible \(\bar x\). Messages must identify the model version and, for local bounds, the search node and its conditioning version. A stale incumbent remains usable if its recorded solution is still feasible; a stale lower bound remains usable only if it is valid for the current subproblem. Pruning is permitted exactly from a simultaneously valid pair satisfying \(\ell_B\geq U\). Any semantic model change crossing these validity conditions requires revalidation before synchronization.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Synchronization is safe only for version-valid lower bounds and verified feasible incumbents; pruning requires both to be simultaneously valid.
assumptions_latex: The objective is minimized.
\(z_B^*\) is the true optimum at node \(B\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A synchronized prune of \(B\) is sound only if \(\ell_B\leq z_B^*\), \(U=c(\bar x)\), \(\bar x\in F_G\), and \(\ell_B\geq U\).

notation.meaning: Synchronized lower bound at node B.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The branch-and-bound citation supports ordinary bound-and-incumbent pruning but not asynchronous versioned synchronization. In addition, the stated conditions are a sufficient certificate for bound-based pruning, not logically necessary for every sound prune; a node may be soundly removed for infeasibility or dominance. The intended synchronization-specific boundary needs a more precise source-backed formulation.

children.title: Diagram Width
children.top_down_role: Maximum or layer-specific state counts as drivers of representation burden and approximation capacity.

knowledge_statements.title: Diagram Width
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Maximum number of decision-diagram states occurring in a single layer.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a finite layered decision diagram have node layers \(V_0,V_1,\ldots,V_L\), with arcs directed from one layer to the next. Its width is \[w(G)=\max_{0\leq i\leq L}|V_i|.\] If the root and terminal layers are excluded by convention, the internal width is \(w_{\mathrm{int}}(G)=\max_{1\leq i<L}|V_i|\). The chosen convention must be stated when comparing widths; for a nonempty standard diagram with singleton root and terminal, the two definitions agree whenever some internal layer has at least one node.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Diagram width is the maximum number of states in any layer, with endpoint inclusion stated explicitly.
assumptions_latex: \(G\) is finite and layered.
Every node belongs to exactly one layer \(V_i\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(w(G)=\max_{0\leq i\leq L}|V_i|\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: width of a layered decision diagram is its maximum layer cardinality
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition is mathematically standard, precise, and appropriate for the Diagram Width leaf, including its explicit endpoint convention. No source with a section, definition, theorem, or page locator is supplied, so it cannot pass evidence review.

children.title: Diagram Length
children.top_down_role: Layer depth as determined by variable order, decision granularity, and compilation structure.

knowledge_statements.title: Diagram Length
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Number of successive layer transitions along a complete layered-diagram path.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a layered decision diagram have ordered layers \(V_0,V_1,\ldots,V_L\), with the root in \(V_0\), terminals in \(V_L\), and every arc directed from \(V_i\) to \(V_{i+1}\). The diagram length is \(L\), the number of layer transitions on every root-to-terminal path. When exactly one decision variable is assigned at each transition, \(L\) also equals the number of variables represented. If long arcs or skipped variables are allowed, length remains the number of declared layer transitions and need not equal the number of arcs on a compressed path.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Diagram length is the number of ordered layer transitions from root to terminal, usually equal to the number of represented variables.
assumptions_latex: \(G\) has declared ordered layers \(V_0,\ldots,V_L\).
Under the standard convention, arcs connect consecutive layers.

children.title: Diagram Node Count
children.top_down_role: Total state-vertex volume across layers, including effects of reduction, merging, and refinement.

knowledge_statements.title: Diagram Node Count
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Size measure for a finite layered decision diagram.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D=(V,A)\) be a finite directed acyclic decision diagram whose node set is partitioned into layers \(V_0,\ldots,V_n\), where \(V_0=\{r\}\) is the root layer and \(V_n=\{t\}\) is the terminal layer. The diagram node count is \[N(D):=|V|=\sum_{i=0}^{n}|V_i|.\] If every intermediate layer satisfies \(|V_i|\le W\) for \(1\le i\le n-1\), then \[N(D)\le 2+(n-1)W.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Node count is the total number of nodes across all layers. With singleton root and terminal layers and at most W nodes in each of the n−1 intermediate layers, the diagram has at most 2+(n−1)W nodes.
assumptions_latex: \(D\) is finite and layered.
\(|V_i|\le W\) for \(1\le i\le n-1\).

children.title: Diagram Arc Count
children.top_down_role: Transition volume, branching density, storage burden, and traversal cost across compiled diagrams.

knowledge_statements.title: Diagram Arc Count
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Arc-based size measure for a finite layered decision diagram.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a finite layered decision diagram \(D=(V,A)\), the diagram arc count is \[M(D):=|A|=\sum_{i=0}^{n-1}|A_i|,\] where \(A_i\subseteq V_i\times V_{i+1}\) contains the arcs between consecutive layers. If every node has at most \(d\) outgoing arcs and each nonterminal layer contains at most \(W\) nodes, then \[M(D)\le d\sum_{i=0}^{n-1}|V_i|\le dnW.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Arc count totals transitions between consecutive layers; width W and maximum outdegree d imply at most dnW arcs over n transitions.
assumptions_latex: Arcs join consecutive layers.
Every nonterminal node has outdegree at most \(d\).
Every nonterminal layer has at most \(W\) nodes.

notation.meaning: arcs from layer i to layer i+1

children.title: Runtime Sensitivity to Width
children.top_down_role: Compilation, traversal, refinement, and solver-callback costs as diagram width changes.

knowledge_statements.title: Runtime Sensitivity to Width
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Worst-case dynamic-programming time for an explicitly represented layered diagram.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D=(V,A)\) have \(n\) layer transitions, maximum layer width \(W\), and maximum outdegree \(d\). A forward dynamic program that scans each reachable arc once and performs constant-time label extension and comparison computes an optimal root-to-terminal path in \[O(|V|+|A|)=O(ndW)\] time. Thus, with \(n\) and \(d\) fixed, the explicit-diagram optimization time grows at most linearly with the imposed width bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A forward shortest- or longest-path computation takes O(ndW) time when the diagram has n transitions, width W, and bounded outdegree d.
assumptions_latex: Arc-label extension and comparison take constant time.
Each reachable node and arc is processed once.
The maximum outdegree is \(d\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The complexity bound is plausible under the stated explicit-representation and constant-time-operation model, but it requires an inspectable source supporting that model and bound.

children.title: Memory Sensitivity to Width
children.top_down_role: Node, arc, state-label, cache, and auxiliary-storage growth associated with wider diagrams.

knowledge_statements.title: Memory Sensitivity to Width
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Working-memory and stored-diagram bounds under width restriction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a layered diagram with maximum width \(W\) and maximum outdegree \(d\), a forward dynamic program retaining only the current and next layers requires \(O(W+dW)=O(dW)\) working memory. If the complete diagram with \(n\) transitions is stored explicitly, its node labels and adjacency data require \[O(|V|+|A|)=O(ndW)\] memory. The streaming bound assumes that processed layers need not be retained or reconstructed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Layer-by-layer optimization uses O(dW) working memory, while explicitly storing all n layers and arcs uses O(ndW) memory.
assumptions_latex: Only two adjacent layers are retained in streaming mode.
Each node has at most \(d\) outgoing arcs.
A constant-size record represents each node label and arc.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(S_{\mathrm{stream}}=O(dW)\) and \(S_{\mathrm{stored}}=O(ndW)\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The working-memory and stored-diagram bounds depend on representation and streaming assumptions and have no supporting citation.

children.title: Width-Constrained Resource Regimes
children.top_down_role: Operating regimes determined by time budgets, memory ceilings, and differing resource bottlenecks.

knowledge_statements.title: Width-Constrained Resource Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sufficient width conditions under time and memory upper-bound models.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose an implementation satisfies \(T(W)\le c_TndW\) and streaming memory \(S(W)\le c_SdW\), where \(c_T,c_S,n,d>0\). Given budgets \(B_T,B_S>0\), a positive integer width \(W\) is guaranteed to satisfy both budgets whenever \[W\le \min\left\{\left\lfloor\frac{B_T}{c_Tnd}\right\rfloor,\left\lfloor\frac{B_S}{c_Sd}\right\rfloor\right\}.\] If the complete diagram instead satisfies the storage bound \(S_{\mathrm{stored}}(W)\le c_SndW\), replace the second denominator by \(c_Snd\). These upper bounds alone do not establish that larger widths violate the actual budgets.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A width is guaranteed to fit the time and streaming-memory budgets when both modeled upper bounds fit them. For explicit storage, the memory threshold has an additional factor n. Widths above these thresholds are not necessarily infeasible.
assumptions_latex: Runtime and memory obey the stated upper bounds.
\(W\in\mathbb N\) and \(W\ge 1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(W\le\min\{\lfloor B_T/(c_Tnd)\rfloor,\lfloor B_S/(c_Sd)\rfloor\}\implies T(W)\le B_T\text{ and }S(W)\le B_S\).

knowledge_statements.title: Width Versus Bound Quality
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Monotonicity for nested relaxed diagrams in minimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\) be the feasible solution set of a minimization problem with cost \(c\), and let relaxed diagrams \(D_W\) encode path sets \(P_W\supseteq F\). Define \(L_W:=\min\{c(p):p\in P_W\}\). If increasing width produces nested relaxations, so that \(P_{W_2}\subseteq P_{W_1}\) whenever \(W_2\ge W_1\), then \[L_{W_1}\le L_{W_2}\le \min_{x\in F}c(x).\] Thus greater width cannot weaken the lower bound, although strict improvement is not guaranteed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For nested minimization relaxations, increasing width removes relaxed paths, so lower bounds are nondecreasing but need not improve strictly.
assumptions_latex: \(F\subseteq P_W\) for every considered width.
The same cost function is used on all encoded paths.
\(P_{W_2}\subseteq P_{W_1}\) whenever \(W_2\ge W_1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(W_2\ge W_1\implies L_{W_1}\le L_{W_2}\le \operatorname{OPT}\).

notation.meaning: path set encoded by the width-W relaxation
lower bound obtained from that relaxation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The conditional monotonicity statement is mathematically sound and its property kind fits the topic, but no decision-diagram source supports the nestedness premise or terminology.

children.title: Relaxed Decision-Diagram Bound Monotonicity
children.top_down_role: Dominance families for nested width increases, state splits, and merge refinements, together with nonnested boundaries.

children.title: Nested-Width Diagram Families
children.top_down_role: Diagram sequences whose state spaces or represented path sets are nested across width levels.

knowledge_statements.title: Nested-Width Diagram Families
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nested relaxed-diagram family indexed by permitted width.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A family \((D_W)_{W\in I}\) of relaxed layered decision diagrams for feasible set \(F\) is nested by width if each diagram has maximum width at most \(W\), its encoded path set \(P_W\) contains \(F\), and \[W_1\le W_2\quad\Longrightarrow\quad P_{W_2}\subseteq P_{W_1}.\] Equality is permitted, so added width need not change the relaxation. Nestedness concerns represented solutions, not merely the numerical widths or node counts of the diagrams.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nested-width family consists of valid relaxations whose represented path sets can only shrink as the permitted width increases.
assumptions_latex: \(I\subseteq\mathbb N\) is ordered by the usual order.
Every feasible solution has a corresponding path in each \(D_W\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(W_1\le W_2\implies F\subseteq P_{W_2}\subseteq P_{W_1}\).

notation.meaning: relaxed diagram with width cap W
path set encoded by the diagram

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The proposed definition is precise and fits the leaf, but it introduces specialized nested-width terminology without an inspectable authoritative source.

children.title: Diagram-Dominance Relations
children.top_down_role: Comparisons of feasible-path coverage, relaxation strength, and bound quality between diagram variants.

knowledge_statements.title: Diagram-Dominance Relations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bound dominance between relaxed diagrams for the same minimization problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D_1,D_2\) be relaxed diagrams for the same minimization problem, with encoded path sets \(P_1,P_2\), common path cost \(c\), and lower bounds \(L_i:=\min_{p\in P_i}c(p)\). Diagram \(D_2\) bound-dominates \(D_1\), written \(D_2\succeq_B D_1\), when \[L_2\ge L_1.\] The stronger set relation \(P_2\subseteq P_1\) implies bound dominance whenever costs agree on common paths, but bound dominance alone does not imply path-set inclusion.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: One minimization relaxation bound-dominates another when its lower bound is at least as large; path-set inclusion is sufficient but not necessary.
assumptions_latex: Both diagrams relax the same feasible set.
Both diagrams use the same objective convention.
The minima defining \(L_1,L_2\) exist.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P_2\subseteq P_1\implies D_2\succeq_B D_1\), where \(D_2\succeq_B D_1\iff L_2\ge L_1\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition and inclusion implication are mathematically consistent for minimization, but the dominance terminology and orientation require a cited source.

children.title: Dominance Validity Across Widths
children.top_down_role: Structural conditions and construction choices governing whether increasing width preserves dominance.

knowledge_statements.title: Dominance Validity Across Widths
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sufficient conditions for cross-width bound dominance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For widths \(W_1\le W_2\), dominance \(D_{W_2}\succeq_B D_{W_1}\) is valid if both diagrams are relaxations of the same feasible set, corresponding paths receive identical costs, and \(P_{W_2}\subseteq P_{W_1}\). Under these conditions, \[\min_{p\in P_{W_1}}c(p)\le \min_{p\in P_{W_2}}c(p)\le \min_{x\in F}c(x).\] Width ordering alone is insufficient: the inclusion condition must follow from a nested construction or be independently verified.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A wider minimization diagram dominates only when validity, common costs, and nested path sets are preserved; numerical width alone proves nothing.
assumptions_latex: \(F\subseteq P_{W_2}\subseteq P_{W_1}\).
Corresponding paths have the same cost in both diagrams.
Both path minima exist.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(D_{W_2}\succeq_B D_{W_1}\) and \(L_{W_1}\le L_{W_2}\le\operatorname{OPT}\).

notation.meaning: width caps with W1 no greater than W2
encoded path set at width Wi

children.title: State-Split Dominance
children.top_down_role: Bound-strength and path-set comparisons produced by replacing aggregate states with finer states.

knowledge_statements.title: State-Split Dominance
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dominance induced by a validity-preserving state split.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D'\) be obtained from a relaxed minimization diagram \(D\) by replacing a node \(u\) with states \(u_1,\ldots,u_k\) that partition the histories reaching \(u\). Suppose each split state retains exactly the continuations valid for its assigned histories, all feasible paths remain represented, and arc costs are unchanged. Then the represented path sets satisfy \[F\subseteq P(D')\subseteq P(D),\] and consequently \[L(D')\ge L(D).\] Hence a validity-preserving state split produces a bound-dominating refinement.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Splitting a relaxed state by incoming history removes incompatible recombinations while preserving feasible paths, so the minimization lower bound cannot decrease.
assumptions_latex: The split partitions histories reaching the original state.
Every feasible path remains represented.
Costs of retained paths are unchanged.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P(D')\subseteq P(D)\) and \(L(D')\ge L(D)\).

notation.meaning: path set represented by diagram D

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The property is plausible under its strong history-partition and continuation assumptions, but state-split inclusion and dominance require an authoritative decision-diagram source.

children.title: Merge-Refinement Dominance
children.top_down_role: Dominance behavior produced by revising merge classes, aggregate labels, or relaxation granularity.

knowledge_statements.title: Merge-Refinement Dominance
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dominance from refining the partition used to merge states.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At a fixed layer, let \(\Pi_1\) and \(\Pi_2\) be partitions of exact states, and construct relaxed diagrams by merging every block into one relaxed state. If \(\Pi_2\) refines \(\Pi_1\), each \(\Pi_2\)-block lies within a \(\Pi_1\)-block, merging is validity-preserving, and path costs are consistent, then \[P(D_{\Pi_2})\subseteq P(D_{\Pi_1}).\] For minimization this gives \[L(D_{\Pi_2})\ge L(D_{\Pi_1}),\] so the finer merge partition bound-dominates the coarser one.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Refining a validity-preserving merge partition reduces spurious state combinations and cannot weaken the minimization lower bound.
assumptions_latex: \(\Pi_2\) refines \(\Pi_1\).
Both merged diagrams retain every feasible path.
Retained paths have consistent costs.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(D_{\Pi_2}\succeq_B D_{\Pi_1}\).

notation.meaning: relaxed diagram induced by partition Pi_i
minimum path cost in diagram D

A source defining the merge construction is required before the claim can be assessed reliably.

children.title: Refinement-Dominance Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Cases where refinement type, state comparability, or nonnested constructions prevent a dominance relation.

knowledge_statements.title: Refinement-Dominance Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of dominance without nestedness, validity, or objective consistency.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Refinement dominance is not implied by width alone. Consider a minimization problem with feasible path set \(F=\{p\}\) and costs \(c(p)=100\), \(c(q)=0\), and \(c(r)=-1\). Let two valid relaxed diagrams encode \(P_1=\{p,q\}\) and \(P_2=\{p,r\}\), with the second diagram wider than the first. Then \(L_1=0\) but \(L_2=-1\), so the wider diagram does not dominate. The failure occurs because \(P_2\nsubseteq P_1\); dominance can likewise fail if refinement removes feasible paths or changes corresponding path costs.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A wider valid relaxation can yield a worse bound when its path set is not nested; removing feasible paths or changing costs also invalidates refinement dominance.
assumptions_latex: The example uses minimization.
Both relaxed path sets contain the sole feasible path \(p\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{width}(D_2)>\operatorname{width}(D_1)\not\implies L_2\ge L_1\).

notation.meaning: relaxed path set of diagram i

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The numerical path-set example illustrates failure of nonnested bound monotonicity, but the claimed diagram widths and realizability of the stated path sets are not specified. An inspectable construction or authoritative boundary source is required.

knowledge_statements.title: Nonnested Approximation Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Shows why bound monotonicity requires nested relaxed path sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the feasible binary language be \(F=\{00\}\), and consider relaxed decision-diagram languages \(R_1=\{00,10\}\) and \(R_2=\{00,01\}\). Both contain \(F\), but neither contains the other. For the maximization objective \(f_c(x)=c_1x_1+c_2x_2\), their bounds are \(B_1=\max\{0,c_1\}\) and \(B_2=\max\{0,c_2\}\). Thus \(c=(1,0)\) gives \(B_1>B_2\), whereas \(c=(0,1)\) gives \(B_2>B_1\). Consequently, validity of two relaxations alone imposes no ordering on their bounds; monotonicity follows only from an inclusion or dominance relation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Two valid but nonnested relaxed diagrams can produce bounds in either order, depending on the objective coefficients.
assumptions_latex: \(F\subseteq R_1\cap R_2\)
The problem is a maximization problem.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Neither \(B_1\le B_2\) nor \(B_2\le B_1\) holds uniformly over objectives.

notation.meaning: path language represented by relaxed diagram i

children.title: Decision-Diagram Refinement Convergence
children.top_down_role: Exact-recovery and search-completeness families under continued width growth, state refinement, or cutset exploration.

knowledge_statements.title: Exact Recovery Under Width Expansion
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-state, ordered dynamic-programming decision diagrams.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider an ordered finite-domain dynamic program with \(n\) stages, and let \(S_i\) be its reachable exact states after stage \(i\). Its exact layered decision diagram has width \(W^*=\max_{0\le i\le n}|S_i|\). Suppose a width-limited relaxed compiler uses cap \(W\), preserves every exact transition and reward, and merges states only when a layer would exceed \(W\). If \(W\ge W^*\), no merge is required, so the compiled diagram is isomorphic to the exact state-transition diagram. Its root-to-terminal paths are exactly the feasible solutions and its optimum equals the original optimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Once the width cap reaches the maximum exact-state count, a merge-only relaxed compiler recovers the exact diagram and optimum.
assumptions_latex: Each \(S_i\) is finite.
The compiler introduces relaxation only through width-triggered state merging.
Transitions and arc rewards are preserved when no merge occurs.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(W\ge W^*\) implies exact recovery of the feasible language and optimal value.

notation.meaning: reachable exact states at layer i
maximum width of the exact state diagram

review_flags: Exact recovery depends on the stated merge-only compilation model; a supporting decision-diagram source is needed.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The theorem is coherent under the stated merge-only compiler model and its content kind fits the leaf, but no cited source supports that precise compilation model or exact-recovery conclusion.

knowledge_statements.title: Exact Recovery Under State Refinement
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Recovery by refining aggregates of exact dynamic-programming states.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let each relaxed state at layer \(i\) represent a block of a partition \(\Pi_i\) of the reachable exact states \(S_i\). Refine blocks without deleting feasible exact transitions. If every final block consists only of states having identical feasible labeled continuations and identical continuation rewards, then quotienting by these blocks preserves every feasible root-to-terminal value. In particular, refinement to singleton partitions \(\Pi_i=\{\{s\}:s\in S_i\}\) produces the exact state-transition diagram. Hence the refined diagram has precisely the original feasible solutions and optimal value.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Refining aggregated states until continuation behavior is exact—and, in particular, until states are singletons—recovers the exact diagram.
assumptions_latex: Every relaxed state is a block of reachable exact states.
Refinement preserves all exact transitions.
Equivalent states have identical labeled continuations and continuation rewards.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Continuation-equivalent refinement preserves exact values; singleton refinement guarantees exact recovery.

notation.meaning: reachable exact states at layer i
partition represented by refined states at layer i

review_flags: A source is needed for the precise state-equivalence and refinement model.

knowledge_statements.title: Cutset-Search Completeness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Completeness of finite branching over unresolved decision-diagram cutset states.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a finite-domain problem have finitely many complete assignments. At every search node, let a decision-diagram cutset partition all represented root-to-terminal paths into finitely many subproblems. Suppose the search branches on every unresolved cutset subproblem, never discards a subproblem unless infeasibility or bound dominance is validly certified, and eventually fixes or separates at least one previously unresolved assignment distinction on every nonterminal branch. Then exhaustive cutset search terminates after finitely many branches. Every feasible assignment occurs in some terminal subproblem, so selecting the best terminal feasible value returns a globally optimal solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite, exhaustive cutset search is complete when branching makes progress and pruning uses only valid certificates.
assumptions_latex: The complete assignment set is finite.
Cutset subproblems cover every represented path.
Each nonterminal branch makes strict assignment-level progress.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The search terminates and returns a globally optimal feasible assignment whenever one exists.

notation.meaning: a finite cutset whose nodes induce search subproblems

review_flags: The supplied sources do not support this decision-diagram cutset completeness theorem.

children.title: Stagnating Refinement
children.top_down_role: Refinement sequences that alter diagram structure without materially changing the represented relaxation.

knowledge_statements.title: Stagnating Refinement
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Strict structural refinement need not improve the optimization bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a maximization problem, let successive relaxed diagram languages satisfy \(F\subseteq R_{k+1}\subsetneq R_k\), and define \(B_j=\max_{x\in R_j}f(x)\). Although the refinement is strict, the bound stagnates whenever \(R_{k+1}\) retains an optimizer of \(R_k\). Indeed, if some \(x^*\in R_{k+1}\) satisfies \(f(x^*)=B_k\), then inclusion gives \(B_{k+1}\le B_k\), while feasibility of \(x^*\) gives \(B_{k+1}\ge B_k\). Therefore \(B_{k+1}=B_k\), even though paths were removed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A strict refinement leaves the bound unchanged whenever at least one former relaxed optimizer survives.
assumptions_latex: \(F\subseteq R_{k+1}\subsetneq R_k\)
Each displayed maximum is attained.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{argmax}_{x\in R_k}f(x)\cap R_{k+1}\ne\varnothing\) implies \(B_{k+1}=B_k\).

notation.meaning: relaxed path language after refinement k

review_flags: The elementary set-optimization claim is clear, but no relevant decision-diagram source was supplied.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary statement is mathematically correct and appropriately scoped, but the record contains no inspectable citation connecting this elementary optimizer-retention condition to relaxed decision-diagram refinement.

children.title: Bound-Quality Plateaus
children.top_down_role: Extended refinement ranges with unchanged or negligible bound improvement.

knowledge_statements.title: Bound-Quality Plateaus
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characterizes constant-bound intervals in nested relaxed diagrams.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\subseteq R_{b}\subseteq\cdots\subseteq R_a\) be finite relaxed path languages for a maximization problem, and let \(B_k=\max_{x\in R_k}f(x)\). The sequence is a bound-quality plateau on indices \(a,\ldots,b\) exactly when \(B_a=\cdots=B_b\). Because the languages are nested, this equality holds if and only if the smallest language \(R_b\) contains an optimizer of the largest language \(R_a\). Thus arbitrarily many strict language refinements may form one plateau while the relaxation remains inexact.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Across nested finite relaxations, bounds stay constant exactly when the smallest relaxation retains a maximizer of the largest.
assumptions_latex: All \(R_k\) are finite and nonempty.
\(R_b\subseteq\cdots\subseteq R_a\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(B_a=\cdots=B_b\iff R_b\cap\operatorname{argmax}_{x\in R_a}f(x)\ne\varnothing\).
review_flags: No supplied locator addresses decision-diagram bound plateaus.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The finite nested-set characterization is correct and the property kind fits the container, but source_refs is empty and no decision-diagram plateau locator supports the formulation.

children.title: Plateau-Inducing Regimes
children.top_down_role: State aggregation, width placement, ordering, or objective structures associated with persistent plateaus.

knowledge_statements.title: Plateau-Inducing Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sufficient regimes for unchanged relaxed-diagram bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(R'\subsetneq R\) be finite relaxed path languages and let \(B(R)=\max_{x\in R}f(x)\). A plateau is induced by any refinement satisfying \(R'\cap M(R)\ne\varnothing\), where \(M(R)=\operatorname{argmax}_{x\in R}f(x)\). Important sufficient regimes are: the refinement changes only paths outside \(M(R)\); multiple tied maximizers exist and at least one survives; or all removed paths have objective value strictly below \(B(R)\). Under each regime, \(B(R')=B(R)\). Bound improvement requires removal or objective degradation of every current relaxed maximizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Plateaus occur when refinement leaves at least one current relaxed maximizer; improvement requires eliminating or degrading all of them.
assumptions_latex: \(R'\subsetneq R\) are finite and nonempty.
The objective \(f\) is unchanged by refinement.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(R'\cap M(R)\ne\varnothing\) is sufficient for \(B(R')=B(R)\).
review_flags: A decision-diagram reference is needed for the intended refinement regimes.
